items.quote: Yes. So I think Sweta, our analysis is that this is accretive to our ROA and ROE outlook for the next two, three years because of following levers.

items.statement: Cost of funds already coming down quarter-on-quarter; fund inflow will help reduce cost further
items.quote: On the cost of funds, we believe that we are already in the phase where the cost of funds have been coming down quart er-on-quarter. And in fact, Vivek, in the last call also, we did mention about it. So that's a continuous process. When the fund actually comes in, this will definitely help us reduce the cost further

items.statement: Growth dependent on market conditions; funds will give impetus to invest more in vehicle finance and small business loans

items.statement: No plan to use proceeds for acquisitions of other companies or entities
items.quote: There's no such plan.

items.statement: Net inflow expected to be INR1,400 crores plus after tax liability
items.quote: Yes. I mean if you exclude, but really the net inflow is really the correct way to look at it, which is really INR1,400 crores plus is what is expected.

items.statement: Gain on transaction estimated at INR1,300 crores plus
items.quote: Gain would be at INR1,300 plus.

items.statement: Transaction subject to customary conditions including RBI approval, lender and shareholder consent
items.quote: The transaction is subject to customary conditions resident, RBI approval, consent from lenders and shareholders.

items.statement: Combined entity EBITDA margin expected in 20%-odd range and revenue INR 4,000 crores plus by FY27-28

items.statement: Merger accretive to revenue growth and margin in first year; 150-200 bps EBITDA margin improvement over standalone guidance
items.quote: What we expect is that after the merger and we really make everything execute it well, it could definitely be 150 to 200 basis points higher than what we have guided at any point of time.

items.statement: Viyash capacity utilization ~70%; no major capex needed for next two years
items.quote: Viyash's current capacity utilization is close to 70%. And we don't see any additional capex requirement for the near future.

items.statement: Viyash EBITDA margin improved from 12-13% to 17-21%; confident of further growth driven by API mix shift and utilization
items.quote: That's how yo u can see ‘25 or ‘24, from 12 %, 13% to it ’s reached to 21%, 17%. And we are pretty confident it's going to grow

items.statement: SeQuent standalone guided high-teens EBITDA by FY27-28; combined entity targets 20%+ EBITDA
items.quote: We should be expecting that by 27-28, we would be in the 20%-odd range for EBITDA margins

items.statement: Key risk is execution of integration plans and regulatory approval timelines for synergies
items.quote: The risks as I see, could be largely around being able to execute well. Yes, I think that's really the principle thing that we all need to make sure that it's all the plans that we have get executed well.

items.statement: Synergy realization timing uncertain due to regulatory filing requirements for intermediate supply
items.quote: But short term, we need to work out because SeQuent as well as Viyash is working totally under regulatory environment. You may know sometimes regulatory takes a little longer time.

items.statement: Combined entity expected to become debt-free soon; finance costs to reduce substantially
items.quote: And we are going to be a debt-free company soon unless we go and invest today. Looking at our EBITDA, it can be debt-free very soon. So, our financial cost is going to reduce substantially.

items.statement: Viyash has 60+ commercial API products, 30-40 intermediates/pre-stores, ~30 NDAs; 5-10 products are global market leaders
items.quote: You can see almost 60-plus products are commercial products, and at least I can say 5 to 10 products we are the market leader.

items.statement: Viyash shifting from low-margin intermediates to high-margin API and complex products; API business doubled in two years
items.quote: Last two years, API business has grown almost double, whereas intermediate business we optimized. Intermediate business is going to be more focused on utilizing for API requirements.

items.statement: Biosecurity Act could be major opportunity for combined entity in US animal health over 5-10 years if passed
items.quote: I see t hat's one of the good opportunities for SeQuent . There's large companies that are looking, the alternative majority is coming from China. That's where they're looking the alternative

items.statement: Merger swap ratio: 56 SeQuent shares for every 100 Viyash shares; at 44% discount to SeQuent trading multiples

items.statement: Merger expected to conclude in 12-15 months subject to regulatory approvals
items.quote: The merger is anticipated to conclude over next 12 to 15 months, subject to the various regulatory and other approvals required.

items.statement: Viyash amortization ~INR 90-95 cr/year for FY25-FY26; partial in FY27 then clears
items.quote: FY25 and FY26 will continue at around that 90-95 crores is the amortization per annum. FY27 will have part of the period.

items.statement: Combined entity annualized EBITDA run rate already INR 400 cr+ in first quarter
items.quote: Given that in the very first quarter, both the companies together are already at an annualized INR400 crores plus run rate on EBITDA.

items.statement: Management structure to continue with continuity; structural adjustments later as needed
items.quote: I think clearly the theme of going ahead is continuity. I think all the management is going to continue fully committed into this role.

items.quote: In Hyderabad, specifically, the capacity that is being built up is about 4 million per annum. And we will work on increasing this once the entire system picks up speed.

items.quote: We still remain an ODM and EMS company. We don't have a Kaynes branded product. And we continue with that strategy as of now.

items.quote: No royalty is to be paid to anybody, any entity outside of India. Since we acquired this part of the acquisition deal, that Iskraemeco brand name can be used for a specified period to service all these orders in India for as long as we wish.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of around 25% for FY25
items.quote: And in terms of revenue growth, guidance would be around 25%.

items.quote: It will be between 3.5% to 4% before exceptional loss.

items.quote: We have increased our guidance from 8% and we have changed it from to 9% to 10% will be the guidance for this entire financial year and as of SSG.

items.quote: So we intend to double our store count on next three years.

items.quote: so sales per square feet is around 7,500 square feet with a store EBITDA pre-IND AS at 13%

items.quote: Operating cost generally lies between including rental, it lies between 20% to 23%.

items.quote: So in terms of store expansion 35 to the 40 stores are that we are targeting for this financial year FY '25.

items.quote: the first half generally tends to have 43% to 48% of the revenue, depending on the seasonality.

items.quote: for FY24 it stands at around 86% of the sales came from the full price sale through for FY24 and I think we intend to maintain the s ame rate for this year little bit o n the better side you can say

items.quote: we have taken 10.76 as the exceptional loss being keeping prudence in mind.

items.quote: INR146 crores was intended to repay our debts and balance was to improve the working capital or for

items.quote: So, it is a PAT of post-Ind AS 4% to 5%.

items.quote: The first phase of new capacity addition of 15,000 MVA will start for commercial production from January 2025.

items.quote: The increase into this is because of the QIP funds, what we have received is placed into the liquidity fund till we utilize it. So we have received the revenue on account of that.

items.quote: this is all going to be capex linked. So to that extent, I think you will see it play out over the next two years

There are larger deals and then there are smaller, but this is an average framework. All deals initially are roughly around 60% license fee and some 40%, which is called implementation charging, which is to configure the system for the user. Bey

items.statement: Revenue distribution historically 42-44% in H1, remainder in H2; slightly back-ended due to perpetual license model
items.quote: I think this business is slightly back-ended towards Q3 and Q4 where larger license deals end up happening. It's a history of every software license product company which has perpetual license. So roughly around -- our distribution today is roughly between somewhere 42% to 44% in H1 and between the corresponding remaining in the H2 part of that.

items.statement: US deal closure cycles elongated; recovery dependent on faster diligence cycles and macro improvement
items.quote: What we have found challenges in our ability to close in terms of the conclusion of those deals happening, that's taken really a large time. So, I'm sure if the market and the economy overall recovers, if some amount of diligence cycles become fast, then we should be able to see better results.

items.statement: LumYn GenAI product targeting cross-sell/upsell in financial services via generative UI; horizontal but go-to-market focused on retail and collection journeys
items.quote: Predominantly, what LumYn is a product, which let's use the traditional machine learnings, but exposes it through a generative UI interface. So that you could almost do, what we call brainstorming or you could do a very interactive discussions with the end business systems you have. So, where we position it? We are right now positioning it wherever the customers find opportunities to either segmen

items.statement: Insurance and healthcare verticals may struggle to reach banking scale unless jackpot hit; banking to remain predominant
items.quote: But I hope that insurance and including insurance health and government should be sizable and material businesses for us. And we do expect in the next 3 to 4 years, they come very close to banking, maybe they become -- both together become equal the size of banking.

items.statement: Equity yield 58 bps, debt 28 bps, liquid 12-13 bps for Q2
items.value: 58 bps equity, 28 bps debt, 12-13 bps liquid
items.quote: For the Q2, equity is 58 basis points, debt was 28 basis points and liquid is between 12 and 13 basis points.

items.statement: Commission rationalization effective 1 Aug 2024 partially offset TER erosion; some benefit seen in Q2
items.quote: One is, of course, as you rightly mentioned, mix of, the asset mix and some bit of rationalization on the brokerage. So, some partial benefit has come in this quarter. It was effective on 1st of August.

items.statement: Equity margins will keep sliding with rising AUM; rationalization only softens pace of decline
items.quote: Let me clarify, Abhijeet, will equity margins keeps sliding? Of course, yes, with rising AUM. What we have tried to do is only soften the pace at which they were falling by doing this exercise.

items.statement: Industry equity net flows H1 FY25 INR2.45T vs full FY24 INR2.37T; SIP September INR245B highest ever
items.quote: As against INR2.37 trillion for FY 23-24 in actively managed equity-oriented funds, industry has recorded flows of INR2.45 trillion in the first half of current fiscal. INR245 billion is SIP's contribution in month of September 2024, again highest ever.

items.statement: HDFC AMC flow market share healthier than book share; ex-NFO flow share higher than AUM share
items.quote: Ex of NFOs would be decent. if I remember correctly it's higher than the book share, yes.

items.statement: Equity-oriented AUM 65.7% of quarterly average vs industry 57.1%; actively managed equity AUM INR4.9T at 12.7% share
items.quote: We closed the quarter with an AUM of INR7.7 trillion, market share of 11.5% with equity -oriented funds now comprising 65.7% on a quarterly average basis co mpared to the industry's average of 57.1

items.statement: Alternative AUM grew from INR2,400 cr to INR4,800 cr in 6 months; VC/PE FoF closed Sep 30 with INR1,200 cr commitments
items.quote: we successfully closed our VC/PE fund of fund, the Category II fund of fund on S eptember 30, where we got commitments of around INR1,200-odd crores

items.statement: Deferred tax liability increased INR69.75 cr due to new capital gains tax rate without indexation on MTM gains till June 30
items.quote: Accordingly, the deferred tax liability recognized by the company on fair value gains on its investment as on June 30, 2024, has increased by INR69.75 crores, thereby resulting in an additional charge on the PAT of the company for quarter ended September 30, 2024.

items.statement: One-time tax hit settled in Q2; steady-state tax rate applies from Q3 onward
items.quote: That's right. Now it will be the normal tax rate going forward.

items.statement: Opened 24 new branches early this year to expand distribution reach
items.quote: We opened 24 new branches this year, early this year. And we serve like all distribution partners across the country.

items.statement: GIFT City subsidiary HDFC AMC International IFSC launching 4 feeder products for NRI/diaspora flows
items.quote: we have set up a who lly owned subsidiary in GIFT City, our HDFC AMC International IFSC and there one of our products is going live very soon. And then we'll have another three products, all these four will feed into domestic mutual

items.statement: Private credit team taking shape; product launch expected over next couple of quarters
items.quote: Additionally, our private credit team is taking shape, and we anticip ate launching a product in this area over the next couple of quarters

items.statement: PMS business developing steadily; total product count near 100; few NFO opportunities next couple quarters but focus on market share in existing categories
items.quote: over the next couple of quarters, ther e could be a few opportunities, but honestly not many. We would like to really build market share in each and every category where we are present

items.statement: Admin/other opex up INR19 cr YoY: INR6.2 cr CSR, INR2.5 cr KYC (unique investors up 50% YoY to 11.8M); rest normal
items.quote: Of the INR19 crores, incrementally INR6.2 crores is due to CSR, that's mandator y expense. Additional INR2.5 crores have been spent on KYC expenses. So , our unique customers have increased by about 50% over a year-on-year basis to 11.8 million

items.statement: Management expects to maintain EBITDA margin guidance of 43-44% for the full year despite regulatory headwinds.
items.quote: On your second question, whether guidance on EBITDA, would we be able to maintain that? Yes, definitely, we would be able to maintain that. We can see improvement in that because now we are able to sell multiple products to the same customer.

items.statement: Regulatory changes in derivatives estimated to impact 13-14% of net broking income per client in the near term.
items.quote: But our estimation is that impact would be roughly in the region of around 13% to 14% of net income that we get from the customer.

items.statement: New business burn rate guided at 2-2.5% of total revenue; breakeven expected in 1.5-2 years for distribution, 2.5-3 years for wealth.
items.quote: As previous earnings call, we guided everyone that this burn rate would be around 2% to 2.5% of our total revenue. So that way, we maintain that because we want to grow all that vertical. So we believe that kind of breakeven for new businesses would be in next 1.5, 2 years and maybe wealth may take around 2.5 to 3 years.

items.statement: Wealth management RM team build-out to be completed next quarter; asset management license in final stages.
items.quote: The RM team is under the ramp-up stage right now, I think the full-fledged team should be built out over the next month or so. So you will see the full built-out of the RM team in the next quarter.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 consolidated EBDAT margin at 49.9%, up 191 bps QoQ normalized; wealth and asset management incubation costs 1.8% of OPM.
items.quote: Our quarter 2 reported consolidated EBDAT margin stood at 49.9%, while this was higher by 1,220 basis points quarter-on-quarter as compared to our reported quarter 1 margin, it was still better by 191 basis points quarter-on-quarter when compared to the normalized quarter 1 margin at 48%.

items.statement: MTF interest rate reduced to 14.99% from 18% effective November 2024 to grow market share; cash delivery brokerage introduced.
items.quote: Effective November 2024, the interest charge on margin trading facility across all clients is being reduced to 14.99% from 18% earlier.

items.statement: True-to-label impact offset by charging for cash delivery orders and interest on non-cash collateral above ₹50,000.
items.quote: We have increased our kind of like -- or maybe we have started charging for cash delivery transactions. We have put -- like we are charging interest on collateral that we receive for -- so that way, by putting all these additional kind of charges on cash segment and charging for collateral that we receive as a margin, we would be able to negate this impact of true-to-label.

items.statement: Client acquisition run rate 50-60% for digital players; 3 million new clients added in Q2 (90% from Tier 2/3+ cities).
items.quote: Operationally, Angel One delivered strong results in quarter 2 FY'25, acquiring approximately 3 million new clients with about 90% coming from Tier 2, Tier 3 and beyond cities.

items.statement: Credit distribution live with ₹3.6B cumulative disbursement; fixed deposits launched with 6 partners; mutual fund SIP registrations >2.3M in Q2.
items.quote: As of the 30th of September 2024, cumulative disbursement through our platform totalled ₹ 3.6 billion.

items.statement: Wealth management launched third-party distribution of mutual funds, PMS, AIFs; content publishing initiated across macro views and asset classes.
items.quote: We have already started to publish content, which is across three different categories of content, which you will see in the Investor Relations presentation as well across macro views on asset classes, across views on overall macro economy and specific news on events which happened.

items.statement: Client funding book averaged ₹39B in Q2, up 48% QoQ; period-end book at ₹43B.
items.quote: With rising volumes in our cash delivery segment, we witnessed corresponding growth in our client funding book as well, which averaged at nearly ₹ 39 billion for the quarter, sequentially up by 48.1%.

items.statement: SEBI derivative regulations (lot size increase, weekly expiry rationalization, 2% ELM hike) may cause short-term volume softness.
items.quote: While these adjustments may potentially result in short-term softness in trading volumes, they are expected to fortify the market in the long run.

items.statement: Credit risk on distributed loans remains with partner NBFCs/banks; Angel One has no NPA exposure.
items.quote: In terms of the default, right, I mean, since we are purely in the distribution business, right, the default completely lies in the books of the NBFC and/or the bank that we have tied up with. So there is no implication of the default on our business whatsoever.

items.statement: Assisted partner network at 9,000-10,000 APs, contributing 22-23% of revenue; plans to distribute loans/insurance via AP channel.
items.quote: So in terms of number of APs, we are in the region of around 9,000 to 10,000. And this business is also growing as equal to our digital business. So share of AP business is around 22% to 23% of our revenue.

items.statement: AMC license in final stages; approval expected any day.
items.quote: So again, in terms of the license, I can say we are in the final stages of getting the AMC license. And it could be any day, any time now that we hear it from the regulator.

items.statement: Revenue expected to be INR 2,150-2,200 crores by end of FY27 with EBITDA margin of 14-14.5%
items.quote: By end of FY27, we are expecting revenue to be in the range of INR 2,150 crores to INR 2,200 crores. And our EBITDA margin will be in the range of 14% to 14.5%.

items.statement: Next financial year growth target of 18-20%
items.quote: Next financial year, we intend to have a growth of 18%-20%.

items.statement: Ordered 1,500 kg/hour wafer line for installation in Q1 next year
items.quote: For wafers we have already ordered 1,500 kg per hour machines line which is expected to get installed sometime in Q1 of next year.

items.statement: Alternate channel run rate INR 26 lakh/month, targeting INR 3+ crores/month by end of FY25
items.quote: We expect all this business to be INR 3 crores plus per month by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 11.6%, down from 12.7% YoY due to A&P spend increase from INR 2 to 5.5 crores and employee increments
items.quote: EBITDA margin remained at 11.6%, down from 12.7% last year. While there has been an inflationary pressure because of increase in raw material prices for Chana and palm oil and a couple of other raw materials, but we have negated that by a couple of our initiatives, which includes grammage reduction as well as some cost optimization measures.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin expected around 12% if raw material prices stay at current levels
items.quote: So, my estimate is that it will be bit higher than Q2 maybe in the range of 12% provided the raw material prices etc remains in the current range.

items.statement: FY25 A&P spend estimated at 1.5% of revenue (INR 18-20 crores), FY26 at 2% (INR 25 crores)
items.quote: Overall, our estimate for FY25 is close to 1.5% of our revenue, which will be INR 18 crores to INR 20 crores this year. And going forward, in FY26 also, we will have a higher, close to INR 25 crores of revenue, 2% of revenue being spent on advertising and marketing.

items.statement: Implemented grammage reduction in INR 5/10 packs and MRP revision in larger packs in September to offset 20% palm oil import duty hike (5% to 25%)
items.quote: In the month of September, the government has raised the import duty of palm oil by 20%. As you all know, 5% import duty has increased to 25%. To address this inflationary pressure and safeguarding our margin, we have implemented corrective measures in the month of September, which include reducing grammage in our INR 5 price point and INR 10 price point.

items.statement: Focus market revenue grew 29% YoY in Q2 and 32% in H1; added ~150 dealers in focus markets
items.quote: Our focus market continued its growth momentum with revenue growth of 29% Y-o-Y in Q2 and 32% in H1 FY25. This was largely a result of our ongoing efforts to expand our distribution network within these regions. During the year, we have added approx 150 dealers in the focus market.

items.statement: Wafers grew 47% YoY in Q2 (49% in H1); Gathiya grew 13% YoY in Q2 (12% in H1)
items.quote: The Gathiya segment grew by 13% Y-o-Y, while Wafers witnessed a substantial increase of 47% in Q2 FY25. Speaking of H1, Gathiya has shown growth of 12% and Wafers 49%.

items.statement: Raw material prices (chana, potato) expected to ease in Q4 with new crop; palm oil prices depend on import duty revision
items.quote: So Q4 is the quarter where again the crop of chana will come and looking at a favourable monsoon which we see last month. I think Q4 is a time where we will see the ease in the raw material prices specifically in chana and potato, palm oil is something which is because of increase in the import duty which the Government has imposed sometime in September.

items.statement: Board approved first interim dividend of INR 1 per share (100% of face value) for FY24-25
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that the Board has approved the first interim dividend of INR 1 per share that is 100% on the face value of INR 1 for FY24-FY25.

items.statement: Capex spend envisaged around Rs.100 crore for the year and construction of integrated R&D center to commence soon in phased manner
items.quote: We envisage spends on CAPEX would be around Rs.100 crore. We also expect to commence the construction for integrated R&D Center in a phased manner soon.

items.statement: First half export revenue was Rs.275 crore; Q2 export revenue was Rs.143 crore
items.quote: The first half revenue for international business is Rs. 275 crore.

items.statement: Domestic crop care formulation business saw minus 6% price degrowth with 18% volume growth in H1 FY25
items.quote: The domestic crop care first half you wanted, right? So, domestic crop care has had a minus 6% price degrowth, I am talking about formulation business and the volume growth is positive at 18%.

items.statement: Export demand recovery remains slow with lower prices and inventory buildup; China keeps market well supplied; US demand relatively better; Europe uncertain
items.quote: Export market demand recovery is still not very promising. Lower prices and volatility are making chemical players also see an inventory buildup. China continues to keep the market well supplied. Demand in the US has been relatively better . Demand remains uncertain in Europe due to operating challenges with unrest in the Middle East further adding more pressure.

items.statement: Herbicide and crop nutrition grew 25% and 29% respectively in domestic crop care; herbicide portfolio under-indexed and being improved progressively
items.quote: The quality of growth was also good, with future growth categories like herbicide and crop nutrition, witnessing 25% and 29% growth, respectively. Herbicide categories is under indexed within our business and we are consciously working on improving the share progressively.

items.statement: Acephate remains a trouble child due to concentrated markets (Brazil, US, India) and competitors Adama and UPL being backward integrated with B2C presence; evaluating cost reengineering and relationship options
items.quote: Acephate will continue to be a trouble, I think it's a trouble child I would say, we have to work on it.

items.statement: Management targets growing better than the market but declines to give a specific number for FY25 growth
items.quote: Well, I think all I have been saying is that our attempt is going to be we grow better than the market. That's our attempt and that's what we are targeting. I am certainly not in a position to give a number.

items.statement: Capex of Rs.650 crore spent out of Rs.800 crore planned over last five years; Rs.200 crore on multi-purpose plant, Rs.100 crore on formulation plant, rest on debottlenecking, sustenance and digital
items.quote: We have done about Rs.650 crore of CAPEX out of the Rs.800 crore of CAPEX that we spoke about in the last five years. And if I slice it, the big one had gone behind multi-purpose plant, which is around Rs.200 crore.

items.statement: Domestic Rabi outlook positive on increased reservoir levels; Kharif liquidation slightly delayed due to extended rains
items.quote: Overall, Rabi outlook is also positive, with increased reservoir levels.

items.statement: Seeds business focuses on five key crops: Cotton, Maize, Millet, Mustard and Rice; cotton hybrid Diggaz crossed Rs.50 crore brand with negligible returns
items.quote: Our focus will primarily be on five key crops – Cotton, Maize, Millet, Mustard and Rice. We believe the focus on such selective crops will aid in driving scale.

items.statement: Seeds business growth driven by price/mix (high single digit) with volume flattish; cotton now largest crop in portfolio contributing to margin improvement
items.quote: Last part of it as I said has come from volume and mix. So, a high single digit would come from price and mix and volume would be largely flattish.

items.statement: China continues to supply at competitive prices making pricing improvement difficult to predict; focus shifting to domestic branded business for premium pricing
items.quote: Pricing is something very, very difficult to predict because no matter how much we continue to undermine China. China has capacity and they have ability to supply at a very competitive price.

items.statement: CSM business: completed pilot scale production of Flavocide for Bio-Gene; three new contracts in FY24; confident new partners will meaningfully contribute to top and bottom line in coming years
items.quote: On the back of three new contracts in Fiscal Year ‘2 4, we have further successfully completed pilot scale production of pre-commercial quantities of Flavocide®, a novel insecticide for Bio- Gene Technology Limited, an Australian company. We are confident that these new partners will meaningfully contribute to both the top line and bottom line in the years to come.

items.statement: Seeds inventory at one of the lowest levels across years; calibrated placements using Seedsay digital tool reduced returns significantly
items.quote: In fact, one thing that probably will help all of you guys our seeds inventory is one of the lowest across various years now . So, the inventory levels have significantly come down.

items.statement: Portfolio rationalization exercise underway for domestic formulation; expected to complete in couple of months; goal is return on capital optimization
items.quote: We are in the midst of exercise and that exercise should get completed in couple of months. So, as we enter the new year, we would be able to actually go with completely what you call streamlined portfolio approach where we may be looking at sale and say, look, whether this sale is desirable or not.

items.statement: Metribuzin achieved highest ever volume in H1 FY25, surpassing full FY24 volume; Hexaconazole showing good momentum with debottlenecking underway
items.quote: In Metribuzin, we have done the highest ever volume in first half '25 and with half year volume surpas sing Fiscal Year ‘24 volume already. Hexac onazole is also showing good momentum, and we are working on debottlenecking to serve the increasing demand.

items.statement: Debt reduction target of Rs. 100 crores over FY25 and FY26
items.quote: our intent is that in two financial years, which is FY '25 and FY '26, we will reduce the debt by about Rs. 100 crores.

items.statement: New initiatives spend target of Rs. 60 crores for full FY25
items.quote: I think we had given at the beginning of the year at about Rs. 60 crores is the annual target.

items.statement: Inventory charge-off of Rs. 50-60 crores expected in H2 FY25
items.quote: I would assume in the region of between Rs. 50 crores and Rs. 60 crores is what would be charged off as an additional inventory in H2.

items.statement: Broadcast advertising demand remains soft with no festive surge seen yet
items.quote: Baseline advertising still continues and hence there is some kind of growth in the digital part of the business. But the surge which normally affects the broadcast business which starts happening is something that we are yet to see.

items.statement: Digital media revenue grew 17% YoY in Q2 FY25 to Rs. 67 crores
items.quote: Digital media revenues for the 2nd Quarter to rate around Rs. 67 crores, which increased by approximately 17% Y -o-Y

items.statement: GST show cause notice received for Rs. 70.25 crores plus interest and penalty
items.quote: we had received the show cause and we have intimated on the exchanges also, with the demand of Rs. 70.25 crores along with the interest and penalty thereon

items.statement: New channel launch deferred due to weak advertising demand environment
items.quote: since the conditions are not ripe yet, the demand scenario on advertising, etc., ad spends is on the lower side. We have held back since we don't see that bettering of that

items.statement: Traditional syndication deal closures delayed due to industry transition, expected in coming quarters
items.quote: there were certain delays in deal closures in our traditional syndication business, which were largely a result of transitional changes in the media industry over the past few quarters. We expect these deals to materialize in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Full-year APE growth outlook revised to 18-20%
items.quote: So, I think 18% to 20% revision in our outlook on a full year basis is something we feel reasonably confident about.

items.statement: Full-year VNB growth guidance of 15-17%
items.quote: We will continue to deliver on a full year basis in that range. Maybe this could be a little bit lower or higher, but roughly in the 15% to 17% range in terms of VNB growth.

items.statement: ULIP mix to remain range-bound in the 30s; non-par savings near 40%
items.quote: Unit-linked will continue to remain range-bound. It is unlikely to reach the levels of 50% that is quite common in our sector, but it will be range-bound in the 30s.

items.statement: Par products targeted to reach ~20% of business in H2
items.quote: Par going up to about 1/5th of our business would be a good outcome in H2, and that's the endeavour.

items.statement: Retail protection momentum expected to sustain for rest of year
items.quote: We expect the healthy momentum in retail protection to sustain for the rest of the year.

items.statement: Credit protect segment soft due to partner disbursement calibration
items.quote: The credit protect segment has been soft this year on account of calibration in disbursements across some of our partners and lines of businesses.

items.statement: Annuity growth slower due to aggressive unsustainable peer pricing; maintaining pricing discipline
items.quote: Our annuity business experienced slower growth on the back of aggressive and unsustainable pricing by some peers. We continue to adopt a calibrated growth strategy, focusing on enhancing our product offerings whilst maintaining pricing discipline.

items.statement: Surrender regulation impact estimated at 100 bps; renegotiating commissions with partners to mitigate
items.quote: We have said that there will be a 100 basis points impact at the company level. At the same time, we will try and reduce that impact by renegotiating with 300-plus partners and all our 2 lakh-plus agents, and we are right now in that process.

items.statement: Commercial transition with distributors expected to complete in H2
items.quote: We expect to complete changeover across all our distributors in H2.

items.statement: Raised Rs 1,000 crore subordinated debt at 8.05%; solvency improved to 192%
items.quote: As we had indicated, we raised subordinated debt of Rs 1,000 cr ore in the last week, thereby improving our solvency to 192% post the sub-debt raise

items.statement: IFRS implementation expected from April 2027 with 24-30 month preparation window
items.quote: IRDA's intent to roll it ou t from April 2027. So , there is a p hase-wise implementation plan, which we understand will be followed where all the large listed as well as unlisted insurance companies will go into Phase 1. And we basically have this window of about 24 to 30 months to get this done

items.statement: H1 VNB margin 24.6% vs 26.3% FY24; compression from product mix and repricing deferral
items.quote: Our H1 value of new business was Rs. 1,656 crore, reflecting a 17.4% YoY growth and new business margins of 24.6%. The margin compression is primarily attributed to product mix and deferment in repricing of certain traditional products.

items.statement: Repricing deferral impacted H1 margin by 30-40 bps; Q2 impact ~100 bps
items.quote: Up to 30-40 basis points is something that we would attribute to delayed repricing. But a significant part of impact would be still attributed to the change in product mix.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic about Q3 momentum but expect seasonal headwinds from furloughs and fewer billing days to moderate growth
items.quote: We are cautiously optimistic about this momentum carrying forward into Q3. However, historically, Q3 experiences seasonal headwinds as well due to furloughs and fewer billing days, which could moderate this momentum to some extent.

items.statement: Wage hikes in Q3 expected to impact margins by approximately 200 basis points, partially offset by operational efficiencies
items.quote: So in terms of our wage hike impact, you could take it maybe approximately 200 basis points, which will be partly offset by our continued operational efficiencies, which we had started driving any which way, 2, 3 quarters back and which are continuing.

items.statement: Q2 order inflow at $1.3 billion TCV; large deal pipeline grown to over $5 billion
items.quote: Q2 order inflow stood at TCV of US$1.3 billion.

items.statement: Large deal pipeline has grown to over $5 billion with strong traction in BFSI and manufacturing verticals
items.quote: I think from a large deal momentum perspective, the pipeline continues to be strong. It has grown to over $5 billion right now from a large deal perspective.

items.statement: EBIT margin expanded 50 bps sequentially to 15.5% in Q2, mainly due to absence of visa costs
items.quote: Our EBIT margin expanded by 50 basis points to 15.5% as compared with 15% in the previous quarter majorly on account of absence of visa costs.

items.statement: Discretionary spend remains on pause for 5-6 quarters except for AI-related investments; cost takeout and regulatory compliance driving deals
items.quote: On the discretionary when clients are trying to build new applications, I think it has been kind of on a pause for the last more than 5, 6 quarters.

items.statement: Furloughs expected to return to normal levels this year after being higher than anticipated last year
items.quote: We realized that last year, the furloughs were a little more than what we had anticipated. So, our expectation this year is that the furloughs will be back to the regular levels that we used to have.

items.statement: AI-first strategy anchored on three principles: AI in Everything, Everything for AI, AI for Everyone; 63% of workforce trained in Gen AI
items.quote: Currently, 63% of our workforce is trained and equipped with Gen AI capabilities.

items.statement: Added 2,500+ employees in Q2 including 1,100+ freshers; headcount rose to over 84,000
items.quote: Our headcount rose to over 84,000 at the end of the quarter as we added 2,500+ employees during the quarter.

items.statement: US elections and macro uncertainty make budget cycle prediction difficult; Travel & Hospitality vertical softness due to Boeing delivery issues and high interest rates impacting real estate
items.quote: It's a little too early to predict about the budget cycle, etcetera, given the fact that in the U.S., elections are also on our way.

items.statement: Target utilization around 85%; currently at 87.7% excluding trainees; margin improvement journey elongated due to external environment, focus on maintaining margins until double-digit industry growth returns
items.quote: Our target utilization range will be something around 85%, that will be ideal.

items.statement: Declared interim dividend of INR 20 per equity share; cash and investments at $1.43 billion (INR 11,974 crores)
items.quote: The Board of Directors have declared an interim dividend of INR20 per equity share.

items.statement: Revised FY25 revenue growth guidance to 3.75%-4.5% in constant currency; operating margin guidance unchanged at 20%-22%
items.quote: With a strong performance in Q2 and our current outlook, we have revised our revenue growth guidance for the financial year. The new guidance is 3.75% to 4.5% growth in constant currency. Our operating margin guidance for the financial year remains the same at 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Q2 operating margin stable at 21.1%; Project Maximus contributed 80 bps benefit offset by 60 bps from higher variable pay and other costs
items.quote: Operating margin was stable at 21.1%. The major components of sequential margin walk are- Tailwinds of - 80 basis points benefit from Project Maximus - 10 basis points from the currency movement Offset by - 30 basis point impact from acquisitions mainly on account of amortization of intangible assets - 60 basis points from higher variable pay and other costs

items.statement: Financial Services discretionary spend increasing in capital markets, mortgages, cards and payments; automotive sector in Europe showing slowness; other verticals prioritizing cost takeout over discretionary initiatives
items.quote: The Financial Services segment in the U.S. continues to see discretionary spend increase in capital markets, mortgages, cards and payments. We have seen slowness in the automotive sector in Europe. Apart from these verticals, demand trends re main stable with clients continue to prioritize cost takeout over discretionary

items.statement: Employee compensation increase to be launched in two phases effective Jan 1, 2025 and April 1, 2025
items.quote: We will launch our employee compensation increase in two phases, effective Jan 1, 2025 and April 1, 2025.

items.statement: Large deals TCV at $2.4 bn in Q2; pipeline for deals below $50 mn increased double digits sequentially
items.quote: Our large deals were $2.4 bn. Our overall pipeline remains strong. We saw a double-digit q uarter-on-quarter increase in our pipeline of deals below $50 mn

items.statement: Deepening Generative AI work: deploying enterprise GenAI platforms, building small language model using industry and Infosys datasets, launched multi-agent capabilities
items.quote: We are deepening our work in Generative AI. items.statement: Head of Sales Joseph Crowley resigned due to medical situation; position vacant temporarily
items.quote: Yes, so the Head of Sales position, that is really due to a medical situation with that leader. And so due to the timeframes involved for that, this is why we've had to unfortunately vacate that position for this point in time.

items.statement: Semiconductor synergy with parent Cyient exists but not expected to materialize for several years; chip design must precede board/box build consumption
items.quote: I think we won't expect anything to play out from that synergy at least for a few years because we will first have to start designing the chips and then looking at how those chips can be consumed in science DLM

items.statement: NIM expected around 4% next quarter without policy rate changes
items.quote: Considering all these factors and without taking into any policy rate changes, we expect that NIM will be around 4% in the next quarter.

items.statement: ROA guided above 1.65% going forward
items.quote: We had guided that our effort would be to ensure ROA is above 1.65% levels and we are confident to maintain the same going forward also.

items.statement: Gross slippages to stay below 1% annualized
items.quote: With our continued close monitoring of accounts we are confident that we'll continue to keep the ratio below 1% as guided in our earlier call.

items.statement: Gross NPA to stay below 2%
items.quote: We expect that we will continue to maintain at below 2% levels as advised earlier.

items.statement: Net NPA to stay below 1%
items.quote: We will continue to maintain net NPA at less than 1% of our loan book.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio to be pegged within 50%
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio is at 46.72%, and we will continue our efforts to peg it within 50%.

items.statement: Cost of deposits expected to rise 10 bps next quarter
items.quote: Based on our historical pattern of renewal of deposits and fresh deposits acquisition, we expect moderated rise in the cost of deposits by 10 basis points in the next quarter.

items.statement: Yield on advances expected flat next quarter
items.quote: Yield on advances is expected to be flat, and yield on investments would be in the similar range for the second quarter -- of the second quarter.

items.statement: NIM at 4.11% for Q2 FY25 and 4.12% for H1 FY25
items.quote: I'm happy to say that the NIM for the quarter is at 4.11%, and for the half year, it is 4.12%.

items.statement: Corporate book degrew 4% due to lower availments and exits where pricing not conducive
items.quote: Corporate book has degrown by 4% during the quarter, mainly due to lower availments in certain seasonal sectors, lower disbursements, repayments. And of course, as I always say, wherever the pricing was not conducive enough, so on our own we have exited those accounts.

items.statement: RAM advances grew 5% QoQ; retail mortgages up 10%, housing 3%, jewel loans 7%
items.quote: I am pleased to share that the same is being sustained in the RAM verticals with 5% quarter-on-quarter loan growth. Commercial advances clocked 6% growth. Retail advance and agriculture advances grew by 4% each. Retail growth was predominantly driven by mortgages, which grew 10% during the quarter. Housing loans grew by 3% and jewel loans by 7%.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio at 26% of advances, aim to cap near 30%
items.quote: So 3 years back itself, we have given an Classification | EXTERNAL indication that we would like to go up to around 30% because too much of concentration in a particular product also is risky. So now if you look at 25.1% has become 26% now

items.statement: First set of lite branches expected to function in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The setting up of the lite branches is under progress and the first set of such branches are expected to function on the third quarter of this current year.

items.statement: Recovered INR180 crores from technically written-off books in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our efforts on recovery of technically written-off books is continuing to yield results as we have recovered a sum of INR180 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: LCR at 128% on revised methodology, fully sorted
items.quote: It has been fully sorted out. It started in last week of June, the revised methodology. And this full quarter, it has been fully on the revised methodology only -- so -- and it varies, for example, the 128% on an average basis for 90 days.

items.statement: FY25 net loan loss to average assets guided at 2% to 2.05%, more likely 2.05%
items.quote: At this juncture from a guidance standpoint, I would say that we estimate the FY25 net loan loss to average assets to be between 2% and 2.05%.

items.statement: Loan loss to average AUM expected to decline to around 2% by Q4 FY25
items.quote: We are cautiously optimistic looking at the portfolio movement or gross flow rate methodology that loan loss to average AUF has hopefully peaked and we estimate loan loss to average to go down to 2% or so by Q4.

items.statement: Medium-term credit cost expected at 185-195 bps for next fiscal year
items.quote: As you said earlier that principally the 172 basis points that we used to be pre-Covid based on the regulatory changes and our write off policy changes adds up being between 185 to 195 basis points.

items.statement: AUM growth guided at 27%-28% for FY25 with new businesses contributing 2%-3%
items.quote: As we forecast full year, we see the growth at 27%-28% with new businesses and mostly being secured in nature contributing about 2% to 3% of the AUM growth for the current year.

items.statement: Medium-term guardrails remain 25%-27% AUM growth and 23%-25% profit compounding
items.quote: We remain guided by our medium-term guardrails which is 25%-27% AUM growth and leading to a 23%-25% profit compounding.

items.statement: New customer additions estimated at 15-16 million for FY25, targeting 100 million franchise
items.quote: We now estimate that our overall new customer addition to be 15 to 16 million in FY25 which will be in line with what we originated last year marginally higher, last year we did 14 million customers, this year we foresee between 15 to 16 million new customer addition.

items.statement: Non-Bajaj two-wheeler financing to reach 720,000 accounts in FY26, fully replacing Bajaj Auto AUM by FY27
items.quote: We expected to disburse just a tad below 500,000 accounts in the current year and scale to 720,000 accounts in FY26. So, as the as Bajaj Auto products AUM goes away this AUM will replace it fully by FY27, by end FY26/FY27.

items.statement: Rural B2C growth forecast at 12%-14% for FY25, potentially 23%-25% in FY26
items.quote: We foresee that business still however may grow only by 12% to 14% on a full year basis. That's on rural B2C at this point in time.

items.statement: Investments in new business launches have peaked, expected to swing from loss to breakeven/profit in FY26
items.quote: I think the point that Sandeep made on investments have peaked out in launch of new businesses and geographies is an important point. And they should swing from loss to start to breakeven/generating profit as we get into the next fiscal.

items.statement: NIM stabilized at current levels, cost of funds peaked at 7.97%
items.quote: Overall NIM in our assessment is now stabilized, between Q1 and Q2 there is hardly any drop. We think the NIM is now stabilized at these levels from here on.

items.statement: 25 bps repo rate cut expected to improve NIM by 10-12 bps over 12 months with 1-2 quarter lag
items.quote: We forecast that on a 12-month trailing basis, a 25 basis point drop in repo rate should clearly lead to a 10 to 12 basis point improvement in the NIM.

items.statement: NIM improvement to be used for growing secured and new business lines, not taken to P&L
items.quote: Idea would be to not take it through the P&L, idea would be to use this opportunity for improving the quotient of secure balance sheet in the overall portfolio and continue to create a resilient balance sheet focusing on the new lines of business that we have launched in the last 2 years.

items.statement: Festive season discretionary consumption showing 20%-22% count growth and 19%-20% value growth in first 19 days
items.quote: So far 20 days into or 19 days into the season, numbers looking like 21% in terms of count. In terms of value, in terms of discretionary its clearly prices have cooled a little across phones and televisions and so on and so forth. Given reduction in raw material prices we are seeing a 19%-20%.

items.statement: Clients with 3+ live unsecured loans show higher default propensity; underwriting tightened for such cohorts
items.quote: Those clients who have more than three or more live unsecured loans are showing higher propensity to default and in general have lower downstream lower collection efficiencies. So, as we look at this data, we are continuing to tighten our underwriting norms for such cohorts of customers across all our products in an intelligent manner.

items.statement: Stage-2 and Stage-3 asset additions slowed to 542 crores in Q2 from 1,100 crores in Q1
items.quote: Just to give you context, our last quarter the Stage-2 and Stage-3 on account of various disruption that we had referred to in Q1 and I am not repeating it has seen actually 1,100 crores of movement. So, Q1 had seen 1,100 crores of addition to Stage-2 and Stage-3 versus that in the current quarter the movement to Stage-2 and Stage-3 is 542 crores.

items.statement: Bajaj Auto captive portfolio wind-down to reduce consolidated GNPA contribution from 18% over 2 years
items.quote: If you look at it today as of September, it's 4.3% of the balance sheet and it is 18% of consolidated GNPA. This is a factual number as of Q2. So, eventually as this book winds down, we will see the benefit come through in the overall loan loss to average AUF.

items.statement: Moody's assigned Baa3/P long-term rating (sovereign rating) to Bajaj Finance
items.quote: We are happy to inform you that Moody's has also assigned a Baa 3/P long term rating which is the sovereign rating to Bajaj Finance as well.

items.statement: FY25 credit growth slower than system, FY26 at or around system growth, FY27 faster than system growth
items.quote: FY '25, we would probably grow slower than the system. FY '26, we may be at or around the system growth rate. FY '27, we should be faster than the system growth rate.

items.statement: NIM stable at 3.45% to 3.5%, printed at 3.46% this quarter
items.quote: The margins have been stable in the range that we have been talking about at 3.45% to 3.5%. It's printed at 3.46%.

items.statement: Target LDR in high 80s within 2-3 years, accelerated from earlier 4-5 year plan
items.quote: Instead of that, there is an opportunity right now with the rate of credit growth being high over the last two years and is expected to come down to maybe the deposit level rate of growth. And so, in this scenario, it was appropriate for us to rethink to say, we will do it within two to three years to get to the high 80s, right?

items.statement: Mortgage growing at 11.7% YoY, non-mortgage retail moderated to 9-10% YoY from 19% previously due to credit calibration
items.quote: And as it relates to non -mortgage retail, we grew 11% this year -- year-on-year in this quarter that you are seeing, but we have moderated the growth purely based on credit dynamics that our credit underwriting standards -- underwriting team looks at certain standards and calibrates that.

items.statement: Loan spreads pressured down while bond spreads up 15-30bps; unable to pass on higher rates due to legacy bank competition
items.quote: If you look at even in this quarter, the bond spreads on a two-year AAA or a one-year AAA bond spreads have moved between 15 to 30 basis points up. Loan spreads in the market are pressurized to come down.

items.statement: No red or amber alerts on asset quality; portfolio stable with retail GNPA at 0.8%; well positioned for cycle turn
items.quote: And good to say that as of now, we are not seeing any red alerts or amber alerts, and we continue to calibrate our growth depending on what pulse we have at the ground level.

items.statement: Added 240 branches this quarter, 350 YTD; continue calibrated branch expansion for reach and density
items.quote: We grew 240-odd branches in this quarter, 350 something for the year so far. Last year, we grew 917 branches. Our objective has been to make those investments and branches now when the credit has been benign.

items.statement: Priority sector lending at ~50% aggregate; small/marginal farmer slightly under target at <1% gap; organic focus at 9-9.5%
items.quote: As far as the PSL achievement is concerned for March '24 that is already published that you will be able to see it. It's in our annual report and various other disclosures. We are close enough in terms of at an aggregate leve l, our PSL was 50 -odd percent aggregate level.

items.statement: HDB Financial IPO process kicked off; must list by September 2025 per upper tier circular; no further details due to publicity guidelines
items.quote: The circular for the upper tier came that requires HDB to be listed by September '25. The process for that listing was kicked off. As you know, we put out certain press releases after various Board deliberations here as well as in HDB between July and August, and the process has kicked off.

items.statement: RBI draft circular on group lending overlap is draft; comments due Nov 20; HDB is licensed regulated entity with no arbitrage vs bank
items.quote: There are two aspects to what you're asking. One is draft circular. The word is -- underlying word here, it is draft, number one. Number two, the comments are required to be submitted by November 20, our bank, and I'm sure the banking fraternity would be providing similar comments.

items.statement: LCR at 128% vs target 110-120%; elevated due to deposit inflows and loan calibration; may normalize when regulatory clarity emerges
items.quote: See, one, the liquidity coverage ratio is at 128. We have told you that our target that we normally tend to operate is between 110 to 120. And somewhere historically, we operated at that 115 or thereabouts plus/minus 1%, 2%.

items.statement: Floating rate loans ~69-70% of book (mostly EBLR); MCLR tiny portion; rest fixed rate
items.quote: The loans that are floating, our external benchmark is, I think, roughly about 69%, 70% or thereabouts which is similar to what last quarter or the previous quarter that we had mentioned. So, it is pretty at that level.

items.statement: Hedges on inherited HDFC borrowings continue; quantified annually in derivative schedule, not quarterly
items.quote: Yes, we do carry those hedges. That hedges presupposes there is a borrowing that is attached. So, to the extent that the bo rrowings have not been paid down, that means they are not rolled down or prepaid, the hedges continue.

items.statement: Savings account credits growing robustly in 20s%; adding >2M customers/quarter; spends on cards high teens to low 20s%
items.quote: When you look at the credits that are coming into the accounts, they are robustly growing, growing in 20s, right . So that means -- that's again contributed by new customers, too. So, I'm not talking about a static customer base. I'm talking about adding every quarter, a little more than 2 million customer base coming in, shows that the credits do increase, and we are seeing robust increase in the

items.statement: Matched modified duration limits near-term NIM impact from rate cuts; medium-term NIM kicker expected when LCR normalizes and liquidity sustains
items.quote: All along we have maintained a very matched modified duration of our balance sheet. So, our view is that we should not have too much of an impact in the range at which we have been operating the margins in the near term.

items.statement: No credit concerns in CRB/MSME book; growth not inhibited by asset quality in that segment
items.quote: We have not seen in our book any kind of a credit that inhibits the growth or inhibits any kind of different approach to how we operate that.

items.statement: Mass ABS project first phase (70,000 tpa) expected to be completed by March 2025
items.quote: On the CAPEX front, the implementation of the first phase of mass ABS project, with a capacity of 70,000 tonnes per annum is expected to be completed by March 2025.

items.statement: FY25 CAPEX projected around Rs 380 crore
items.quote: FY25 our CAPEX is projected with around 380 crores

items.statement: Haryana greenfield project pre-project activities ongoing; will take six to eight months before work can start
items.quote: we bought the land, we are doing the pre-project activities including the environment clearances and environment impact assessment and other approvals which are needed. So, all that work is going on, it is a long drawn process. lt will take another six to eight months before we can really start the work there

items.statement: Normal EBITDA margin range is 9% to 10%; FY22 high margins were due to post-COVID supply constraints and high shipping rates
items.quote: we are currently in at normal delta scenario where we are at between 9% lo 10% EBITDA margins

items.statement: Power cost at Nagothane plant expected to fall ~25% once solar supply from PPA with TP Saturn/Tata Power commences
items.quote: based on our current production levels, we expect that our electricity cost will come down by 25% with regard to Nagothane

items.statement: Domestic PS demand strong; OEM sector grew ~30% in H1 FY25; non-OEM segment saw some slowdown
items.quote: Demand for PS is good in lndia, since OEM sector is strong. lt's only that in the non-OEM sectorthere has been some slowdown. OEM demand is strong if I look atthe overall first half of the year, the OEM sector witnessed almost 30% growth in the demand

items.statement: Volume growth guidance for FY25 revised to 5-6% YoY due to export slowdown; earlier volume target ~340,000 tonnes
items.quote: Now with the slowdown in the export market, our volume growth could be on 5% to 6% over the previous year.

items.statement: Revenue mix: ~2/3 from PS, ~1/4 from EPS, ~1/10 from other manufactured products
items.quote: It is two thirds from PS, about one fourth from EPS and one tenth from the other products, for manufactured product sales.

items.statement: Mass ABS line 1 potential revenue ~Rs 1,000 crore at peak utilization
items.quote: The line one would give us around 1000 crores.

items.statement: Annual FY25 revenue guidance of INR 2,225 crores and EBITDA margin of 24%
items.quote: To conclude, we stick to our annual guidance of achieving revenue of INR 2,225 crores, an EBITDA margin of 24% for FY '25 and are very confident with the order book we have , that we will be able to execute the same in the balance part of FY '25.

items.statement: Confident of achieving FY25 annual guidance despite Q2 revenue dip due to delayed order inflow
items.quote: However, we see good demand and orders in H2 and are optimistic of achieving our overall annual guidance of FY '25.

items.statement: Gear division order intake INR 432 crores in Q2 FY25, up 15.2% YoY; order in hand INR 627 crores as of Sept 30, 2024
items.quote: The order intake for Q2 FY '25 stood at INR 432 crores up by 15.2% on year -on-year basis. Order in hand is INR 627 crores as on 30th September 2024.

items.statement: MHE division order inflow INR 104 crores in Q2 FY25, up 154% YoY; open order INR 339 crores as of Sept 30, 2024
items.quote: The order inflow during the quarter ended September 2024 stood at INR 104 crores as compared to INR 41 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, up by 154% on year -on-year basis. The open order as on 30th September 2024 stood at INR 339 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 22.1%, down from 24.5% YoY due to higher freight, one-time repairs, and product mix shift
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 22.1%. margin saw a dip primarily due to higher freight costs and one -time repairs and maintenance expenses incurred during the quarter.

items.statement: Gear division EBIT margin 20.5% in Q2 FY25 vs 26% YoY, impacted by one-time repairs, air freight, and product mix changes
items.quote: The EBIT margin for Q2 FY '25 stood at 20.5% as compared to 26% in Q2 FY '24. EBIT margin was largely impacted on account of certain one -time repair and maintenance expenses as mentioned previously. Increase in freight cost, especially a ir freight for certain deliveries to marquee OEMs in the stipulated timeframe and changes in the product mix with respect to engineered and catalogue products.

items.statement: MHE division EBIT margin 26.5% in Q2 FY25, up ~549 bps YoY due to better product mix and higher aftermarket contribution
items.quote: The EBIT margin stood at 26.5% as against 21% in Q2 FY '24, increasing approximately 549 basis points on a year-on-year basis. The increasing is largely on account of better product mix and higher contributions on the aftermarket segment.

items.statement: One-time repair costs INR 1 crore and air freight INR 1 crore plus packing material INR 1.68 crores in Q2 FY25 due to Red Sea crisis
items.quote: So we upgraded to that also with total amount included crores for this Q2 which is having an impact on it. On account of the freight, because of this geopolitical tension, to deliver our goods, we have to opt for the air freight, which itself cost to me additional cost of INR1 crores for that all. So, over and above that we also have to incur some specific expenses for the material -- packing mate

items.statement: Majority of clients agreed to bear extra freight costs due to ships rerouting via Cape of Good Hope
items.quote: And we have also taken it up with our clients and requested them to give us extra amounts for the increase in freight because now the ships are going through Cape of Good Hope rather than going through the Suez Canal. So majority of them have agreed to it. So that would not be an issue going forward.

items.statement: Domestic demand momentum increasing post-elections; power, mining, steel, cement sectors showing strong traction for H2 FY25 and FY26
items.quote: What we find is that especially in India, after the elections, the momentum and the number of inquiries has been continuously increasing, okay? The demand for products in material handling as well as in gears is on the rise, okay? It started a bit slowly, but now it has got good momentum. And we believe that after Diwali it would further add to the momentum, okay? Things are looking good like befo

items.statement: Export business growing with 28% revenue contribution in H1 FY25; targeting 50% by FY30; breakthrough in Russia and OEM traction
items.quote: With increasing references and OEM tie-ups, we are optimistic of increasing our overseas business and achieving revenue contribution to 50% by FY '30 from overseas business.

items.statement: Capex of INR 40-45 crores in H1 FY25; machine tools ordered, most to be installed in H2 FY25; revenue contribution from FY26
items.quote: This year we did additions of nearly INR 40 crores, INR45 crores in the first half. And we are expecting more machines to reach over here in H2 and I think most of them will get installed in this year itself. Garvit Goyal: And the revenue will start kicking in next year

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (Red Sea crisis) increasing freight costs; air freight used for timely OEM deliveries
items.quote: Apart from that, this particular quarter, because of the Houthis intervention in the Gulf of Aden, we had to pay extra freight to transport the products to Europe as well as to United States, which has also reduced our margins.

items.statement: Consolidated net free cash surplus INR 500+ crores as of Sept 30, 2024; H1 FY25 operating cash flow INR 175 crores, EBITDA to CFO conversion 117%
items.quote: Further, on the balance she et front, we are happy to say that the consolidated net free cash surplus stood at INR 500 plus crores as on 30th September 2024. The cash flow from operations stood at INR 175 crores for H1 FY '25 and EBITDA to CFO conversion stood at 117%.

items.statement: Interim dividend declared of Re 0.50 per share (50% of face value Re 1)
items.quote: Furthermore, we are pleased that the board has declared an interim dividend of Re . 0.50 each at the rate of 50% per equity share of face value Re. 1 each.

items.statement: Management does not provide revenue guidance
items.quote: As you know, we don't provide any guidance.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin was 16.5% in Q2 FY25, up 125 bps QoQ
items.quote: Our operating EBITDA for the quarter was at 16.5%, showing an improvement of 125 bps quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Full quarter wage hike impact of 120-130 bps expected in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Wage hike, as you rightly said, we have done partially this quarter and the full quarter impact will be in Q3, which will take the full quarter impact. So, we believe quarter-on-quarter 120 to 130 bps impact will come.

items.statement: Targeting North America margins in mid-teens by end of FY25
items.quote: By the time we end this year, we want to be in mid-teens at least. That's the target we are running with.

items.statement: Endeavour to operate at 17%-18% EBITDA margin
items.quote: So again, as we said, that we endeavour 17% to 18%.

items.statement: 12-month order backlog grew 17.9% YoY, flat QoQ in constant currency
items.quote: During the quarter, we have onboarded 14 new customers, and consequently, our 12-month order backlog grew by 17.9% year-on-year. On a quarter-on-quarter terms, it's a marginal increase of 1.2% in INR terms, broadly flat when you see on a constant currency basis.

items.statement: UK government healthcare investment driving positive business impact
items.quote: The health care investment of the government, which is now much more stronger and directional is very positively impacting our business.

items.statement: North America grew 18% QoQ across all sectors including Oracle, Salesforce, Data and Healthcare
items.quote: We saw 18% quarter-over-quarter growth in North America. This has been backed by healthy performance across all our sectors and which is Oracle, Salesforce, Data and including healthcare and all the other commercial verticals that we focus on.

items.statement: AI use cases expected to generate revenue in next two quarters
items.quote: We are running quite a few POCs with our customers, and we hope as we get into the next two quarters, we'll start seeing some revenue flow from these new applications or use cases that we are doing.

items.statement: Significant investments in AI skills, training, tooling and partnerships
items.quote: We are making some serious investments in terms of resources and capabilities to really upgrade our skills there, including training and tooling and partnerships.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic due to US elections, UK budget finalization, Middle East unrest
items.quote: We have some important global events happening, the elections in North America, the U.K. going through their strategic directions and priority finalization. And of course, there is some unrest in the Middle East market.

items.statement: DSO increased to 95 days, expected to improve in Q3-Q4 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, our DSO got expanded to 95 days versus 92 days. This was predominantly due to certain expected collections getting right shifted. We don't see any challenge. And in Q 3 to Q4, we'll be able to further improve the DSO profile of the company

items.statement: Borrowing increased by ~$24-25M for MST earnout payout, no further earnouts expected
items.quote: There is an increase of approximate USD 24mn to USD 25mn during the quarter as we had to borrow money for the payout of earnouts relating to MST acquisition. It was the only one amount which has been discharged. And now Mastek owns the Salesforce MST business completely and there is no further payout, which is expected in the future quarters.

items.statement: Strategic reduction in client count continuing, further reductions planned in AMEA region
items.quote: We still see some more reduction in accounts, especially in the AMEA region, where we continue to have still a pretty long tail. So we would be making some more reductions in the AMEA region in terms of the number of small accounts or non-priority accounts that we have.

items.statement: Industry expected to grow 7-8% in Q3 FY25; TVS will outperform industry
items.quote: I think industry will definitely do well, 7% to 8% is a good growth rate.

items.statement: Capex guidance maintained at INR1,200-1,400 crores for FY25
items.quote: INR1,200 crores to INR1,400 crores, that is the range we gave last time. That still holds on.

items.statement: Investment spend around INR1,500 crores for FY25
items.quote: Investment, just a minute, I think investments again around INR1,500 crores is what we said last time.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 70 bps YoY to 11.7% in Q2 FY25; confident of continued improvement
items.quote: Recorded highest ever operating EBITDA of INR1,080 crores, with a growth of 20% and margin improved by 70 bps from 11% during Q2 of last year to 11.7% during this quarter.

items.statement: Material cost improved from 74% to 71.4% YoY; no significant commodity headwinds seen
items.quote: Last year was 74%. This year is 71.4%.

items.statement: Festival season industry growth 4% overall; 10-11% during Navratri; TVS growing significantly better
items.quote: During Navratri, it was around industry grew by 11% and TVS has grown significantly better during this season.

items.statement: EV penetration at 7% in Q2; iQube sales up 31% YoY to 75,000 units; three battery options launched
items.quote: It is already around 7% in Q2, so overall the penetration of EV.

items.statement: TVS Credit book size INR26,652 crores, up 13% YoY; 27-28% two-wheeler concentration
items.quote: The book size is 26,652, grown by 13% over last year's quarter 2.

items.statement: Red Sea challenges continue with increased transit times; countermeasures taken; Africa facing currency depreciation and inflation
items.quote: Challenges in Red Sea have continued in the current quarter. The transit times have increased.

items.statement: Norton motorcycle launches expected in FY26 (6 quarters from now)
items.quote: It will take another 6 quarters for the product to be available in the market, okay? And these are going to be brilliant products, and you will see products from ' 2026, okay, which in our financial year, 2025-26.

items.statement: EV revenue INR1,600 crores for H1 FY25
items.quote: For the first half it is about INR1,600 crores.

items.statement: ESOP provision of INR11-12 crores in Q2 FY25
items.quote: There is a provision of about INR11 crores to INR12 crores towards that ESOP.

items.statement: No impairment needed for European e-bike business; inventory reduced and cash generated
items.quote: There is no need for any impairment-related provisions. We are very confident about that business and the future.

items.statement: Exports revenue INR2,229 crores; spares revenue INR930 crores in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Spares is about INR930 crores and exports revenue is INR2,229 for Q2.

items.statement: Africa constitutes 55-57% of export volumes in H1 FY25
items.quote: Africa is about, I think first half, it's about 55% to 57%.

items.statement: EV manufacturing capacity can be increased in 3 months (90 days); dealer network at 750 touchpoints
items.quote: We have enough capacity. And even whenever we want to increase the capacity, it's a question of about 3 months, okay 3 months, 90 days is not a big period.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 credit cost guided at 1.3% to 1.5%
items.quote: we do foresee for FY '25 exit, the credit cost numbers in the range of 1.3% to 1.5%.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 NIM guided at 6.5% to 6.7%
items.quote: what we expect for the full year closing is in the range of 6.5% to 6.7%.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 ROA visibility at 1.8% to 2%, bullish on 2%
items.quote: we do have a visibility for the full year to be clearly in 1.8 to the 2 range and I would still be more bullish on the 2 range for the FY '25 exit.

items.statement: 3-year disbursement CAGR aspiration of 15% to 20%
items.quote: We are looking from a 3-year horizon to be in the 15% to 20% CAGR.

items.statement: Medium-term credit cost corridor of 1.2% to 1.5%

items.statement: No fresh equity raise planned in current financial year
