items.statement: Diversification at 6% of mix, below 15% plan; MSME, leasing, mortgages, insurance agency building blocks in place
items.quote: this is currently at -- I mean it's at 6% currently and will go up marginally for the rest of the year but admitting that this is trended below plan. The plan was quite aggressive at 15% of the overall mix.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance of at least Rs 10,000 crore
items.quote: we think that we will be able to close this year with a capex of about Rs 10,000 crore at least.

items.statement: EBITDA growth expected to exceed 15% for FY25
items.quote: Now, this will surely bring the growth in EBITDA that we projected, which will be more than 15%.

items.statement: EBITDA growth expected in excess of 20% over next couple of years
items.quote: Therefore, the growth is going to correspond to that kind of capex, which it will be in excess of 20%.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex deployed Rs 4,400 crore, 1.7x YoY
items.quote: The total capex of first half of the current year, which is Rs 4,400 crore, is 1.7 times of the capex that we deployed in the same period last year.

items.statement: FY25 capex split: distribution Rs 1,600-1,700 crore, smart metering Rs 3,000 crore, rest transmission
items.quote: Out of this Rs 10,000 crore, the distribution would be around Rs 1,600 crore to Rs 1,700 crore, smart metering around Rs 3,000 crore, and the rest will be from the transmission side.

items.statement: Under-construction transmission projects ~Rs 31,000 crore, to commission over FY25-FY27
items.quote: we have secured four new transmission projects and with that our under-construction projects have reached to ~Rs 31,000 crore from Rs 17,000 crore.

items.statement: Under-construction projects to contribute ~Rs 4,200 crore EBITDA upon completion
items.quote: Once these projects worth ~Rs 31,000 crore are completed, it will contribute to EBITDA of about ~Rs 4,200 crore.

items.statement: Expect to add Rs 15,000-20,000 crore transmission projects in next 6 months
items.quote: we hope to get about Rs 15,000 crore to Rs 20,000 crore worth project more in next six month's time.

items.statement: Transmission bidding pipeline Rs 85,000 crore in next 6 months, another Rs 1 lakh crore in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: in the next six months, Mohit, we expect to witness a bidding of about Rs 85,000 crore capex of transmission project.

items.statement: Smart meter deployment target 30-35 lakh meters in H2 FY25, 40-45 lakh total FY25
items.quote: We expect to add about 30 to 35 lakh meters in next six months. So, we will close year with the installation of about 40 to 42 lakh meters.

items.statement: Smart meter deployment rate reached 10,000/day, targeting 16,000-20,000/day from next quarter
items.quote: We have already reached upto 10,000 meters per day from 4,000 meters per day and expect to take it up to 16,000 meters per day to 20,000 meters per day.

items.statement: FY26 smart meter target ~1 crore meters, balance in subsequent year
items.quote: at least we will be able to add about 1 crore meter next year and balance one in the subsequent year.

items.statement: C&I business: 20 MW contracted, 250 MW in discussion, targeting 5,000 MU by year-end for Rs 150 crore annualized EBITDA
items.quote: By the year-end, we will be able to close, or we'll have a volume of about 5,000 million units. And that will contribute on an annualized basis of about Rs 150 crore of EBITDA.

items.statement: C&I targeting 7,000-10,000 million units in couple of years
items.quote: what we are targeting is about 7,000 million to 10,000 million units in a couple of years.

items.statement: Smart meter margins 80-85% overall, may dip to 75% in initial ramp-up years
items.quote: The smart meters have a margin of around 80% to 85%. In the initial years because of the initial ramp up, the margins may come down to around 75%.

items.statement: C&I margins range from 10 paise/unit for service contracts to Rs 1+/unit for complex contracts
items.quote: it's only a service contract then would be in a simple back -to-back contract then it could be around Rs 10 paise, but if it is a complex contract, a lot of stitching to be done and position is to be taken, then obviously those margins will be in a higher

items.statement: IRRs in recent transmission bids have increased, aggression reduced, no aggressive bidding forcing IRR reduction seen
items.quote: You must have seen the IRRs have increased in the recent bids. The level of aggression certainly has reduced.

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected above Rs 2,000 crore with at least 16% EBITDA margin
items.quote: And if you talk about the top line revenue, that will be also more than 2000 crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected at 20% year-on-year
items.quote: 26 we are expecting 20% growth in the top line.

items.statement: Brownfield capex of Rs 80-90 crore for backward integration to be completed in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: CapEx. So initially we are planning to do as Vimal ji mentioned 80 to 90 crores from the preferential allotment.

items.statement: Preferential allotment of Rs 200 crore approved; 25% expected within 15 days of regulatory approvals
items.quote: We are expecting an in-principal approval for the preferential allotment and we'll be hoping to complete the preferential allotment and 25% payment will be received within 15 days of receipt of all regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded from 26% to 34% YoY in Q2 FY25; B2C gross margin 40-45%, B2B 20-25%
items.quote: The increase in margins was account of stability in raw material prices and higher sales of branded products.

items.statement: Branded business now 65% of revenue; branded volume grew 35% YoY in Q2 FY25 (24% from new launches)
items.quote: Our focus on strengthening our branded business is yielding positive results. So, our branded business is now accounting for 65% of our overall revenue.

items.statement: Expecting strong rabi season due to 88% reservoir levels; Q3 and Q4 sales expected to be significantly better than last year
items.quote: We are expecting a good rabi season, upcoming rabi season.

items.quote: This product has been well accepted by the farmers and we look forward to doin g 100 crores plant business in this full year of induction

items.quote: We have fully updated with the proceedings and as of now, we don't have any extra demand whatever is our regular, we are paying that on time always that is our advantage and everything and according to us, there is no demand we are expecting for this income tax, no extra demand, I mean.

items.statement: Chinese dumping stabilized as prices hit floor; factory shutdowns in China supporting price stability
items.quote: now, we can say to stabilize because once any of the factory in China they are they are under the cost when they are producing. They have to stop because under the cost they cannot survive, so now I would say the situation is ther e where prices have fallen down a lot and now the situation is that the factory has to stop because they cannot run at that level

items.quote: FY '25, we will end up at around INR9,000 crores overall. And '26, I believe we should end up at around INR12,000 crores company-wise.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 2% range for full year FY25 despite Q1-Q2 uptick
items.quote: We had always said that it would be in the 2% range on an overall basis. We'll stick to that and we'll continue to maintain that.

items.statement: Micro LAP expected to be less than 5% of book in near term; guidance for mix after 1 year
items.quote: I would expect Micro LAP to be less than about 5% in the near sort of -- in the near term.

items.statement: HFC sale proceeds of INR1,750 crores to be used for core CV and small business disbursement, loan repayment and opex
items.quote: So the money will be used for our core business which is CV and small businesses. So it's really towards the general business that we do, which is really toward disbursement, loan repayment and regular opex.

items.statement: CV disbursement yields improved to 18.5% from 17.5% a year ago; overall portfolio yield to move toward 18% in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Our yields have also improved significantly. And with our focus on Tier 3 and Tier 4 and also focus on light commercial vehicles and other smaller assets, which we combine and call it as Focus4, the yields have gone up to 18.5% from about 17.5% that was there about a year back.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost reduced from 12.7% in Q4 FY22 to 10.1% in Q2 FY25; repaid INR500 crores high-cost NCDs in Q2
items.quote: Over the last 3 quarters, incrementally funds are being raised at lower levels as the confidence of the bank and the other investors -- other lenders on IndoStar has improved. Our incremental cost has come down from about 12.7% that was there in Q4 FY'22 to 10.1% in Q2 FY'25.

items.statement: Used CV demand to remain strong due to scarcity from COVID years, scrappage policy overhang, and high new vehicle costs
items.quote: Over the past two years, the used CV industry has grown by close to 30% due to price hikes, driving limited supply. This scarcity originates from the COVID years, sale of new vehicles being muted and driven by the move from BS-IV and the industry being impacted by COVID.

items.statement: GNPA at 4.97% and net Stage 3 at 2.5% for standalone; written off INR57.4 crores (>730 DPD) and sold INR320 crores to ARC in August
items.quote: Currently, our GNPA stood at -- stands at 4.97% for FY'25 Q2 for the stand-alone entity. We have also launched our new small business loan division with a focus on micro loans against property, particularly targeted at Tier 3, Tier 4.

items.statement: CV disbursement INR1,499 crores in Q2 FY25, up 53% YoY; consolidated disbursement INR1,724 crores
items.quote: The commercial vehicle disbursement for Q2 FY'25 reached INR1,499 crores, showing a growth of 53% over the previous year of INR948 crores.

items.statement: Raised INR2,361 crores incremental funding in Q2 including INR1,391 crores from banks; completed maiden public NCD issue of INR266 crores at 10.3-10.7% coupon
items.quote: In terms of funding, we have made substantial progress in improving our liquidity position by improving incremental funding -- raising incremental funding of about INR2,361 crores in the second quarter, including INR1,391 crores which came from bank, either in the form of term loans or working capital demand loan or securitization.

items.statement: Used cars and used tractors each not expected to exceed 10% and 5% of CV book respectively; co-lending with ICICI suspended since May 2022
items.quote: It should not be more than 10% each, 10% on used cars and 5% on used tractors.

items.statement: CRISIL upgraded long-term rating to stable from negative, reaffirmed CRISIL AA- and A1+ for commercial paper
items.quote: On September 9th, 2024, the long-term rating of IndoStar Capital Finance Limited's facilities and instruments was upgraded by the rating agency CRISIL to stable from negative while reaffirming the rating at CRISIL AA-, and short-term rating of commercial paper is reaffirmed at A1+.

items.statement: Branch network at ~480 by year-end; no longer targeting 1,000 branches; valuation outsourced to 3 Pan-India agencies, collections in-house
items.quote: We will be, at the end of the year, around 480 branches. Next year, we are planning. We'll come back to you on that.

items.statement: Project LEAP goal of ₹200 billion revenue to be achieved in FY25, a year ahead of FY26 target
items.quote: With ₹100 billion of revenue achieved in the first half, we are set to achieve our Project LEAP goal of ₹ 200 billion revenues a year ahead of the targeted FY 26 timeline.

items.quote: It is pertinent to note that in spite of the contraction, the Wires & Cables business continued to generate margin within the guided EBITDA range of 12% to 14%.

items.quote: So, as of now, as at end of September, the open order book of the RDSS scheme for us was roughly about ₹48 billion.

items.quote: To summarize the key takeaways, we expect the demand momentum to remain strong in the Wires & Cables business , with second half to be better than the first half.

This move underscores our confidence in the business, our business and debt free asset light model, which consistently helps us in delivering a strong return ratios, including ROI and ROC.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin was 38%, down year-on-year due to ₹1 crore Dreamforce event spend, ₹25-30 lakh Odoo event spend, ₹60 lakh travel, and ESOP costs.
items.quote: Other expenses, ₹1 crore is for the Salesforce event, and another ₹25 lakhs, ₹30 lakhs relate to our Odoo event that we attended. And around ₹60 lakhs include for the travel and stay of our employees. So altogether, a ₹2 crores portion that increases in other expenses.

items.statement: More than 80% of revenue comes from repeat customers; top 5 clients contribute 38% and top 10 contribute 52% of H1 FY25 revenue.
items.quote: more than 80% of our revenue comes from the repeat customers. At half year one, our top five client contributed 38% of the total revenue, and our top 10 clients contributed 52% of the total revenue.

items.statement: 80% of revenue from overseas markets; North America 79%, Europe 9%, Rest of World 12%; domestic 20% of total revenue.
items.quote: we continue to maintain a strong international focus with 80% of our revenues coming from the overseas markets. North America remains our largest overseas market with 79% share, followed by Europe 9% and rest of the world 12%. And domestic business contributes 20% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Hired senior talent including a CA with TCS/EY/KPMG background for business analysis and an IIT Delhi graduate with 20-year experience as Director of Operations joining November 19.
items.quote: recently, we have hired a very senior business analyst, BA person who has started his career, who's a CA, who has started his career from TCS, then E&Y, and then KPMG, and he was involved in requirement gathering of the famous Indian government project, income tax. He was the main person. We have hired that person also. We have hired a Director of Operations also. He is going to join on 19th of No

items.statement: Strategic partnership discussions underway with Oracle, Red Hat, IBM, and Dell in India and internationally to drive collaboration and growth.
items.quote: we have been trying to sort of for ge partnerships with big tech giants. For example, we're in talks with Oracle. We're in talks with Red Hat. We are in talks with IBM. We are in talks with Dell. So, all and not only India, outside of India also

items.statement: ESOP non-cash expense will reduce EBITDA by around 2% starting Q3 FY25
items.quote: I think the ESOP cost would be there, and it would be reducing our EBITDA by around 2%.

items.statement: Branding and certification investments are long-term with no immediate revenue impact
items.quote: We have just attended the event , okay? And it is not something that immediate we will start getting the result. It is a long-term. We need to continue it. W e need to continue this

items.statement: Almost all existing clients are asking for Gen AI Private GPT solutions
items.quote: Almost all of our clients are coming to us asking for this. Almost all our clients are coming back to us asking for this.

items.statement: Company remains services-focused; products like Private GPT serve as capability demonstrations to win services deals
items.quote: We are completely into services, and product we are developing, it is not something that we are expecting any drastic change. Okay. So, we are still dependent on the services, but product we are developing in the last previous calls also I explained, products are something which shows them our capability and which is the, you can say, which opens a door to enter into their business.

items.statement: No FX hedging policy currently due to USD tailwind; 80% revenue from North America
items.quote: Currently, we don't have any hedging policy. Simply the reason being the USD tailwind, because the dollar rates are increasing and rupee is depreciating.

items.statement: Acquired 25-30 new customers in Q2 FY25 with initially low ticket sizes that grow over time
items.quote: We have acquired around more than 25, 30 customers in this quarter, quarter two. And since the ticket size, at starting the ticket size used to be low, then significantly it increases at latter point of time for all other projects that we enter into.

items.statement: Actively exploring acquisitions in Salesforce, Big Data, and AI; signed NDAs with merchant bankers
items.quote: I have signed the NDA with some merchant bankers. They are connecting us with the companies who are into Salesforce or Big Data or AI even. Unfortunately, we could not find a good company. One or two are in the second level, but still, I can say that, I will take a step very carefully. But, yes, now this is the right time where I need to look for acquisition also.

items.statement: Three-year horizon for planning; five-year revenue target not provided due to uncertainty
items.quote: First, I will try to reach my three-year target, which I have told you that 30% sales growth, plus minus 2. And then we can sit again that, what will be the next plan for the three years. Five years is not possible, because three years is the time where things will get completely changed.

items.statement: Revised FY25 revenue growth guidance to 7%+ in constant currency from earlier 12-14% YoY
items.quote: Consequently, for the full year, we expect to grow at 7% plus in constant currency terms, versus an earlier expectation of growing between 12% and 14% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Expect mid-single digit YoY growth in Q3 FY25 accelerating to double-digit YoY growth in Q4 FY25
items.quote: And for the third quarter, that growth would be about mid-single digits on a Y-o-Y basis. And that would accelerate to double-digit growth on a Y-o-Y basis in Q4.

items.statement: Full year EBITDA margins expected at higher end of 22-24% guided range
items.quote: The margins are expected to be at the higher end of the guided range of 22% to 24% for the full year.

items.statement: Revenue visibility increased to USD 368 million from USD 350 million previous quarter
items.quote: Our visibility stood at USD 368 million. This was up from USD 350 million previous quarter.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 capex was INR 118 million
items.quote: The capex for the quarter was at INR118 million.

items.statement: Management consulting and professional services firms reduced spending more than expected; North America real estate business weak
items.quote: However, the volume is down quarter-on-quarter primarily due to lower-than-expected spending by management, consulting and professional services firms who are some of our large customers as well as lower volume in the North American real estate business.

items.statement: Expect professional services vertical to remain under pressure in Q3 FY25 with thawing in Q4
items.quote: We do expect this vertical to be under pressure for the October, November, December quarter. We expect that some of the thawing will take place. So, we'll see some sequential growth in Q4.

items.statement: Banking and life sciences leading YoY growth; tech segment starting recovery
items.quote: Banking and life sciences are leading year-on-year growth, while tech as a segment is starting to see recovery for us.

items.statement: High uncertainty persists; professional services firms cutting costs due to declining growth and partnership model margin pressure
items.quote: However, over the last few months, there has been significant cost pressure as they have seen declining growths. And given that they are run as partnerships, they want to ensure that they maintain margin and therefore, lower their variable cost and we got hit because of that.

items.statement: Added two new MTS customers (top 5 FMCG leader and top 10 energy company); renewed four contracts with one scope expansion; 100% renewal rate maintained
items.quote: During the quarter, we added two new MTS customers, one a top five FMCG leader and the second a top ten energy company. In addition, we renewed four contracts and we had one scope expansion. The company continues to maintain a track record of 100% renewals.

items.statement: Active pipeline of inorganic opportunities; M&A related expenses ongoing
items.quote: We also have an active pipeline of inorganic opportunities that we are pursuing, and we'll report more on this as we move forward with any of them.

items.statement: Effective tax rate for full year expected around 27% to 28%
items.quote: We expect the tax rate for the full year to be around 27% to 28%.

items.statement: Credit cost for FY25 may be 90-100 bps, higher than prior 80 bps guidance
items.quote: At this point in time, it looks like we may -- it may be a little higher than 80 basis points, okay, given what we are seeing. Now as a step towards that, we've done a discretionary provisioning this quarter and maybe we could see 90 basis points or even 100 basis points in the -- for the year entirely.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance for FY25 raised to 30-35% from 25% medium-term target
items.quote: Overall 30-35% I think is reasonably there for the taking in the current financial year.

items.statement: Opened 46 branches in Q2 FY25; target 80 branches for full year (50 gold, 30 mortgage)
items.quote: We opened 46 of our projected 80 branches. In Q3, there will be a marginal increase in terms of people cost for the remaining branches that we will open. And the intent is to get done with the branch opening agenda by the end of Q3.

items.statement: Cost-to-income rose to 58.6% in Q2 from 55.4% in Q1 due to branch expansion costs
items.quote: Our expenses went up by about INR18 crores quarter-on-quarter and consequently, our cost-to-income has also moved up from 55.4 in Q1 to 58.6.

items.statement: Gold loan growth driven by gold price rise and 50 new branches; co-lending partnerships expanding
items.quote: The gold loan business is in a good place. It is robust. And as soon as the new co-lending arrangements kick in, we will have the ability to press the pedal on originations, even in the slightly lower yield segment.

items.statement: Small mortgage growth to be measured; prioritizing portfolio management over disbursements
items.quote: In Q3, definitely. Because as any organization would, we continually review our practices, see what kind of borrowers are stressed and all that. And we calibrate our approach. So I can say that since we are already almost a month into Q3, there will be a marginal slowing down in this quarter.

items.statement: Additional INR22 cr ECL provision taken; gross stage 3 at 1.9%; stress seen across self-employed informal segment
items.quote: However, reflecting our view of the environment and feedback from what we see on the ground, we have taken an additional ECL provision of about INR22 crores during the quarter. So our ECL and there on the slide in the deck is up from INR122 crores to INR151 crores.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for Q3-Q4 at 100-110 bps; PCR increased 250 bps QoQ
items.quote: As of now, I think we should go with a three-digit bps number, maybe 100, 110 bps number for Q3, Q4. So we are watchful.

items.statement: Medium ticket LAP originations up 50% QoQ, 130% YoY; offsetting small ticket slowdown
items.quote: If you see our originations in the medium ticket lap, it has gone up 50% quarter-on-quarter. And the year-on-year growth in that book is 130%.

items.statement: CRISIL upgraded rating to AA+; all three agencies at AA+; 85% borrowings floating, 40% external benchmark linked
items.quote: Finally, in Q2, we received a rating upgrade from CRISIL. We are now rated AA+. It's across CRISIL, India Ratings, and CARE. All the three rating agencies, we have a AA+ rating.

items.statement: Net worth crossed INR2,400 crores; book value per share INR64.6 as of Sep 30
items.quote: Our net worth, as on September 30, crossed INR2,400 crores. We came in at INR2,402 crores. This was up from INR2,322 crores in June 24. Our book value per share as of 30th September stands at 64.6.

items.statement: Management reiterated earlier guidance and will work on it in Q3 FY25
items.quote: On the guidance piece, I have reiterated the guidance we have given earlier. We will work on this in quarter three and come back.

items.statement: Cost-income ratio expected to normalize back towards late 50s in H2 FY25
items.quote: I do believe that with this strategy, our credit cost in the second half, our cost income coming back towards late 50s that it used to be, should be things that one can expect, and we will be working towards that.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to be significantly lower in H2 FY25 as peak provisioning is behind
items.quote: Second, we will not see an elevated prov ision like we saw in the first half because what is the biggest flow-through possibility they've all flown through

items.statement: Unsecured portfolio de-growth of 7% in H1 FY25 not expected to continue in H2 FY25
items.quote: First, we will not have a drop in unsecured by 7%. This means revenues will be better, and fee income will be better.

items.statement: Added 22 branches in last one year with 16 more in pipeline for current financial year
items.quote: We added 22 new branches in the last one year. We added four new branches in the current financial year with 16 in pipeline.

items.statement: Affordable Housing and Micro LAP crossed INR 10,000 crore, now largest business segment
items.quote: Our affordable housing and Micro LAP business, which is led by Rincoo Vachha, has crossed the INR 10,000 crore mark. And affordable housing, which was just trailing the Micro LAP business, has become our largest business on the bank.

items.statement: Supply chain finance grew from INR 378 crore to INR 597 crore with significant runway for growth
items.quote: Supply chain has gone from a INR 378 crore to INR 597 crore business. And again, the reason why this business does well is not just because of demand. It is also because as we get new customers and add new geographies, we have barely started the business early last year.

items.statement: CGTMSE guaranteed book targeted to reach INR 800-1,000 crore by March 2025 from INR 120 crore currently
items.quote: We currently have a book of INR 120 crore. By March end, we should be looking at INR 800 crore to INR 1,000 crore of books, which will be completely under guarantee program.

items.statement: MFI collection efficiency stable at 98.5%-98.7% in Q2 FY25, similar to Q1 FY25
items.quote: So, we are ranging between 98.5% to 98.7%. Manish Ostwal: Was this quarter one, sir? Management: Quarter one was around 98.6 % to 98.7%. So, it's always between the range of 0.2 basis point here and there. It's always ranged between 98.2% to 98

items.statement: Tightened MFI exposure limits: off-us exposure capped at INR 50,000, total unsecured exposure at INR 1.25 lakh for all customers
items.quote: One thing what we've implemented now is the exposure off us for any customer, whether it's existing to Jana or new to Jana, it cannot be more than INR 50,000. Total exposure for a new-to-bank customer cannot exceed INR 1.25 lakhs, it was initially INR 1.5 lakhs, and for existing, it was INR 2 lakhs, both have gone down to INR 1.25 lakhs.

items.statement: Secured PCR increased to 29.7% from 18% in March 2024, overall PCR at 67.2%
items.quote: We've grown it to 29.7%. Unsecured also has shown an increase in PCR. The third piece is on the BC book. While we are covered 93.4% in terms of PCR, there is also a service guarantee which we haven't really considered in all of this.

items.statement: Expecting new refinance sanctions from two institutions in October-November 2024 at competitive rates
items.quote: We are expecting new sanctions and borrowing limits during this quarter. Probably it will come in end of October or early November from refinance institutions. So that is expected during this month or the early next month, which is at a competitive rate to deposits.

items.statement: Reduced fixed deposit rates in July 2024 and savings bank rates in October 2024 to lower cost of deposits
items.quote: In the month of July, we brought down our fixed deposit rates. And similarly, in the month of October, we brought down our saving bank rates, which will help us to bring down the cost of deposits further.

items.statement: Borrowing costs expected to be lower from Q3 FY25 due to better refinance pricing
items.quote: All I can tell you is that the borrowing costs from next quarter will be lower than what it is this half, purely because we expect better pricing.

items.statement: Secured business grew 16% in H1 FY25 and expected to continue same solid growth in H2 FY25
items.quote: Our secure business, as I mentioned earlier, has grown a 16% clip in the first half alone, and that will continue to see the same solid growth that we've seen in the first half.

items.statement: Net credit cost for H1 FY25 at 1.9% after adjusting for INR 115 crore accelerated provisioning and recoveries
items.quote: If I adjust that and the recoveries, my recoveries which is reflected in the other income line, my net credit cost is INR 247 crore for the half year, which is at about 1.9%.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance of 20% maintained for FY25
items.quote: Among the guidance things, AUM growth of 20%, I think is not a risk. It is something that I do think we will hit in second half.

items.statement: Net NPA target below 1% for every quarter going forward
items.quote: I would always expect Jana to have net NPA below 1%. That will be our going in position for every other quarter after this.

items.statement: Secured book gross NPA expected to remain steady or improve by 20 bps in H2
items.quote: That's what I was trying to say, Rajiv, because we ha ve some backlog to clear. We are fully focused on it and at least our sense is that from here it should remain steady at best get 20 bps better on gross NPA

items.statement: Credit cost expected to be lower in Q3 vs Q2
items.quote: So fair to say that yes, Q3 will be lower credit cost for sure from Q2.

items.statement: Unsecured book growth expected to turn positive in H2 after -7% in H1
items.quote: Now if we make sure our unsecured is at 0% growth. I'm just being conservative, I'm not saying it will be zero and secured growth by 16%. I think we will be closer to the number you would anticipate.

items.statement: BC book reduced from INR 2,500 crore in March to INR 1,950 crore currently
items.quote: And I'll just tell you the peak number roughly was INR 2,500 crore of BC book in March. It is down to INR 1,950 crore.

items.statement: Secured portfolio yield at 13.41% across Home Loan, Micro LAP and MSME
items.quote: If you take my MSME, Home Loan and Micro LAP book, the yield is 13.41% between the three.

items.statement: Unsecured portfolio yield at ~19.99% (microfinance minus BC payout)
items.quote: And I mentioned earlier the yield on the unsecured book which is largely microfinance minus the payout to BCs because they have a portion of the revenue is roughly about 19.99%.

items.statement: Cost of funds at 8.1% due to high LCR of 261% vs peer average of 130%
items.quote: Yes, so good point. Yes, I think it is higher than our peers. And the reason it is high is because our LCR is at 261%. And that is also higher than our peers. Industry average is 130%.

items.statement: LCR to be reduced slowly over next 6 months as deposit growth environment eases
items.quote: Would we like to reduce our LCR and hence our costs? Slowly over the next 6 months as the situation eases, we will do it.

items.statement: First 21 days of October show encouraging unsecured disbursement response
items.quote: I must tell you that in the first 21 days in October, it looks encouraging. So, we'll certainly have a look at that.

items.statement: Only 1 of 17 BC partners expected to exceed service guarantee; others committed to recovery
items.quote: We do not see us being out of pocket with any BC except one. Second, very importantly, is all BCs are committed to getting recovery behind them.

items.statement: No rub-off from MFI stress to secured book; common customer base not large
items.quote: We are not seeing any microfinance rub off on our book. So I'm saying this very simply because there is no connectivity we can see, and we are not feeling any challenge coming from a MFI behavior into any of our secured books.

items.statement: FY25 presales guidance maintained at INR 7,000-8,000 crores despite launch delays
items.quote: Yes. So if you're going to put all questions, then it's fine, but if we wanted to answer that, yes, we are still going by that guidance.

items.statement: Annual sales target of INR 10,000 crores in 3 years reaffirmed
items.quote: Yes, yes. So we stand by that.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 bookings of INR 1,412 crores and collections of INR 644 crores
items.quote: For the quarter under review, we achieved booking worth INR1,412 crores for our already launched projects and strong collections of INR644 crores from all projects during the quarter.

items.statement: Acquired 10 acres in Worli with GDV INR 14,000 crores and 5 acres in Gurugram with GDV INR 1,400 crores in Q2 FY25
items.quote: We also made two major acquisitions during the quarter, where we acquired ownership rights of 10 acres of land parcel in Worli, with a GDV of INR14,000 crores. And we also acquired 5 acres of land parcel in Gurugram, NCR with GDV of INR1,400 crores.

items.statement: Real estate project-level EBITDA margin at 30%
items.quote: Yes. Our project margin has been about 30%.

items.statement: Paper business EBITDA decreased 22% YoY and 10% QoQ due to lower NSR and rising input costs
items.quote: Sales volume in Q2 '25 increased by 7% Y -o-Y and 9% Q -o-Q; however, EBITDA decreased by 22% Y-o-Y and 10% Q-on-Q due to lower NSR, rising input cost pressure from increasing wood and imported pulp costs, thus constraining profitability.

items.statement: Paper prices down 4% YoY, wood and imported pulp costs rising, pricing pressure expected to continue
items.quote: In Q2 financial year '25, the paper, board and tissue prices continued their downward trajectory with average net sales realization down by 4% year-on-year and were almost at par with previous quarter.

items.statement: Real estate demand robust across Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities, inventory at all-time low, strong outlook for 3-4 years
items.quote: Inventory levels are still pretty low. Number of players are less, supply is less, comparatively less. Supply has increased in some markets, definitely. But still, I see there is a very good leeway for strong branded, trusted brands, players, etcetera, to have a good run for at least the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: H2 FY25 launches: Wellesley Road (INR 1,050 cr), Sarjapur (INR 2,700 cr), Trimaya phase (INR 700 cr), Navya phase (INR 1,400 cr), Hindalco phase 1 (INR 1,800 cr)
items.quote: So Wellesley Road, which we're planning this quarter is about INR 1,050 crores. Sarjapur is going to be a very big launch in Bangalore, in Q4, is about INR 2,700 crores. And Hindalco launch, which we are planning in March of Q4, that is expected to be a

items.statement: Paper business not expected to generate cash flow in FY25, profits may not reach 50% of last year
items.quote: I don't think we expect to generate any cash flow this year because half year is gone. And there has not been a significant inflow of cash from the paper business. The outlook does not look very good, but we hope that it will be better in the second half, but we don't expect profits to probably reach even 50% of what we did last year.

items.statement: Potential contractor and skilled labour shortage if real estate and infrastructure demand continues growing
items.quote: Because the kind of demand, which we expect both in real estate and in infrastructure construction, the availability of good contractors could be an issue and further downstream, the availability of skilled labour could be an issue.

items.statement: International sales contributing 20-25% of bookings from Dubai, Singapore, Middle East, US, UK
items.quote: Yes, as of now, we are seeing about 20%, 25% of these bookings coming from international markets.

items.statement: Standalone net debt INR 3,000 crores, comfortable with debt-equity ratio around 1x, can borrow up to INR 5,000 crores if needed
items.quote: Our net debt on a stand-alone basis is right now INR 3,000 crores. So we can easily -- if required set ourselves to INR 5,000 crores if required on a stand-alone basis, maybe we will be slightly above the 1, but of course, see that we are spending it on some good acquisitions.

items.statement: Niyaara Phase 3 (Tower C) launch planned for next financial year, Worli 10-acre acquisition at least 1 phase launch next year
items.quote: What we are planning is that we would definitely be aiming to launch Tower C, which is the last phase of Niyaara, next financial year. Simultaneously, we're also thinking of launching this this newly acquired asset of 10 acres, at least 1 phase of that.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15% for FY25 reiterated
items.quote: This year, we have a whole revenue growth of 15%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 23-25% for FY25 maintained
items.quote: we maintain at 23% to 25% what guidance we have already given for the current financial year

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 800 crores for FY25 maintained
items.quote: we are expecting a total capex of INR 800 crores in the current financial year

items.quote: we are confident minimum 15 % growth guaranteed for us in next five years. We have made already for next five years o ur internal plan which at appropriate point of time we may share with you also

items.quote: it is the composition of product mix during the first hal f which has given us this margin of 45%. Overall, during the current year, we expect to have the gross margin of 42% only as we have given the guidance

items.statement: H2 FY25 execution plan: LRSAM INR 1,600+ cr, Himshakti EW INR 800-900 cr, Instrumented EW Range INR 750 cr, Akash Army INR 500 cr, D-29 EW INR 500 cr, Weapon Locating Radar INR 450 cr

items.quote: major challenges whic h we had seen earlier about LRSAM and other those big - ticket items already streamlined. So, we are not facing any challenge. Some other small items which are not affecting our turnover that much

items.statement: Expects to reach INR 10,000 crores revenue in 3 years' time frame
items.quote: In 3 years' time frame, we should reach to something like INR 10,000 crores of revenue. I quite believe that we should be able to do that.

items.statement: Total order book stands at ~INR 6151 crores as on Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our total order book now stands at ~ INR 6151 crores as on Q2 of FY25.

items.quote: We expect the fiber market to revive from the first quarter of the fiscal 2025-26. We are seeing signs of recovery as more tenders and enquiries are coming up.

items.quote: So capex, which we have planned everything stands tied up by way of equity, debt and internal accruals. So our debt equity ratio is likely to remain in this range of 0.25 to 0.30.

items.statement: Expects telecom products revenue of ~INR 2000 crores for FY25; current order book for telecom products ~INR 800-900 crores

items.quote: Fiber Optic Cable business, the current capacity utilisation is about 45%, and which we expect to improve from the next quarter, as I said.

items.statement: Expects INR 5000-8000 crores opportunity for HFCL from BharatNet Phase III (total project ~INR 65000 crores)
items.quote: So, as I have said, we are more or less expecting somewhere between INR 5,000 to INR8,000 crores, that is my best estimate at this point of time.

items.statement: Targets up to 70% of optic fiber segment revenue from international markets in next 3 years; 40-50% of telecom segment revenue to be export-driven in next 3 years
items.quote: We are targeting a significant increase in export revenue from our optic fiber segment, aiming for up to 70% of revenue to come from international markets in next three years. Additionally, we plan for 40-50% of our telecom segment revenue to be export -driven within the next three years.

items.statement: Defence revenue expected to start from next year (FY26) as electronic fuzes and other products complete trials
items.quote: Yes. These are under trial at the moment. And I sincerely believe that from the nex t year onwards, this revenue would start coming

items.statement: O&M revenue currently ~INR 80-100 crores/year; expected to grow to INR 300-400 crores from FY27/FY28
items.quote: But from year FY'27, it will go to INR300 crores to INR400 crores.

items.statement: Full-year volume growth guided at 3% to 4% YoY
items.quote: We have said. We repeat that full year growth guidance we have said in terms of volumes, we said 3% to 4%, and we have given just now as you heard our EBITDA also we have given

items.statement: H2 volume growth guided at 7% to 8% YoY
items.quote: H2 volumes we have looked at second half about Y-on-Y basis 7% to 8% and that's how we stick and for entire year, we are looking at about 4%, thereabouts plus or minus, and that's what we think is realistic at the moment to assume.

items.statement: H2 EBITDA per ton increase guided at Rs 150-170 over H1
items.quote: In terms of EBITDA, we are again looking at between the first half to second half. We have projected about between Rs. 150 to Rs. 170 upswing in the EBITDA format, and that is how we see it translating.

items.statement: Full-year capex revised down to within Rs 700 crore
items.quote: CAPEX for the whole year, we expect to go about within 700 crores.

items.statement: Kundanganj Line 3 on track for commissioning next year; Prayagraj project not yet commenced
items.quote: Our progress of our Kundanganj's third line is going on satisfactorily and on track, and we hope when that comes in next year, we will have some of the incentives which we lost because of Kundanganj incentive getting expired last March will get restored.

items.statement: Project Unnati and Shikhar together expected to deliver Rs 70/ton efficiency gain in H2
items.quote: For these two projects, in the second half, we are expecting efficiency of around Rs. 70 a ton, for Unnati and Shikhar, taken together.

items.statement: Bikram coal block cost expected at Rs 1.10/1000 kcal vs current central region fuel cost of Rs 1.40-1.50/1000 kcal
items.quote: Our cost from Bikram coal block is expected to be around Rs. 1.10 paisa per 1,000 kilo cal, and the ongoing rate for fuel in the central region is between 140 and 150.

items.statement: No significant price improvement seen post-August; further decline unlikely after festivals and harvest
items.quote: I don't think there is any significant improvement, Mangesh. This is based more or less terms. One has not really seen any consistent improvement or improvement which sticks. And I Birla Corporation October 24, 2024 personally don't expect to see any very significant changes between now and at least till mid

items.statement: Maharashtra election impact on demand and pricing expected to last until at least January
items.quote: In the West, especially Maharashtra, we are being circumspect because of the elections which have been announced and that impact will continue for about a month at least and whichever government comes in, by the time they settle in, new funds are sanctioned, etc., I think we will get into at least January there.

items.statement: Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj will disrupt logistics and eat into peak season Jan-Feb
items.quote: In our core market, we are also factoring in the Maha Kumbh, which is going to happen in Prayagraj. That is once in a 12-year event, as you know, and that entire area, the logistics get Birla Corporation October 24, 2024 impacted. So that will also be something which will eat in to the peak season period of January, February, which is usually there

items.statement: Net debt expected to close around Rs 3,000 crore; no plan to sell strategic investments to reduce debt
items.quote: So, debt level, we expect to close around 3,000. Net debt, we expect to close around 3,000 crores.

items.statement: Incentive receivables (ex-West Bengal) at Rs 450 crore; West Bengal disputed amount Rs 140 crore now cleared by Supreme Court
items.quote: Total, if you were to say what is the receivable on account of incentives from various governments as on date, it is 450 crore. Aditya Saraogi: Excluding West Bengal. Sandip Ghose: Excluding West Bengal, where we have an additional amount, which was under, which was sub judice because the government had contested it. And that contest has been disposed off by the Supreme Court

items.statement: Premium mix at 61% in Q2, up from 51%, driven by strategic focus on higher-return segments amid weak value segment pricing
items.quote: If today the prices have come down and if I am selling below capacity for whatever reason I can't participate, I would focus which is giving me the maximum return. So, it is a combination of product mix and geo mix.

items.statement: Mukutban Q2 volume 5 lakh tons at 340 km lead; full-year incentive guidance Rs 100 crore
items.quote: We have guided for total incentive of about 100 crores for the whole year. We are standing by that guidance, okay?

items.statement: Bikram coal mine commercial production expected from Q1 FY26; Sial Ghoghri already producing 2.5-3 lakh tons/year
items.quote: Captive coal mines as already we had informed for the Bikram, already Sial Ghoghri is in operation for which we do around 2.5 to 3 lakhs tons per annum and for Bikram Coal Mines, we are going to start the first coal production going to start from the Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Market volume growth remained muted; urban growth moderated since MAT June while rural growth turned accretive but gradual.
items.quote: Market volume growth trajectory remained muted in this quarter. At an MAT level, total FMCG volume growth has slowed down slightly in recent months. Since MAT June, urban growth has moderated. While rural growth has become accretive to total growth , its pace of recovery has been gradual though.

items.statement: Crude palm oil and tea saw 10% and 25% YoY inflation; management believes increases are persistent and is taking calibrated price hikes.
items.quote: Following a prolonged period of benign commodity prices in this quarter, crude palm oil and tea experienced inflation of 10% and 25% year -on-year, September Quarter 2024 Earnings call of Hindustan Unilever Limited respectively. Given our assessment, that this price increase is here to stay, we are now taking calibrated price

items.statement: Home Care and Beauty & Wellbeing delivered high single-digit growth; Personal Care declined 5%; Foods & Refreshment revenue declined marginally.
items.quote: 2 of our segments: Home Care and Beauty & Wellbeing delivered high single -digit growth. These 2 segments put together constitute circa 60 percentage of our total business. While Personal Care is seeing a sequential increase in turnover, it will take a couple of quarters for the actions put in place to reflect in numbers. Performance in Foods & Refreshment has been subdued due to continued downgra

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of INR19/share and special dividend of INR10/share, total payout INR6,814 crores.
items.quote: I'm very pleased to announce that the Board has approved an interim dividend of INR19 per share, along with a special dividend of INR10 per share. Together, this will mean a total payout of INR6,814 crores.

items.statement: MAT business winning crossed 60% in September, ahead of December target; gaining market shares in last 3 months per Nielsen.
items.quote: I'm very pleased to report that our MAT business winning number has already crossed 60% in September, ahead of our earlier estimate of December '24. September Quarter 2024 Earnings call of Hindustan Unilever Limited We are also now gaining market shares in the last three months as per the latest Nielsen

items.statement: 75% of brands gaining or maintaining brand power; value weighted distribution >95%.
items.quote: At present, circa 75% of our brands are either gaining or maintaining brand power and our value weighted distribution continues to be more than 95%.

items.statement: Full year effective tax rate after PPA expected marginally above 26%.
items.quote: Effective tax rate after PPA for the first half was 26.1%, and we expect our full year ETR to be marginally above 26%.

items.statement: Applied for more than 20 patents covering design, material, and formulation for the new Stratos soap formulation developed over 5 years.
items.quote: Yes, we have applied for more than 20 patents, and these are all kind of patents, design patents, material patents, of course, formulation.

items.statement: Superior formulation enhances pricing power and reduces exposure to commodity volatility, particularly palm oil.
items.quote: And as far as margins are concerned, probably the question behind your question. And ultimately, if the products are superior, our ability to command a right price point gets more enhanced.

items.statement: Initial trends for Stratos soap are encouraging with sequential volume growth in September quarter and early signs of volume market share improvement.
items.quote: Initial trends are good. Sequentially, we sold more in September quarter compared to what we sold in June quarter. There is initial early signs of volume market share improving.

items.statement: Near-term demand trends are stable going into the current quarter; urban weakness is broad-based across the country.
items.quote: What we can say with some degree of certainty is near term that demand trends tend we feel are stable going into the quarter we are in.

items.statement: Tea commodity inflation is running at 25%; price increases started in December quarter and will be calibrated over the quarter.
items.quote: 25% is the scale of tea commodity inflation, which has happened. So going forward, of course, we'll end up taking price increases, which we have done, started taking price increases in December quarter.

items.statement: Price increases in tea will be taken in smaller calibrated chunks net of savings, similar to the approach for Skin Cleansing.
items.quote: Our learning always has been when you take price increases tak e in smaller chunks. And when you drop prices drop in larger chunks, so that you don't end up getting saddled with trade pipe line

items.statement: Tea volumes impacted by continued downgradation during deflationary period; expecting stabilization as price increases take effect.
items.quote: And the reason we called out that the downgradation which has happened for Tea in the deflationary period has continued to happen.

items.statement: HFD focus is on driving consumption and premiumization; Plus range performing well with 250 bps corporate market share gain and 700 bps penetration improvement since acquisition.
items.quote: Since we acquired the business, 250 bps improvement in corporate market share of nutrition drink. Since we acquired the business, 700 bps improvement in penetration levels.

items.statement: Urban growth weakness is across the country, not concentrated in specific regions; secular shift toward organized trade continues.
items.quote: Overall in terms of urban, it's across the country. It's not that there's a dramatic difference in one part of the country as compared to the other part of the country.

items.statement: Channel mix: ~70% General Trade, ~20% Modern Trade, 6-7% E-commerce, 3% other channels; gaining share in organized trade.
items.quote: We still are GT-dominant business. 70% of our business comes from general trade, roughly 20 percentage comes from modern trade, 6% to 7% from e-commerce and 3-odd percentage from other channels.

items.statement: Organized trade delivers better margins than General Trade due to different portfolio mix (less mass/sachet presence).
items.quote: Typically, organized trade, you end up making better margins compared to general trade and that emanates from the fact that the portfolio that you sell in organized trade is different than what we sell in general trade.

items.statement: A&P spend was ~9.5% of sales in the quarter, ~100 bps below the typical ~10.5% run-rate, driven by competitive phasing, reach objectives, and innovation timing.
items.quote: are roughly little September Quarter 2024 Earnings call of Hindustan Unilever Limited over 9.5% A&P spends in the quarter. And if you look at our average for last year, typically 10.5% what we do. So we have, let me say, 100 bps lower compared to a typical trend of spends in this quarter

items.statement: Quick commerce is a small part of e-commerce (~6-7% of total business); ice cream is >10% of quick commerce sales; market shares in quick commerce mirror general trade shares.
items.quote: So in Q-commerce, ice cream is roughly more than 10 percentage.

items.statement: Beauty & Wellbeing growing ~7%; premium portfolio (Ponds, Simple, Love Beauty & Planet) ~INR 2,000 crores growing high double-digits with 60%+ organized/e-com contribution; mass skin care (Glow & Lovely) still needs work.
items.quote: This entire portfolio is already about the scale of almost INR2,000 crores and is growing in very high double digits, has a very high e-commerce and modern trade contribution almost 60- odd percent.

items.statement: OZiva (majority stake) and Wellbeing Nutrition (minority stake) performing well; OZiva full acquisition expected by end of next calendar year per 3-year agreement.
items.quote: With OZiva, we already have our very clear contract in place as that at the end of 3- year period with an agreed pre-formula will end up acquiring the balance business that will happen by the end of next year, end of next calendar year.

items.statement: Tea and Skin Cleansing are highly price-elastic categories; no pantry loading observed ahead of price hikes; industry stock levels stable.
items.quote: Typically, Jay, there are a couple of categories which are more sensitive to price in FMCG, Tea and Soaps (Skin Cleansing), are those categories which are very sensitive to price change.

items.statement: Guiding for 12-14% organic top-line growth over the medium term
items.quote: clearly the 12% to 14% guidance that we have given is the pure organic growth

items.statement: Expecting full-year organic growth higher than 12-14% due to weak prior-year base
items.quote: this year, the organic growth will be higher than 14%, simply because last year's second half was terrible for us

items.statement: Guiding for 22%+ EBITDA margin for FY25, up from earlier 20%+
items.quote: Earlier, we were talking about 20% plus. Now, we are confident of 22% plus for sure

items.statement: Targeting 100-150 bps EBITDA margin expansion year-on-year over next three years
items.quote: delivering a 100 bps to 150 bps, if not more, margin expansion year on year over the next three years

items.statement: Peak EBITDA margin potential seen at 30%+ within three years as scale improves
items.quote: I believe in 3 years, we should be closer to 30%, if not breaching the mark

items.statement: Asset-light model with full manufacturing outsourcing; no capex needed for operations
items.quote: Our model is such that we actually do not require investments by itself in the business

items.statement: Cash balance of Rs 93.4 crore as of Sep 30; all cash generation earmarked for inorganic acquisitions
items.quote: all of this cash and whatever we generate even going forward will be used for inorganic strategies only

items.statement: Acquired Yash Pharma India/Bhutan business for Rs 94 crore; business did Rs 48 crore sales at ~12% margin
items.quote: We paid INR94 crores to acquire

items.statement: H1 FY25 sales mix: 50% gynaecology, 20% orthopaedics, rest split between dermatology and paediatrics
items.quote: 50% of our sales would be in the space of gyna ecology. Another 20% odd will be in ortho and between Derma and Pedia would be the rest of the sales splitting almost equally

items.statement: Core business grew 5% YoY in Q2 after declining in H2 FY24 due to dydrogesterone competition and Indomethacin spurious products
items.quote: our core business is also back on track with growth of 5% over q2 last year

items.statement: Gross margins ~65%+; margin expansion driven by operating leverage on fixed field-force costs as sales grow 12-14%
items.quote: Our gross margins in the business are fairly decent at about 65%, if not more. And therefore, our growth in sales, which is where we are guiding towards 12 % to 14%, will certainly lead to margin expansion

items.statement: MR attrition 20-30%; field-force productivity at 2.8 lakh/month vs industry 5-10 lakh; targeting 4-4.5 lakh in 3 years
items.quote: getting it to 4 to 4.5 lakhs range in next 3 years is what is feasible

items.statement: Stock split approved: face value from Rs 5 to Rs 2 to improve liquidity
items.quote: the Board at their meeting held on 23 Oct 24, have approved a stock split to change the face value of our equity shares from Rs. 5/ - to Rs. 2/-

items.statement: Two-pronged inorganic strategy: brand acquisitions in existing therapies or business acquisitions with field force for new sub-chronic therapies
items.quote: Brands within the therapies we are in or businesses with field force if we were to get into additional therapies. But our therapy choice will be sub-chronic

items.statement: New product MemUp (menopause HRT) launched; concept-building product with insignificant current sales but large addressable population
items.quote: MemUp is the first hormone replacement therapy product or the first product in the country to deal with menopause

items.statement: Not in CDMO business; pure domestic sales & marketing; use CMOs/CDMOs only for own product development
items.quote: we are not in CDMO business at all , we are a pure domestic pharmaceutical sales and marketing organization

items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stands at 313 million compared to 488 million in Q3 2023. And for June quarter, June 2024 quarter, it was at 383 million.

items.statement: Margins pressured by raw material inflation, adverse customer and product mix, supply chain constraints, and geopolitical disruptions
items.quote: There has been pressure on margins due to a host of reasons, which includes raw material inflation, supply chain constraints and sales and product mix to name a few.

items.statement: BOPP and polyester prices rose 10-15%, forming a sizable chunk of raw material basket; full pass-through not achieved in same quarter
items.quote: I mean if you look at, there is an increase of almost 10% to 15% for these 2 products.

items.statement: FMCG demand subdued; rural recovering but urban under strain; inflationary pressures impacting consumer spending across segments
items.quote: In our overall ecosystem of FMCG sector from where we get most of our demand, inflationary pressures had impacted the demand across most of the segments, affecting the consumer spending.

items.statement: blueloop contribution steady at 27-28% of sales; new product adoption slower than expected due to customer qualification delays and sustainability pledge timing
items.quote: as our CFO explained during his remarks that the blueloop contribution continued to be around 27%, 28%.

items.statement: Investing in operations and technology across manufacturing processes for blueloop; new plant commissioned for backward integration
items.quote: we have been investing in the operations and technology, where you can see that there is a clear impact in terms of investments.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis disrupting supply chains, vessel availability, and freight costs; geopolitical issues impacting export and raw material import costs
items.quote: Global supply chain disruptions emanating from geopolitical issues are also having an impact on the export as well as having an impact on import of certain raw material in the cost.

items.statement: Freight cost impact estimated at INR25-30 million for the quarter; impairment of INR4.5 crore on fixed assets (non-recurring)
items.quote: I'll say that maybe at least the impact would be in the range of around INR25 million to INR30 million for this quarter.

items.statement: ECB of INR1 billion repaid in Q3; only remaining debt is ECB of INR1 billion; debt-to-equity 0.1; surplus cash in term deposits and mutual funds yielding 7%+
items.quote: During the quarter ended September '24 we have repaid ECB of INR1 billion. And with that, the only debt we have in our portfolio of ECB 1 billion.

items.statement: No specific revenue or volume growth guidance given for CY2026; growth aspirations aligned with Huhtamaki Oyj directional figures and India country growth
items.quote: I don't think we give a guidance on the sales growth also for the future.

items.statement: Non-core asset disposals completed: Ambernath and Thane land parcels sold last year; no further assets held for sale
items.quote: I think we are done all. So, there were 2 land parcels, which we have done the deal in the last year. One was for Ambernath and one for Thane.

items.statement: Competitive intensity high due to excess capacity and weak demand; price recovery limited by market dynamics and contract timing
items.quote: when you look at the demand and supply situation, definitely, there is a capacity in the market and demand is not growing. In that context, we have seen even the third quarter, demand is not coming from other market, and also there -- definitely there is a pressure and the competitive situation is really, really becoming more aggressive.

items.statement: Food and daily essentials packaging is core focus; mix skewed toward food where FMCG challenges are most pronounced
items.quote: By the way, if you need to -- then if you see Huhtamaki, we call ourselves as a food company - - food packaging company, so you can then... Saurabh Patwa: Okay, understood sir. Dhananjay Salunkhe: Food and daily essentials, okay, food and daily essentials. So essentially, that's the focus area

items.statement: No plans for BOPP backward integration; R&D and investment focused on PE and paper-based sustainable structures
items.quote: Coming to the backward integration on PP, no, we do not have any plans on that. So, we want to invest in our focus, our R&D efforts and the investments on the PE and paper.

items.statement: Operational excellence mitigating cost inflation (electricity, fuel, salaries) but benefits masked by flat volumes and adverse mix; leverage expected when sales grow
items.quote: today, if you see whatever improvements which we are doing are able to take care of the inflationary trends in terms of electricity, in terms of fuel, in terms of the annual salary increases and so on, which are basically significant, right?

items.statement: Export realizations not directly comparable to domestic due to different product requirements; domestic competitive pressures expected to persist near-term
items.quote: Again, Akshay, it's very difficult to comment because we cannot compare apple to oranges. There are different requirements for different businesses.

items.statement: AUM growth expected 11-12% by end of Q3 FY25 and 13-14% by end of FY25
items.quote: Going forward we expect that by the end of the third quarter this AUM growth should be in between 11% to 12% and then going forward by end of fourth qua rter it should be around 13 %-14% or we will try to at least cross that

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 10-12 bps for FY25 and FY26
items.quote: But however, we are sticking to the same guidance in terms of 10 to 12 bps in terms of our credit cost.

items.statement: Spread guidance maintained at +2.5% and NIM at +3.5%
items.quote: So, that also should help us in the third quarter and so we don't expect any deterioration in the spread and we continue to have the same guidance of (+2.5%) spread and (+3.5%) NIM.

items.statement: AUM growth target of 15-17% for FY26
items.quote: And growth, for next year I think we would continue to have about 15% to 17% is what we would aim in terms of the AUM growth.

items.statement: Major IT transformation project estimated CAPEX 250-350 crores over 7 years, contract award by Dec 2024
items.quote: But yes, if you look at the simple IT costs have gone up. So, we are not sure whether it will be in the range of around 300 crores instead of 250 crore s or it would be around 350

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected 16-16.5% till new IT system implemented, then 17-18%
items.quote: So, this is one time cost, and we expect that the cost to income ratio should be in the nature of 16%-16.5% till the time the new IT system is there. Otherwise, it should be in the range of 17% to 18%

items.statement: Self-employed share increased to 35-38% of incremental lending, target 65-35 salaried/self-employed mix in 2-3 years
items.quote: Yes, actually we had about 72% salaried and 28% self-employed. But incrementally it is right now around 35% or that about 35 38% is coming to self-employed. But on the overall mix, we are still closer to the same 70-30 or thereabouts only. We are open to go up to 65% in the salaried and 35% in the self-employed.

items.statement: LAP share currently 5%, target up to 7% of portfolio
items.quote: For LAP right now we are around 5%. We would be okay going up to about 7% because eventually in terms of our excluding, after eliminating the CRE portion of the housing portfolio also, the pure housing we would like to kind of keep it up to around 70%.

items.statement: Disbursement growth 28% QoQ and 18% YoY in Q2 FY25, first half disbursements ~4,500 crores
items.quote: in terms of disbursem ent, we have had a good quarter. There's been a good satisfactory improvement in terms of the disbursement growth over Q1. In terms of compared to Q1, there's a growth of 28% and compared to Q2 of last year there's a 18% growth in the disbursements

items.statement: Telangana disbursements stable but negative growth due to demolition issues and registration problems
items.quote: So, only Telangana, we are having a bit of a problem, and we are going a little slow because of the same issues of registration and there are some incidents regarding demolitions and all of unauthorized properties because of which the sentiment is a little low.

items.statement: SMA-1 and SMA-2 increased by ~102 crores, focus on reduction in Q3 FY25
items.quote: But yes, about 102 crores approximately increase in our SMA-1 plus SMA-2 which is what we need to work on in this quarter. So, this third quarter we will definitely be focusing on bringing this down.

items.statement: NHB refinance sanction received at lower cost than bank borrowings, to be used for incremental portfolio creation
items.quote: Another aspect which has recently happened is that we have also got a sanction from NHB for a refinance sanction which will be at a cost lower than what we are borrowing from banks and NCD and everything.

items.statement: Branch expansion of 15 branches in FY25, targeting 300 branches by FY28
items.quote: In terms of our branch expansion, we are planning for 15 additional branches in this financial year, and this would be mostly in the north and western geographies.

items.statement: Building direct sales channel, target 20% of business from own sales force by FY27 (currently 80% sourced externally)
items.quote: In the long run we expect about 20% of the business to come through this sales channel and our sourcing should come down from the present 80% to about 60%. That's the breakup. 60-40 is our goal which we expect to achieve in the next 2 years by FY27.

items.statement: 45% of bank term loans repo-linked, 35% MCLR-linked; 25 bps repo cut translates to ~10 bps liability cost reduction
items.quote: Last quarter we had a 40-40 breakup of bank term loans linked to repo and MCLR. We have had some MCLR linked loans. We have either reprice or we have repaid and that is why now and moved to repo linked loans. So, we have about 45% of our bank term loans which are linked to repo, 35% linked to MCLR and the balance we have T-bills and all those things.

items.statement: IT upgrade Phase 1 (LOS-LMS) going live in Q3 FY25, cost ~3 crores/quarter already factored in
items.quote: We have a present L OS-LMS package which we are upgrading. That is the first phase of our technology transfer that we are doing it. So, that is something which we have already implemented in the sens e that it is already tested. The UAT has been completed. Our parallel run across branches has also been completed. So, that is going to be implemented now

items.statement: Target 4% ROA on steady-state basis as exit FY26
items.quote: Our target is off to get to a 4% of ROA on a steady state basis as we exit FY 26 is a sequential target.

items.statement: Project 150 bps yield increase from micro enterprise mix shift to 30%+ AUM in 6 quarters
items.quote: So when you look at 6 quarters down the line, we would be at about 400 micro enterprises branches and the contribution of the AUM would be upwards of 30%, thereby a complete product and a product mix change at the AUM level delivering 150 basis points incr emental yield

items.statement: Expect cost of borrowing to reduce 75 bps over next 6-10 quarters
items.quote: We have projected that we'll have a total cost of borrowing reduction of 75 basis points.

items.statement: Credit costs to peak and stabilize around 2% by end of FY26
items.quote: our models tell us is that our credit costs will peak and then gets stabilized at around 2% by end of next year

items.statement: Plan 250 micro enterprise branches by end FY25 and 400 by end FY26
items.quote: Our target of 250 locations by end of this year and 400 locations by end of next year looks possible.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 loan origination INR1,917 crores, highest ever
items.quote: Our last quarter was a quarter wherein, we did the lifetime highest loan origination of INR1,917 crores and vis-a-vis our first quarter, obviously, there was a massive and significant jump.

items.statement: Micro enterprise disbursement INR456 crores in Q2 FY25 vs INR209 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: And that's why in this quarter, we delivered INR456 crores vis -a-vis INR209 crores from our micro enterprise channel, which is that we were able to double the volume or more than double the volume in just 1 quarter.

items.statement: Co-lending volume INR650 crores in Q2 FY25, highest ever
items.quote: And that's why we have highest ever co -lending volume in the last quarter, which was INR650-odd crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 PAT INR35.5 crores, 17% QoQ growth
items.quote: Overall, the PAT is INR35.5 crores vis-à-vis INR28.9 crores in Q2FY24 and INR30.4 crores in the Q1FY25. So, there is a 17% QoQ growt h on PAT as well.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved to 53% in Q2 FY25 despite 46 new branches
items.quote: If you look at this quarter's data, this is 53% , probably you may look at it as 1% saving on the previous quarter, however you have to take into account that we have opened 46 branches, micro branches during this quarter.

items.statement: Cost of funds may rise 5 bps for 2-3 months then decline from Q1 FY26
items.quote: We think that it may still go up by about 5 basis points for the next 2, 3 months, and then it will start settling down. And then from Q1, definitely, it should go down.

items.statement: Exit run rate in September upwards of INR700 crores monthly disbursement
items.quote: Our exit run rates in September were upwards of INR700 crores, which means that the next quarters will see higher than those run rates and therefore this is the new base level for us.

items.statement: Micro enterprise AUM contribution 11% end Q2 FY25, targeting 30%+ in 6 quarters
items.quote: The jump in micro enterprises business, the contribution of the business going to about 11% of the total disbursement this quarter rather than -- 11% of the AUM at the end of this quarter to reach to the 150 basis points incremental yield, we -- our micro enterprise business, which is coming from 210 branches today, will start really accelerating with another 50 branches coming up during this year

items.statement: Supply chain book wound down from INR722 crores peak to INR355 crores, INR35 crores GNPA, no further stress expected
