items.quote: We have been winding down our vendor finance book for about a year now. We had a peak AUM of INR722 crores. Today, we are at INR355 crores. And the reason we have been doing that was that, that business was not making commercial sense.

items.statement: Overall GNPA 2.1%, net NPA 1.4%, Stage 1 assets ~94%, collection efficiency ~96%
items.quote: The gross NPA at the end of this quarter was 2.1% and a net NPA of 1.4%. In last quarter, Stage 1 assets actually has improved over the previous quarter and now it's close to 94%.

items.statement: Raised $40 million from DFC, 70% for women entrepreneurs; earlier onboarded FMO, ADB, GMO
items.quote: Recently, we have announced a deal with DFC, which is for $40 million. It is not only a deal which should be looked into isolation. It is our continuous effort where we have onboarded earlier FMO, ADB, GMO, etcetera.

items.statement: Iron ore production guidance of 13-14 million tons for FY25 assuming EC clearance by mid-February
items.quote: FY24-25, so we expect around 13 million to14 million ton s a ssuming that the EC for the expansion comes by mid-February or so

items.statement: DRI plant production guidance of around 330,000 tons per year
items.quote: And our D RI plant of around 330,000 tons a year will be the overall guidance

items.statement: Capex of INR 1,714 crores incurred in H1 FY25
items.quote: Speaking about capital expenditure, we incurred a capital expenditure of INR1,690 crores in FY24 and INR1,714 crores in H1 FY25.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 3,400-3,500 crores for FY25 and close to double that amount in each of the next two years
items.quote: We intend Lloyds Metals and to do around INR3400 crores to INR3500 crores in this year of capex and followed in the next 2 years of almost close to double sort of a thing what we are doing here

items.statement: Fundraise via QIP and warrants to fund capex without debt; warrants 35% received, 65% more expected
items.quote: We had a fundraise through QIP as well as warrants. Warrants is still around 35% is what we got and we will be getting 65% more. So, this would be funding for the projects. It would be without, we still maintain it would be without debt.

items.statement: Long-term iron ore supply agreement with Sunflag for around 1 million tons per annum at cost-plus basis
items.quote: based on this same order, we entered into an over purchase agreement where we supply them almost –they have a requirement of around 1 million tons per annum. So, at a cost- Lloyds Metals and plus basis

items.statement: Iron ore EBITDA per ton of INR 1,668 in Q2 FY25 (up 17% YoY) and INR 1,782 in H1 FY25 (up 21% YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA per ton for quarter Q2 FY25 INR1 ,668 up 17% year -on-year and f or H1 FY25 INR1,782 up 21% year-on

items.statement: Iron ore realization of INR 5,516 per ton in Q2 FY25 (up 19% YoY) and INR 5,638 in H1 FY25 (up 11% YoY)
items.quote: Iron ore realization, for quarter Q2 FY 25 the iron ore realization was INR5,516 per ton up 19% year-on-year and for H1 FY25 it was INR5,638 up 11% year-on-year

items.statement: Two price hikes taken in October: ~INR 425 and ~INR 380-400 for fines; ~INR 425 and ~INR 500 for lumps
items.quote: We have taken one price hike of 425 and the second one is around 380 or 400. in the fine sector. And in the lump sector, the first one was 425. Riyaz Shaikh: Second one, I think, is INR500

items.statement: MDO cost expected to reduce by INR 150-200/ton after mining stabilizes; further INR 150-200/ton reduction after beneficiation starts; slurry pipeline to cut transport cost by ~INR 600/ton
items.quote: After enhanced mining, the MDO cost should come down once it stabilizes by around INR150 to INR200 a ton and once the beneficiation starts by another INR150, INR200 then the volumes go up really high number one. Number two the slurry pipeline cost once it is started which will start along with the present plant that should reduce our transport cost by around INR600 a ton also.

items.statement: Beneficiation cost estimated at INR 800/ton, offset by slurry pipeline savings and lower royalty on low-grade ore
items.quote: The cost of beneficiation would be around INR800 a ton, but that is more than offset by the fact that this material would be piped by slurry pipeline to our steel plant or pel let plant facility, number one a s well as the royalty would come down because we are doing this beneficiation outside the mine area and the royalty would be paid on lower grade material

items.statement: All-inclusive cost of beneficiated ore (mining, beneficiation, royalty, transport) expected to remain around INR 2,800-3,000/ton
items.quote: The all inclusive charge of beneficiation, royalty and transport to the consuming center that is either pellet or steel plant would remain more or less the same as of today. Okay around INR2,800 to INR3,000.

items.statement: Domestic iron ore market buoyant; international prices stable around $100 for 62% grade; first double price increase in months seen in Indian market
items.quote: The iron ore market dome stically remains buoyant. There is some headwind, but the prices have remained stable at around $100 for the 62% grade in the international market. And in the Indian market for the first time after many months we have seen a double price increase in the market itself

items.statement: 85 km slurry pipeline completed in 8-9 months; awaiting first pellet plant completion by March 2025 to start utilization
items.quote: We are excited to announce the successful laying of the 85 kilometer slurry pipeline, completed in record breaking time and probably one of the fastest durations of around 8 to 9 months since we started the project. This pipeline is now awaiting the completion of the first pellet plant which will be completed within this financial year in Konsari.

items.statement: Beneficiation pilot plant commissioned March 2024 yielding 68% Fe and 38% yield (vs 35% expected); first commercial plant targeted 6 months ahead of original FY27-28 schedule
items.quote: The beneficiation plant we have started a pilot plant which was commissioned in end of March 2024. That pilot plant is giving us very good results. We are getting little better results than what was earlier thought to be. We are getting 68% FE output through the beneficiation.

items.statement: EC clearance for mine expansion to 25 MTPA expected by mid-February 2025; public hearing post Maharashtra elections
items.quote: The mining plan has been approved. The TOR has been approved. Now the public hearing would happen post this Maharashtra Elections. And subsequent to that, the EC would be issued by the Central Government, MOEA. So that is the process that is in place What has been completed, what is remaining. So we expect the timeline by February 15th, 20th, something like that.

items.statement: IPS benefit of INR 72 crores received in H1 FY25 (one-time for past investments); new IPS series at 150% for Gadchiroli pellet and DRI plants to start post-commissioning in FY26
items.quote: company received close to INR72 crores as IPS benefits from previous years contributing to overall performance and this forms part of our other income for reporting purposes

items.statement: Consolidated annual volume growth guidance of 20% and EBITDA margin of 15%-16% for the year
items.quote: So overall, we'll continue to maintain our consolidated annual volume growth guidance. We have been talking about 20% and I'm confident of achieving that and also maintaining EBITDA at 15%-16% for the year.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin close to 18%; Thailand EBITDA margin 11% to 12%
items.quote: This coupled with restriction on import from China and again has led to improvement in the EBITDA margin in India also, which is close to 18%. Even our Thailand business has reported healthy EBITDA margin of 11% to 12% led by volume growth and running our operations very efficiently.

items.statement: India volume growth of 23% in bead wire and 10% in total wire sales; Thailand volume growth of 32% in first half
items.value: India bead wire +23%, total wire +10%; Thailand +32%
items.quote: So, we have done an impressive volume growth in India of 23% of bead wire and the total wire sales have grown by 10%. We have done a very big growth in Thailand, 32% volume growth in Thailand in the first half of this year

items.statement: Chennai facility started production with ~1,000 tons sales in Q2; targeting 14,000 tons for PLI commitment; exit run rate of 2,000 tons/month
items.quote: Chennai has started production and as told you in the earlier call, it will be in phased manner. So, we have done around 1000 tons of sales from Chennai this quarter, which is going to grow in the coming months.

items.statement: Chennai facility breakeven at 18,000-20,000 tons when supplying to prime customers
items.quote: No, I think with current expenses and major saving in the transportation costs, it should break even at 18,000 to 20,000 tons volume when we are supplying to prime customers.

items.statement: Chinese dumping in Southeast Asia impacting Thailand margins; competition from Tata Steel, Arti Steel, Bansal Wire in India
items.quote: Definitely. That's the only factor where we are losing on margins. There are a lot of places where there are no margins, but to keep our fixed costs in control, we need to keep certain volumes up and running.

items.statement: Focus on bead wire only; Chennai facility dedicated to bead wire; exports targeted at 30,000 tons from India in 3 years
items.quote: Our projected exports from India is 30,000 tons in 3 years time. I cannot draw a straight line to tell you that this is what it will happen and this is how it will happen.

items.statement: Bridgestone Thailand largest factory approval audit in December; 20% allocation expected from Q1 calendar year
items.quote: And there is a final audit that is going to happen in December. Team is coming from Japan for the audit. And we are already discussing a 20% allocation from that factory, starting from first quarter, the calendar year first quarter, so Jan, Feb, March.

items.statement: Europe and North America prices structurally 15%-20% higher than Southeast Asia; freight volatility impacts realized margins
items.quote: Structurally, the prices are definitely much better, 15%, 20% higher than Southeast Asian market, but last two quarters there had been a lot of volatile situations.

items.statement: Chennai capex ~INR300 crores for 60,000 tons; 60% assets capitalized, balance in CWIP; INR5 crores trial run costs capitalized
items.quote: Around, 60% of the assets are capitalized. And balance are in the WIP. And gradually everything will get capitalized. As we start the more and more machines, complete the trial, those machines will be capitalized.

items.statement: Chinese imports in India down from 3,000-3,500 tons/month to 400-600 tons/month due to BIS/QCO
items.quote: So the volumes which had gone up to 3000 tons a month, or 3500 tons a month in one month, have come down to 400, 500, 600 tons maximum import numbers we see now.

items.statement: India capacity utilization 80%-85%; Thailand capacity utilization 80%-85%
items.quote: It's almost 80%, 85% utilization we are running both in Thailand and India.

items.statement: Freight cost saving of ~INR3,000/ton by supplying from Chennai to South India vs cross-country from Pithampur
items.quote: So in India, typically 65% of tyres are made in South India and we are in the western part of the country or in the central part of the country. So we are paying extra cost of freight of around INR3,000 per ton, which should be saved when we supply from Chennai to those locations.

items.statement: Net debt to equity remains below guidance range of 0.5x
items.quote: Our net debt to equity remains below our guidance range of 0.5x.

items.statement: R32 capacity expansion capex of INR84 crores expected to complete by February 2025
items.quote: Additionally, the expansion of R32 capacity with a capex of INR84 crores is proceeding as scheduled and is expected to be completed by February 2025.

items.statement: AHF project with INR450 crores investment on track for commissioning by end of FY25 or early FY26
items.quote: Our AHF project, which involves an investment of INR450 crores, is on track, and we anticipate commissioning by the end of FY 2025 or early FY '26.

items.statement: Agro specialty plant at Dahej with INR540 crores capex under commissioning, commercial production by November 2024
items.quote: Our upcoming agro specialty plant at Dahej with a planned capex of INR540 crores is under commissioning jointly with our customers to ensure a safe and efficient start-up and commence commercial production by November '24.

items.statement: Surat project with INR30 crores capex commissioned, first dispatch in November 2024
items.quote: Simultaneously, our Surat project with an outlay of INR30 crores is commissioned, and the first dispatch will be in November 2024.

items.statement: cGMP4 Phase 1 with INR160 crores capex progressing as planned, commissioning by end of Q3 FY26
items.quote: Phase 1 involving an outlay of INR160 crores is progressing as planned, and we aim to have it commissioned by end of quarter 3 FY '26.

items.statement: Strong order visibility for Specialty Chemicals Dahej and Surat assets driving improved capacity utilization from Q3 onwards
items.quote: There is a strong visibility to order pipeline for Dahej and Surat assets that will drive improved capacity utilization and growth from Q3 onwards.

items.statement: CDMO has firm orders for H2 FY25 with strong customer projections for FY26
items.quote: We have a strong order visibility with firm orders for the second half of FY '25. Additionally, our strategic focus on late stage and commercial molecules continues to give positive results with the business continuing to witness higher levels of customer inquiries than previously.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin at 20.7% in Q2 FY25, improving sequentially from 19.2% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Operating EBITDA margin stood at 20.7% as against 20.8% in Q2 of FY '24 and improving sequentially from 19.2% in Q1 of FY '25, reflecting higher realizations in HPP as also benefits from efficiencies secured within the businesses.

items.statement: HFO plant running at optimal capacity meeting about 80% of demand, with growth potential
items.quote: Remember on the HFO project, we've always said that what we are doing today is we've got the plant running to optimal capacity that's still meeting about 80% of the demand. So there is growth over there, too, right?

items.statement: Channel inventory concerns considered overblown; focus on strategic relationships to protect absolute EBITDA despite pricing pressure
items.quote: I think, again, channel inventory in our view is like a dead horse, yes, there's too much beating going on, on that. I think we have to recognize the fact that -- and as we've said this before, that this market means that in a strategic relationship, you have to work closely with your partners.

items.statement: CDMO revenue target of $100 million by FY27 maintained
items.quote: There is a guidance out there of the $100 million by FY '27. We stand to it, yes.

items.statement: Board-approved capex continuing into FY25 and FY26 includes R32, AHF and cGMP4 projects
items.quote: So the capex that will continue into '25 and '26, of what I can tell you now, are only the Board-approved projects, which are R32, AHF and the cGMP4, yes.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals expected to show year-on-year growth in H2 FY25 based on firm purchase orders
items.quote: So I think you should expect to see a year-on-year growth coming through. Nitin Kulkarni: And this is what we are talking is based on the POs and the firm orders which we have in

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals will see pricing reduction but absolute EBITDA protected through higher capacity commitments
items.quote: And like I said, there will be a reduction in pricing, but the absolute EBITDA will be protected or increased because we've now got higher capacities that we are committing to them.

items.statement: Targeting full year ROA of 1% in FY26
items.quote: We are looking at a full year ROA of 1% in the year 25-26. That is what we are gunning for.

items.statement: Cost to average assets target of 2.6% for next full year
items.quote: Actually, not for Quarter 3 and Quarter 4, but for the next full year, what we want to be is around 2.6%.

items.statement: NIM at 3.27% considered bottom; expect improvement from Q3/Q4
items.quote: I strongly believe that we are at the bottom end of the NIM and cost to deposits is continuing to hold at the current levels.

items.statement: Structural shift from penal interest to penal charges causes single digit bps NIM reduction
items.quote: Like I told you, you can't charge penal interest anymore, so it will come as penal charges and as soon as you collect it, you will get it. So, you will have a single digit bps change happening between NIM and fees

items.statement: Cost of funds flattened at 7.17%, cost of deposits at 7.09%
items.quote: So, cost of fund is kind of flattened out at 7.19 coming down to 7.17 and cost of deposit is 7.10 coming to 7.09.

items.statement: MFI+BC reduced from 18% to 16% of AIB book (25% of overall book)
items.quote: 16% of the AIB book is MFI plus BC and that book is 25% of the overall book. So, you can do the math yourself, 16% and 25%. And I'll tell you how to read this. You look at the previous investor presentation and see what the MFI and BC percentage was and I'll tell you what it was. It is actually 18%. That 18 has come down to 16 now.

items.statement: Mortgage stock 50-50 Home Loan/LAP; incremental LAP > Home Loan
items.quote: On the stock 50-50, on the incremental, we are trying to ensure that the BL is more than the HL and that has turned around.

items.statement: Targeting average ticket size increase from 28-30 lakhs to 40-50 lakhs
items.quote: We're also working to ensure that this, the average ticket size which currently hovers around 28 lakhs to 30 lakhs is hitched up to between 40 lakhs to 50 lakhs.

items.statement: Savings deposits grew 27% YoY; CASA improved to 25.61%
items.quote: Savings has grown by 27% year-on-year clearly showing the effort leading to the desired result.

items.statement: Upgraded Finacle, transaction banking, lending (FinOne), treasury, SIEM, AML, behavioral biometrics over last 12-18 months
items.quote: The bank has upgraded Finacle system, th e transaction banking system , the lending system, FinOne, the treasury management system from TCS, the SIEM system for cyber security, a compass system for AML, behavioral biometrics

items.statement: MFI environment may take at least a year to normalize; avoiding high-yield MFI growth
items.quote: The MFI environment I would tend to presume will take a year at least to get back to normal. I could be wrong. Okay, but that's just an educated, rather uneducated guess. So, there are two elements. So, that being the way it is, I don't see ourselves rushing headlong into high yield MFI assets which would have otherwise done.

items.statement: Mortgage sourcing in 2023 had quality issues; LTV and income norms tightened 4-5 months ago
items.quote: Our sourcing in '23 was not the quality that we aspire for. We have made some changes. And the new vintages are behaving better. But specifically, within home loans, the mortgage sourcing in 12 to 24 month bracket was not the kind of quality that we wanted it to be.

items.statement: Promoter infusion of $10 million expected in Q3 FY25
items.quote: If you ask me, it'll happen in Q3.

items.statement: Core fee income rose QoQ from Rs 114 cr to Rs 139 cr; five quarters of sustained growth
items.quote: Core fee income was 107 going up to 124 to 136 to 143 to 205. Such quarter-on-quarter for five continuous quarters, that kind of rise does not happen by coincidence.

items.statement: Cost to income ratio improved from 67.8% to 64.3% QoQ
items.quote: Net -net, we have had 11 bps improvement in ROA. In our journey where the next stop is a yearly RO A of 1%. Our ROE has moved from 10.93% in Q1 to 12.65

items.statement: Confident of meeting full-year sales guidance of INR17,000 crores despite Q2 sales dip
items.quote: we are very strong that we should be able to meet our guidance that we had given to you for the full year

items.statement: FY25 exit rental EBITDA guided at INR5,300 crores (INR5,000 crores DCCDL + INR300 crores DLF)
items.quote: the FY '25 exit rental, and I would add the other income, because that's the total rental revenue, so to say, will be as guided earlier in the ballpark of INR5,000 crores. And add to that another about INR300 crores in DLF. So it will be INR5,300 crores

items.statement: FY26 rental EBITDA expected to jump to INR6,800 crores (INR5,800 crores DCCDL + INR1,000 crores DLF)
items.quote: For FY '26, this total will jump to about INR5,800 crores for DCCDL and will jump to about INR1,000 crores for DLF, taking it to about INR6,800 crores

items.statement: Accelerated CapEx programs on rental business including Downtown Gurgaon, Downtown Chennai, retail in Downtown Gurgaon, Atrium Place, and 3 plazas in Gurgaon, Delhi, Goa
items.quote: we have accelerated our CapEx programs, as Mr. Khattar will elucidate during this hour. The Downtown Gurgaon, the Downtown Chennai, the retail in Downtown Gurgaon, the Atrium Place, the 3 plazas that we are developing in the final stage of completion in Gurgaon, Delhi, and Goa

items.statement: Dahlias RERA filing shows total revenue of INR26,000 crores at prelaunch price with 70%+ margin
items.quote: In RERA, what we have filed right now is the total revenue of about INR26,000 crores for Dahlias based on the prelaunch price that Aakash has. These numbers will obviously keep on going upwards as the price keeps on moving. But what's been reported in RERA officially is a total revenue of INR26,000 crores and a margin of 70% plus

items.statement: New project margins targeting 40%+ for most projects, Dahlias at 70%+ to maintain weighted average in late 40s
items.quote: in most of our new projects, which are not Dahlias, we are targeting a 40% plus/minus. And obviously, Dahlias would be a 70% plus/minus, so that the weighted average of the late 40s can be maintained going forward

items.statement: Strong prelaunch response for Dahlias with EOIs backed by 9% money received, double expectations
items.quote: the kind of the first set that has come out has come out almost double to what your expectations were. So hopefully, that should also reflect in the stock values

items.statement: Phase 5 residual stock will be predominantly super luxury projects
items.quote: it's safe to assume that Phase 5 will predominantly be the super luxury projects only now in that sense, so you can make your own assumptions

items.statement: Will not be reckless in writing checks for land acquisition in any geography including NCR
items.quote: We will never be reckless on writing any checks for any geography, including NCR. That is very clear

items.statement: Combined free cash flow generation of INR2,000+ crores per quarter (INR1,200 crores DevCo + INR900 crores RentCo pre-dividend/CapEx)
items.quote: we continue to generate about INR2,000 crores plus of free cash flow per quarter

items.statement: One Midtown cash flows expected to start from Q3 FY25 with significant chunk by Q4
items.quote: we expect that the cash flow should start coming in from Q3. And hopefully, between Q3 and Q4, a large chunk of it should get accounted for

items.statement: Targeting gross debt zero at DLF level in next 3-4 quarters unless significant opportunity arises
items.quote: if there's no other significant opportunity that is pursued, I think that's a target which remains on track frankly in the next three to four quarters

items.statement: Analyst Day planned for February 2025 to showcase Dahlias, Downtown, Privana and Atrium Place progress
items.quote: after the Q3 results are over, so sometime in February at a mutually convenient date, we would like to organize an Analyst Day

items.statement: NRI business grown from 3-8% to almost 28% this year, pan-India demand for super luxury from Tier 2 cities
items.quote: Our NRI business has grown from 3%, 8% to about almost now 28% this year. So we will continue to make sure that not only in India, but across the globe, we will continue to market DLF products

items.statement: Dahlias RERA carpet price filed at ~INR1 lakh/sq ft vs Camellias at INR1.3 lakh/sq ft (completed), pricing to step up in batches of 50 units
items.quote: Actually, the RERA carpet that we have filed for Dahlias, it's about INR1lakh a square foot. Aakash Ohri: So Saurabh, Camellias is a completed project. Dahlias is a 4-year -- I mean, 4 to 5 years horizon. So obviously -- in fact, I thought you were complimenting us saying that very aggressive pricing

items.statement: Expect ongoing rollouts of a major customer and start of rollouts and 5G loading by other major customer to drive near to medium term growth
items.quote: We expect the ongoing rollouts of a major customer coupled with start of rollouts and 5G loading by the other major customer to continue to drive our near to medium term growth.

items.statement: Demand outlook for next few quarters continues to be strong and expect to continue delivery momentum
items.quote: demand outlook for the next few quarters continues to be strong and we expect to continue the delivery momentum

items.statement: Order book indicates continued momentum for both tower and tenancy growth
items.quote: However, if you look at rollouts that have happened this year , they still remain on the higher side than what we have done in the past and looking at order book, I believe we will continue this momentum.

items.statement: Maintenance capex stable at Rs 2.9 billion in September 2024 quarter
items.quote: In September 2024 we have spent Rs.2.9 billion and before that was Rs.2.6 billion and before that was Rs.3.4 billion and so on so it is a stable number quarter -on-quarter.

items.statement: Energy margins impacted by seasonality in Q1 and Q2, expected to recover in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: So typically Q1 and Q2 , the energy margin is impacted by the seasonality which we expect to recover in the Q3 and Q4

items.statement: Renewal framework from FY2022 remains consistent with similar discount levels
items.quote: the framework is very consistent, so just as a recap we had signed a renewal framework in FY2022 and that was the time when we had really a bulk sort of a renewal , thereafter there has not been any major lumpy renewal in the last two financial years but pretty much the framework remains consistent and the discount levels are also very similar to what we had worked out.

items.statement: ARPT stable as loading upside offset by mix drag from new low-capex towers and renewal discounts
items.quote: So overall with the upsides and the downsides together, we are looking at a very stable situation but large part of the offset that is happening in the loading is the mix.

items.statement: GST show-cause notice on passive infrastructure assets considered remote liability, matter sub-judice
items.quote: based on our assessment , we believe that the liability currently is not evolving on the company, and we consider this as remote. This is an ongoing thing. Just because it is a very large number, we have disclosed it , there are also other matters linked to this which are currently in the courts, so the matter is a bit of sub-judice matter but currently it is a disclosure.

items.statement: Completed buyback of 56.8 million shares at Rs 465 per share
items.value: 56.8 million shares at Rs.465 per share
items.quote: During the quarter , the Company successfully completed the buyback of 56.8 million shares at a price of Rs.465 per share .

items.statement: Collected over Rs 23 billion in past 12 months from major customer, doubtful debt provision reduced to Rs 35 billion
items.value: Rs. 23 billion collected, Rs. 35 billion provision
items.quote: We have collected a total of more than Rs. 23 billion in the last 12 months. This has resulted in our provision for doubtful debt reducing to about Rs. 35 billion.

items.statement: Solar site count increased to over 25,000 with quarterly additions close to 4,000
items.quote: renewable energy portfolio continues to expand with our solar si te count increasing to more than 25,000 and quarterly additions being close to 4,000

items.statement: PAN-India uptime maintained at 99.96% despite weather disruptions 1.5x higher than last year
items.quote: Despite this, the dedicated efforts of our field teams helped us maintain a PAN-India uptime of 99.96% reaffirming our competitiveness in operating and maintaining such an extensive distributed asset base.

items.statement: Vodafone Idea active equipment deal tenancies expected to start rolling out mid-to-end of current quarter
items.quote: We see this coming towards the mid-to-end quarter is what indications we get from the customer so hopefully this quarter will see some things rolling out.

items.statement: Dividend policy unchanged, board to decide at year-end based on free cash flow
items.quote: we have a very clear dividend policy which directs u s to distribute the free cash flow so at the end of the year the Board will take a call in line with the policy.

items.statement: Net finance cost fluctuates with interest collection on overdue, difficult to predict for next quarters
items.quote: Like I said, it is very difficult to predict because the net finance cost is also dependent on the finance income which is nothing but the interest that we collect on the overdue right.

items.statement: Board approved raising up to ₹14 billion via subordinated NCDs over next 12 months to augment solvency and aid growth

items.statement: Raising ₹14 billion sub-debt will increase solvency ratio by roughly 20% and hits current regulatory cap
items.quote: if we raise the ₹ 14 billion, that should increase the solvency roughly 20%. This is the cap that we have hit at this point.

items.statement: H1 FY2025 VNB margin at 23.7%; management does not guide margins, focuses on absolute VNB growth
items.quote: We are not guided by VNB margin. We are looking at growth in absolute VNB.

items.statement: Margin impact from yield curve decline on non-par and annuity products; rates realigned from October
items.quote: Given the product changes necessitated in Q2-FY2025 due to the new regulations, we had limited ability to align rates in our non-linked and annuity portfolio in line with the market movement in G -Sec yields. Starting October, we have started aligning product rates with prevailing G-Sec yields.

items.statement: ULIP share rose to 51.6% of APE in H1 FY2025 from 42.4% a year ago; non-linked savings fell to 18.1%
items.quote: Contribution from linked savings product to overall APE increased from 42.4% in H1-FY2024 to 51.6% in H1-FY2025 on account of customer preference shifting towards ULIP products from non -linked products given market buoyancy.

items.statement: Protection and annuity together constitute 48.2% of new business premium; annuity share rose to 9.7%
items.quote: Protection and annuity are our focus segments which together constitute 48.2% of the new business premium and we expect it to continue doing well.

items.statement: Agency and Direct channels grew 45.7% APE YoY in H1 FY2025; added 29,000+ agents
items.quote: Agency and Direct business contribute 45.9% to overall APE and 53.6% to retail APE in H1-FY2025. We will continue to invest in our proprietary channels to drive business growth further.

items.statement: ICICI Bank banca premiums steady at ₹100-110 crore monthly; protection and annuity focus driving growth
items.quote: ICICI Bank is now quite consistent at ` 100 crores- ` 110 crores on a monthly basis. So, they've been quite consistent.

items.statement: Group term pricing pressure continues due to competition; underwriting focused on risk-reward
items.quote: Coming to the group term business, there has been a continued and significant trend of price reduction in this area, largely attributable to increased competition.

items.statement: Commission structure talks with partners ongoing; exploring clawback, deferral, progressive commissions, and reductions
items.quote: we are working with our partners to work out various models, which could be around clawback of commissions , if paid in full or deferred commissions, or even reducti on in commission in certain products, where to protect customer interest, that is the only option available.

items.statement: Cost to TWRP savings improved to 17.9% in H1 from 19.2% in Q1; investing in people, tech, process for future leverage
items.quote: Our Cost to TWRP on the savings line of business stood at 17.9% in H1 -FY2025 which has come down from 19.2% in Q1-FY2025. Our objective is to bring efficiency in savings line of business while we continue to focus on growth in protection business.

items.statement: Renewal premium growth subdued (~3%) due to maturing 2013-14 policies, ULIP lock-in expiries, and past growth recalibration
items.quote: There are two elements to this. One is that we do have some of our policies which are of a longer tenure, typically 10 years and above, which are now hitting the point of maturity, where, of course, these are in some sort of planned outgo.

items.statement: Surrender rates on ULIPs have dropped H1 YoY; absolute surrenders higher due to larger eligible book
items.quote: as you compare H1 to H1, surrender rates themselves have dropped, but of course the eligible book itself is much large and therefore you would have seen an absolute volume go out.

items.statement: Variable annuity product under exploration; no product ready yet, hedging strategies being evaluated
items.quote: frankly, at this point, we don't have a product. We continue to explore what are the structures that we could put in place to provide this product to our customers.

items.statement: Added over 1 lakh agents in last 2.5 years; focus on right advisor profiles for product-customer fit
items.quote: over the last 2.5 years, I think we have added over a lakh of agents.

items.statement: Committed to achieve around 20% EBITDA margin for full FY25
items.quote: we committed to achieve around 20% EBITDA for the entire financial year, yes.

items.statement: Expect healthy growth in CDMO in FY25 supported by scheduled project deliveries in Q4
items.quote: Against the industry backdrop, we expect healthy growth in FY '25, supported by scheduled project deliveries for late -phase clinical programs in Q4.

items.statement: On track to deliver full-year growth outlook driven by facility ramp-up and CDMO project deliveries in H2
items.quote: Our performance is well on track to deliver full -year growth outlook, which will be driven by facility ramp-up and scheduled CDMO project deliveries in the second half of this financial year.

items.statement: Invested INR137 crores in Q2 and INR262 crores in H1 FY25
items.quote: On the capex front, we invested close to INR137 crores for the quarter and INR262 crores for first half.

items.statement: Capex plan of around INR2,000 crores ongoing, predominantly for CDMO, with INR225 crores for bio and INR200 crores for FDF CMO
items.quote: Bio, arou nd INR225 crores, and CDMO will be the major, and then probably FDF another INR200 crores. This is for the CMO. And of course, the rest all will be the CDMO, and API will be lower.

items.statement: Current order book for product basket looks encouraging, maintaining leading share in first-line HIV treatment
items.quote: The current order book for product basked looks encouraging, and we continue to maintain a leading share in the first-line HIV treatment.

items.statement: Gross margin maintained at healthy 55% for Q2 and H1 FY25
items.quote: Gross margin maintained at a healthy level for Q2 at 55%, and for H1, it is at, same, 55%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 15% for Q2 and H1 FY25, suppressed due to operational deliveries and growth project investments
items.quote: Our EBITDA for quarter 2 stands at INR182 crores and margin at around 15%. For H1, INR353 crores with a margin of around 15%.

items.statement: ARV API sales lower due to planned facility shutdown for modifications; operations resuming this week
items.quote: ARV APIs reported revenues of INR368 crores. This was lower compared to last quarter, as we had to undertake certain modifications in the manufacturing facilities, which created capacity shortages for a few products, affecting dispatches in the Q2.

items.statement: Sustained demand in CDMO services with over 90 active projects (70+ Human Health, ~20 Animal Health and Crop Production)
items.quote: We are working on over 90 active projects in total, over 70 in Human Health and about 20 in the Animal Health and Crop Production.

items.statement: CDMO division recorded INR299 crores sales in Q2, 8% growth in H1; soft growth due to resource allocation to high-value complex programs
items.quote: In CDMO, we continued operational and commercial improvements and recorded a sales of INR299 crores. On H1 basis, the division recorded 8% growth.

items.statement: Operating deleverage at end of cycle; expect it to be behind soon as complex CDMO projects ramp up
items.quote: Maybe we are at the end of the deleverage. If you ask me, when we will leverage, maybe we have to wait a few quarters, but we at the end of the deleverage right now. Yes.

items.statement: No plans for QIP or fundraise; capex to be funded from internal accruals and depreciation
items.quote: No, we are not thinking in that direction at this juncture.

items.statement: Net debt at INR2,679 crores, debt-to-EBITDA 3.4x; expect improvement based on H2 performance, net debt to stay below INR3,000 crores
items.quote: Our net debt stood at INR2,679 crores, and debt to EBITDA is around 3.4x. This we expect to improve based on H2 performance.

items.statement: New small molecule R&D center at IKP Hyderabad commenced operations in October 2024 with flow chemistry, biocatalysis, high potent chemistry capabilities
items.quote: As highlighted in my initial remarks, we have commenced operations at our new small molecule R&D center in October 2024. The facility will leverage advanced capabilities like flow chemistry, biocatalysis, high potent chemistry.

items.statement: Targets double-digit growth for the full year if market improvement continues; digital initiatives expected to show results in Q4
items.quote: We believe some of our digital initiatives that we have put in, which got -- last of that got over at the end of the second quarter. We'll start showing results maybe in the fourth quarter of the year and as a team, we changed the double-digit growth for the organization.

items.statement: Digital business expected to deliver 30%+ margins versus 20-22% for radio
items.quote: We are about 20%, 22% of the margins that we talk about. We will be a 30% plus on digital, which is a good 10%, 20%, 15% more.

items.statement: Industry slowdown in July-August with recovery from September; Q3 start looks good
items.quote: The slowdown, obviously, I know in my speech also, I mentioned was for the month of July and August and second half, which is starting September, slightly showing recovery. And the start of the quarter for the third quarter looks good.

items.statement: Advertisement yield grew 8% year-on-year in Q2
items.quote: We have increased, I told you, 8% over last year's similar quarter.

items.statement: Digital revenue contribution at 11% in Q2 with 33% YoY growth; revenue split 65% FCT, 11% digital, 10% on-ground, 14% non-FCT on-air
items.quote: The digital segment achieved an impressive of 33% year-on-year growth, contributing 11% to our total revenue.

items.statement: Digital investments primarily in specialist manpower for video, influencer and distribution platforms; SMINCO platform development cost under Rs.1 crore
items.quote: For the investment in SMINCO, we already said we have less than Rs.1 crores is what we had invested from a platform development is concerned. And that's a one-time investment.

items.statement: Inventory utilization at 71% in H1 FY25; 38% of industry client base and 30% of new radio clients chose Radio City
items.quote: Our inventory utilization in H1FY25 stood at 71%, showcasing the efficiency of our operations and our ability to maximize all the resources.

items.statement: Phase III auction participation depends on government standardizing license fees at 4% of gross revenue and extending timelines; will bid in existing states or strategic new markets
items.quote: So as AROI, which is our industry forum, has already, a, appealed to the government to kind of relook at the licensing fees because if you know the newer market, they have agreed to the 4% of the gross revenue as the licensing fee.

items.statement: Full year cost of funds expected at 7.10%-7.15% vs earlier 7.20%-7.25%
items.quote: And we now expect the full year cost of funds to be in the range of 7.10% to 7.15% range rather than 7.20% to 7.25% initially expected.

items.statement: Full year loan growth target of 25% remains on track despite MFI and credit card slowdown
items.quote: Our loan portfolio now stands at ~INR105,000 crores, and we remain on course to hit our growth target of 25% for the year despite slowdown in MFI and calibrated approach in credit cards.

items.statement: Full year cost-to-income ratio expected around 60%
items.quote: Operating expenses would be seasonally higher in H2, but I expect cost-to-income ratio to be around 60% for the full year.

items.statement: Full year ROA target defended at 1.6%
items.quote: For the full year, we aim to defend ROA of 1.6%.

items.statement: NIM expected to be protected close to 6%
items.quote: So we expect that our NIM should get protected close to 6%.

items.statement: Full year credit cost expected to remain broadly at H1 level (~1.28%) with 5-10 bps variance
items.quote: As things stand today, we expect credit costs to remain elevated and finish full year around broadly the same level as Half 1 based on the current outlook. There could be a variance of 5, 10 bps, depending on the economic condition in the second half too.

items.statement: No branch expansion this year; leveraging 140 Fincare branches for synergy benefits over 18-24 months
items.quote: We've got around 140-odd branches from Fincare. So we haven't done any kind of branch expansion this year. That is helping us to be at lower cost.

items.statement: Yield on gross advances stable at 14.4%; incremental disbursement yield at 15.2% driven by wheels (+30bps), MBL (+40bps), housing (+130bps)
items.quote: Our yield on assets -- yield on gross advances was broadly stable at 14.4%.

items.statement: Cost of funds stable at 7.04% in Q2 vs 7.03% in Q1; incremental cost of funds at 7.3%
items.quote: Our cost of funds was stable at around 7.04% compared to 7.03% in quarter 1 FY '25.

items.statement: Early signs of pickup in economic activity over last 3-4 weeks; optimistic on improved H2 operating environment
items.quote: There are some early signs of pickup in economic activity over the last 3 to 4 weeks and we remain optimistic of an improved operating environment in later half year as consumer confidence, rural demand, private investment up again.

items.statement: 81% of disbursements in high ROA assets; secured verticals (Wheels, MBL, HL, Commercial Banking, Gold) performing well
items.quote: And more importantly, 81% of our disbursement was in high ROA assets.

items.statement: MFI credit cost elevated at ~3% in H1; may go higher; October-November shows early recovery signs but need one more quarter to assess
items.quote: MFI, which is 7% of our book is cyclical nature and asset quality is elevated, driven by industry-wide issue of overleveraging of customers. As we did communicated previously, we expect a 3% annualized credit cost through the cycle for MFI, and we are building our provisions accordingly.

items.statement: Credit card credit costs elevated in Q2; calibrated new issuance and strengthened collections; expect elevated costs in H2
items.quote: Credit costs in this portfolio in quarter 2 are elevated as per the expected lines and headline numbers is further impacted by lower base effect. We expect credit costs to stay elevated in second half also.

items.statement: Secured retail GNPA uptick driven by seasonality and weather; expect pullback in H2
items.quote: The uptick in our GNPA in this asset class during the quarter is driven by seasonality, and weather-induced challenges. We expect a pullback in the second half driven by both pickup in economic activity and seasonality.

items.statement: Applied to RBI for voluntary transition to Universal Bank license to strengthen deposit franchise
items.quote: We have recently filed an application with RBI for voluntary transition to Universal Bank and upgrade to Universal Bank license will strengthen our deposit franchise with a better brand acceptance and higher customer perception of safety and trust.

items.statement: CASA ratio at 32%, CD ratio at 86%; total deposits crossed INR 1 lakh crore to ~INR 110,000 crores (12.7% QoQ)
items.quote: All key parameters remain on track with CASA ratio at 32% and CD ratio at 86%.

items.statement: Advances growth guidance of 18% plus/minus 1% for FY25
items.quote: Our growth targets of 18% (+-/1) with more secured buyers will continue to happen.

items.statement: EEB portfolio growth guidance of 10% to 12% for FY25
items.quote: I think we will be working towards a growth of between 10% to 12%.

items.statement: NIM guidance range of 7% to 7.5% for FY25
items.quote: Our broad range of net interest margin between 7% to 7.5%. Our endeavor is to be within that particular range.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 1.8% to 2% for FY25
items.quote: We had guided that we will be in the range of 1.8% to 2% of credit cost for FY5.

items.statement: Opex to assets ratio guidance similar to FY24 level for FY25
items.quote: We guided that in FY25, cost to opex ratio should be at similar level of FY24 as we would continue to invest in people, technology and building key capabilities through the year.

items.statement: Yield difference of roughly 10% between EEB book and secured portfolio
items.quote: Actually, the yield difference is roughly around 10% between the EEB book and the overall secured portfolio books.

items.statement: EEB DPD pool at Rs 1,984 crores (3.3% of EEB advances), SMA 0 increased to 1.5%
items.quote: The overall EEB DPD pool (SMA 0, 1 & 2) was at Rs. 1,984 crores representing 3.3 % of EEB advances and reflecting an increase of Rs.548 crores QoQ.

items.statement: Gross slippages increased to Rs 1,115 crores in Q2FY25, mainly in EEB book
items.quote: However, in this quarter (Q2FY25), gross slippages were higher at Rs 1,115 crores. Increase in slippages in Q2 was mainly in the EEB book, where it increased to Rs 752

items.statement: Secured portfolio increased to 47% of advances from 42.8%
items.quote: Our secured book now constitutes 47% of advances up from 42% in March 2024.

items.statement: Retail assets grew 92% YoY, Commercial Banking 40% YoY, Housing 17% YoY
items.quote: The Secured book growth was contributed by Retail Assets which grew at 92% YoY, Commercial Banking Assets which grew 40% YoY and Housing which grew at 17% YoY.

items.statement: CGFMU final claim payout of Rs 315 crores plus Rs 228 crores recoveries to be booked as Other Income on settlement
items.quote: The outstanding claim pay out of Rs.315 crores and the recoveries, from the first tranche claim, held in the Bank's books of Rs.228 crores as on March 31, 2024, i.e., total of approx. 543 crores will be suitably accounted in the Bank's P&L as part of 'Other Income' on settlement of the claim.

items.statement: Board approved enabling resolution for QIP up to INR 2.88 billion implying up to 6% dilution at INR 48,000 crore market cap, valid for 12 months
items.quote: Our Board has passed the resolution requesting his appointment. And now we will take this resolution to the general body very shortly, so that his appointment becomes effective. The second resolution that we had today was about the proposal to raise capital via the QIP group.

items.statement: QIP proceeds for potential acquisitions in cost reduction, adjacencies, compliance, and China; not for single large deal but multiple reasonable-sized opportunities
items.quote: So, there are such I would say, 4 or 5 types of companies. There's no one very large, but reasonable size 3, 4 opportunities. Also, in addition to that, I must say that we have some very significant opportunity for consolidation and mega deals.

items.statement: Reiterated FY25 guidance: 18-22% YoY CC revenue growth, EBITDA margin 20.5%+; revenue expected at lower end, margin a few decimals higher
items.quote: We believe that due to cost reduction, which we have to give to our clients, both on fixed price and especially basically reducing the cost for them. The revenues will be on the lower side of guidance while the profits will be on the higher side, while we have talked about 20.5% plus, it will be a few 0.2 to 0.3 decimals higher than what we have mentioned earlier.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA 20.8% after absorbing full quarter impact of increments and ESOP cost (2.7% impact); PAT INR 203 crore includes INR 29.3 crore one-time insurance claim
items.quote: The EBITDA is at 20.8%, which is 27.7% year -on-year growth over the last quarter this year. This is after absorbing the increments, which we had given proper full increment. And also, additionally ESOP-cost.

items.statement: Strong pipeline with $207 million wins in Q2 across geographies; large strategic deal conversations ongoing but timing uncertain due to OEM caution and project start delays
items.quote: With this, I would also like to say that our pipeline continues to be strong with our current wins during the quarter of $207 million which I mentioned about the various reasons why we will continue to see opportunities in the market.

items.statement: Q3 not expected to be strong due to uncertainty on when recent large deal wins will start; European OEM caution and year-end timing causing delays
items.quote: So, while we have got very strong good wins in last 2 quarters, based on the environment, we are not 100% sure when they would start. And so, I would consider it not so strong quarter 3 from that perspective.

items.statement: Growth driven by Asia (Japan, Korea, India), Powertrain and Middleware practices; passenger car revenue up 5.3% QoQ and 26.4% YoY; fixed price projects and offshoring increasing
items.quote: The growth has been largely driven through Asia. And when we talk about Asia, in this case, it is more about Japan, Korea and India. It is driven by Powertrain and Middleware as the practice areas, and the passenger car basically is grown by 5.3% quarter-on-quarter and 26.4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Offshoring increasing to reduce client costs; volume growing but revenue impact lower due to onshore-to-offshore shift; productivity gains and fixed price projects supporting margins
items.quote: Absolutely, I think the first part is the volume is not impacted. Volume is growing. While we are trying to increase our productivity and other things, as you can see, we still continue to add net headcount in some ways and improve the productivity both.

items.statement: European OEMs under financial pressure from China competition and weak economy; US OEMs cautious but opportunities from China software ban and off-highway; China engagement selective for innovation ecosystem and compliance
items.quote: In case of Europe, we believe that most of the European OEMs are certainly struggling in terms of their financial performance. And however, we believe that in due course, there will be a consolidation and due to both the competence, relationship and the scale, KPIT will be a beneficiary of the consolidation.

items.statement: Investing in QORIX (now part of Eclipse and COVESA foundations) and N-Dream (gaming, 26% stake); QORIX revenue not consolidated, integration services revenue to KPIT; main product 12-18 months away
items.quote: In QORIX at least certain revenues have started , though for the large offerings which we have, it will take some time. It has become a part of Eclipse Foundation and Covesa Foundation. And these two will certainly help us in our endeavour to make it really an industry-leading platform.

items.statement: TCV last 6 quarters mostly $150-200M range except Q4 FY24; large deal pipeline in Europe, Americas, Asia but timing uncertain; existing clients can double revenue organically
items.quote: So, Karan, as we discussed earlier on, there are a few clients in Europe as well as in Americas, where we are actually in conversations of building long- term large engagements. And of course, there are conversation s in Asia as well

items.statement: Volkswagen Group relationship strong; hybrid/powertrain opportunities increasing as EV targets adjust; confident on 2-3 year growth
items.quote: We believe that there are significant opportunities with the Volkswagen Group. As you know, it's -- you looked at some of the announcements that Volkswagen Group have made. They really need -- they are in the process of reinventing themselves in many ways.

items.statement: M&A criteria: not EBITDA or EPS dilutive within 12-18 months, strong cash conversion, critical for clients, top 2-3 global player in area; walked away from more deals than pursued
items.quote: First, we make sure that it is not a margin dilutive in a certain period, maybe 12 to 18 months it is not a margin dilutive. It's not dilutive on EBITDA, that's the first point. Second, it is not EPS dilutive, that is the second part we look at.

items.statement: Employee cost guidance: 2-3% YoY increase standalone, 4-4.5% consolidated for FY25; declining trajectory through FY29
items.quote: At least 2%-3% increase on the employee cost on a standalone basis, and close to around 4%-4.5% on the consolidated level. And the overall guidance that we have been given till 2028-2029, the employee cost should be on a declining trajectory.

items.statement: Admin expense guidance: 8-10% YoY increase standalone, 10-12% consolidated for FY25
items.quote: And on the other admin expenses, the range, the increase would be around 8%to 10%.

items.statement: Equity/hybrid yield ~75 bps, ETF/index ~6-7 bps, cash/arbitrage ~10 bps, income ~20-21 bps; yields stable QoQ and YoY
items.value: 75 bps equity/hybrid, 6-7 bps ETF/index, 10 bps cash/arbitrage, 20-21 bps income
items.quote: I can say for equity and hybrid fund, it's close to around 75 basis points. ETF and index fund is roughly around 6 -7 basis points. Cash and arbitrage is around 10 basis points and income fund at around 20 to 21 basis points.

items.statement: Expect good equity and hybrid inflows in next two quarters driven by performance turnaround and hybrid focus
items.quote: So, on the equity and the hybrid side, yes, the management focus is there, and we should expect good inflows in the next two quarters.

items.statement: Longer duration debt funds to attract inflows if rate cut cycle plays out; currently flows in short duration/money market
items.quote: But if the interest rate cut cycle plays out, then definitely a longer duration product will be the flavor of the season and not only UTI Mutual Fund but the entire industry can witness a good amount of inflows as far as the long duration product is concerned.

items.statement: Hybrid category mobilizing ~₹2,500 crore in H1 FY25; major part of incremental SIP inflows
items.quote: In fact, for the half of the financial year, we are mobilizing excess of close to around ₹ 2,500 crore on the hybrid category.

items.statement: UTI Alternatives expected to turn core PAT positive from FY26; three to four new funds launching
items.quote: So, from the alternate we are quite hopeful that at least from the beginning of the next financial year this company will turn into core PAT positive.

items.statement: Investing in international expansion: new offices in New York, Paris, Dubai, Singapore; hiring in key geographies
items.quote: We have opened an office in Paris as well as in the United States. So, initial establishment cost, as well as the rental cost of these two offices have come into.

items.statement: Digital strategy investment: Salesforce tie-up, revisiting digital assets, hiring in digital space globally
items.quote: We are investing in our digital strategy that goes directly to the P&L. We have tied up with the Salesforce. We ar e revisiting our digital assets and we are also hiring in the digital space so far as employees are concerned

items.statement: One-time deferred tax charge of ₹12.10 crore in Q2 FY25 due to budget change in capital gains tax rate and removal of indexation
items.quote: As a result, the deferred tax liability recorded on fair value gains on the investment as of June '24 has increased by ₹ 12.10 crore, thereby resulting in an additional one-time charge in the net profit of the company as on September 30, 2024.

items.statement: UTI Alternatives: SDOF-I (₹71 cr) and SDOF-II (₹467 cr) in exit stage; SDOF-III (₹540 cr) fundraising; Multi Opportunities Fund-I (₹1,598 cr) investing; Real Estate Opportunity 1 (₹130 cr) fundraising
items.quote: UTI SDOF-I received SEBI approval in August 2017 and has final close in May 2019. It has a net commitment of ₹ 71 crore and is in the exit stage. • UTI SDOF-II received SEBI approval in February ‘21 and had the final close in May ‘22. It had net commitments of ₹ 467 crore and is currently in exit stage. • UTI SDOF-III received SEBI approval in April ‘22 and has a net commitment of ₹ 540 crore. It

items.statement: Commission rationalization on stock AUM not done; exploring option for Q4 FY25 or FY26; marginal sharing policy on incremental inflows continues
items.quote: as far as the rationalization of commission is concerned, yes, we are exploring that option , d efinitely not in this particular quarter, but maybe quarter four or beginning of the next financial year, we will take a call on that

items.statement: Pension fund yield: gross ~3 bps, net ~1.5 bps after 50% PFRDA fee; Unified Pension Scheme with 10% higher allocation to boost AUM
items.quote: the gross f ees is close to around 3 basis points. And as you are aware, 50% of the fees is required to be paid back to PFRDA for development of pension fund. So, on a net basis, the incremental fees is close to around 1.5 basis points

items.statement: ESOP expense ~₹3.5 crore for H1 FY25, ~₹5 crore for full FY25 (same standalone and consolidated)
items.quote: We have expenses close to around ₹ 3.5 crore for half year and for the whole of the financial year, the number should be in the range of around ₹ 5 crore only.

items.statement: Target 10% volume growth and 15% value growth annually while maintaining current profitability levels
items.quote: We will maintain the status quo what we are doing currently, sir. The 10% by volume and 15% by value is what we keep targeting and maintaining the profitability also at current levels is what we will be pushing forward for.

items.statement: Expect margins to stay in same ballpark; may pass savings to farmers and consumers if things improve
items.quote: We expect margins to stay in the same ballpark and if things improve, we might be able to pass the savings on to our farmers and consumers.

items.statement: Maharashtra integrated plant capex estimated at INR200-250 crores over FY25-26, civil works starting by end of November
items.quote: The rough number right now because we were between INR200 crores to INR250 crores is what we are looking at an overall project cost which will be done in stages.

items.statement: Maharashtra plant operations targeted to commence by April 2026, with 15-16 month construction timeline
items.quote: Targeting April 26 maybe little earlier, little later one two months, this way that way can be the range.

items.statement: Maharashtra milk procurement target of 7 lakh litres per day in next three years from current 2 lakh litres per day
items.quote: Our target is to take this procurement t o around 7 lakh litres per day in the next three years

items.statement: VAP share of revenue expected to stabilize at 39-40% range
items.quote: We will continue to keep it in those ranges of 39% to 40% is what we think it is.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margins expected within plus or minus 100 bps of current levels
items.quote: So in terms of steady state margins we can assume it somewhere plus or minus 100 bps in the current levels? Dodla Sunil Reddy: Yes sir

items.statement: Orgafeed margins sustainable at around 13% with plus/minus 100 bps variation
items.quote: No, it will be sustainable. So plus or minus 100 b ps this way that way depending on the commodity

items.statement: Milk procurement prices expected to see only marginal increases in FY25; FY26 outlook depends on summer season
items.quote: Broadly speaking, when we look at the procurement prices of the current year of '25, there will only be marginal increases and we don't think that it will go up substantially and status quo will be maintained.

items.statement: Milk prices kept unchanged after previous quarter cut; confident to sustain robust volumes
items.quote: Since we made a price cut in the previous quarter, this time around we have kept our milk prices unchanged and are confident to sustain our robust volume throughout the year.

items.statement: Strong festive demand expected for ghee and sweets in upcoming quarter; butter and SMP sales to continue as part of VAP portfolio
items.quote: In the upcoming quarter, we expect a strong festive demand for the ghee as well as sweets. Further, we will continue to pursue butter SMP sales as a part of our VAP portfolio.

items.statement: No consumption slowdown seen in big cities; growth trajectories maintained despite food inflation
items.quote: Our market, we have been seeing growth, sir, because whatever we are selling, the same names like DMart and whatever, where we are retailing also, we have seen reasonable uptake and uptake coming in. So we are seeing no slowdown, but the growth to be maintaining the growth trajectories, even in the big cities.

items.statement: Butter and SMP bulk sales were INR166 crores in Q2 FY25; consumer VAP (curd, ghee, paneer) grew to INR211 crores
items.quote: Total, madam, for this quarter, we have done around 378 crores of turnover. Out of that, SMP is around 40 and butter is around 126, if you remove it. So, we have done around INR211 crores of other than bulk sales, B2C.

items.statement: Africa Q2 gross margin dropped to 25% from 43% in Q1 due to delayed monsoon; expected to recover in Q3
items.quote: So, this financial year, first quarter, it was 43%, and second quarter is 25%.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR3 per share declared; may increase by year-end; cash deployment for Maharashtra expansion and acquisitions
items.quote: One is, as we have already announced in my talk earlier, we are giving an interim dividend, and we'll try to see if INR3 per share. We'll also be looking at by end of the year to see if it will be a little more of a dividend, which will come in.

items.statement: Inventory reduction of INR141 crores from March to September; will continue aggressive procurement and inventory build-up in H2
items.quote: If you see last March we are at around INR390 crores. Now we are at INR231 crores. There is INR141 crores of reduction in the inventory.

items.statement: On track to achieve 1,000 stores by March-25 and 2,000 stores by December-26
items.quote: broadly, yes, we are on track to achieve the 1,000 stores by March-25 and 2,000 stores by December-26, as per our guidance.

items.statement: Food delivery GOV growth guidance is 20%+ CAGR over next few years, not 30% near term
items.quote: We've always spoken about 20%+ GOV growth as guidance on a CAGR basis over the next few years. I don't think we've ever indicated that the business is likely to grow at 30% in the near term.

items.statement: Quick commerce Adjusted EBITDA margin target of 4% to 5% seems more realistic and achievable
items.quote: But the guidance we've given on margins is that we believe this business can reach 4% to 5% (Adjusted EBITDA margin). With every passing quarter, that seems more realistic and achievable to us.

items.statement: Board approved enabling resolution to raise up to $1 billion via QIP, subject to shareholder approval; actual size depends on market conditions
items.quote: The board has passed an enabling resolution to raise up to $1 billion, which is also subject to shareholder approval. The actual fundraise size will be dependent on demand and market conditions at that time.

items.statement: Capex of INR 214 crore spent on 152 new stores and seven new warehouses
items.quote: Regarding capex, the bulk was spent on the store expansion that we have laid out in the letter. In addition to the 152 stores we opened, we also added seven new warehouses.

items.statement: Contribution margin flat for last 2-3 quarters due to fixed costs from new store openings captured above contribution line
items.quote: This is why we haven't seen any contribution margin expansion in the last two or three quarters, largely because of the expansion we're doing.

items.statement: AOVs similar across top 7-8 cities; some non-Delhi markets have higher AOV than Delhi
items.quote: If you look at the top seven-eight cities, the AOVs are similar, actually fairly similar. In fact, there could be one or two markets outside of Delhi where the AOV is higher than Delhi.

items.statement: Non-grocery categories like beauty, electronics, toys still growing; focus on building infrastructure across all categories
items.quote: the ones we launched over the past year such as beauty, electronics, and toys are still growing categories. We're still learning which use cases within these categories have further room for growth.

items.statement: Fundraise not linked to discounting; have enough cash to discount if needed but not planning to
items.quote: We're not raising money to start discounting more. We need do what is right for the business first, and we don't think that discounting is going to help our business at this point in time.

items.statement: Delhi NCR share of Blinkit GOV fallen from ~47% to <40%; now largest player in all major metros outside Chennai and Hyderabad
items.quote: If you look at it sequentially, the share of Delhi NCR in our business continues to fall. We had given this data a couple of quarters ago when we had said that the share was around 47%; today, that number is less than 40%.

items.statement: Quick commerce audience overlap with food delivery decreasing; QC appeals to broader demographic
items.quote: The overlap is decreasing over time because we're seeing that quick commerce is appealing to a much wider demographic than food delivery.

items.statement: No plan to move away from marketplace model or own inventory; current structure does not allow inventory ownership
items.quote: At this point, though, there is no plan to move away from our current business model

items.statement: Store expansion pace may be lumpy due to external dependencies like licenses; not expected to be linear
items.quote: This expansion could be lumpy because we don't control the entire process of opening a store. There's a lot of dependency on external bodies, licenses, and so on. So please don't expect this to be linear.

items.statement: Not considering private labels at this point but will continue to evaluate
items.quote: Not considering at this point Nikhil, but we'll continue to evaluate.

items.statement: Targeting 4% volume growth for full year FY25
items.quote: I am really looking at a 4% volume growth for the full year.

items.statement: Targeting net debt below Rs 4,030 crore by end of FY25
items.quote: by the end of this fiscal we should be lower than last year's Rs. 4,030 crores

items.statement: Long-term net debt target Rs 3,500-4,000 crore
items.quote: in the long term we are comfortable operating the Company at Rs. 3,500 to Rs. 4,000 crores

items.statement: FY25 capex may be Rs 20 crore shy of Rs 400 crore upper end
items.quote: We may even be shy of maybe Rs. 400 crores by 20 odd crores in H2

items.statement: Next expansion capex to start end of FY25 or early FY26
items.quote: sometime end of this year, early next year, we should start our next expansion

items.statement: Project Bridge 2.0 yielded Rs 50/ton cost reduction in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Project Bridge 2.0 is on track and has yielded a reduction of Rs. 50 per ton in operating cost in Q2 FY '25

items.statement: Targeting Rs 75/ton cost reduction from Bridge 2.0 in H2 FY25
items.quote: In H2, we should be looking at about Rs. 75 per ton, given the pace at which these various projects are moving

items.statement: Blended realization fell 2.7% QoQ to Rs 5,362/ton in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our Q2 blended realization is Rs. 5,362 as against Rs. 5,513

items.statement: Power & fuel cost at lowest in 12 quarters at Rs 1.54/Mcal
items.quote: The Company has reached the lowest blended fuel cost in the last 12 quarters at Rs. 1.54 per Mcal

items.statement: Demand recovery depends on budget execution and post-monsoon pickup from mid-November
items.quote: post the budget a lot of schemes were announced by the government, but they have not kicked-off on the ground as of now. But I am optimistic that once the Pooja is done, money has to flow into the market and construction will pick up

items.statement: Premium product share in trade segment reached record 43% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Premiumization remains a key focus area for the Company, with premium product share in the trade segment reaching a record high of 43% in Q2 FY '25

items.statement: Cautious on demand outlook and pricing; budget disbursement and execution key monitorable
items.quote: we are cautious about the demand outlook and pricing dynamics in the cement industry. While the Union Budget has announced an infrastructure investment of Rs. (+11) lakh crores, actual disbursement of funds and project execution on the ground remains a key monitorable

items.statement: Net take rate on DLG merchant loans expected to be a little north of 5% over the life of the loan, net of DLG cost.
items.period: over the life of the loan
items.quote: our net take rate, for the DLG business, like I mentioned, should be alittle bit north of 5% over the life of the loan. So when I'm saying net, that is net of DLG cost, that is notdissimilar to loans which are without DLG

items.statement: Contribution margins have returned to near 55% without UPI incentives, which is expected to be the new norm.
items.quote: Important to note that if you notice our contribution margins, they have gone back tonear 55% without any UPI incentive, which is the guidance that we had done with the UPI incentive andin my belief, this is going to be the new norm

items.statement: Expect to not only meet but exceed guidance of one profitable quarter by end of year, delivering significant profitability this year.
items.quote: we expect to not only meet that guidance but exceed that guidance. So deliver somesignificant profitability this year and then with all the tailwinds that we have, especially on merchant payments, merchant lending, personal loans, and the huge improvements that we have had in our coststructure, we expect to get very meaningfully profitable

items.statement: Evaluating shift of cloud costs from opex to capex model to improve capital efficiency as AI scales.
items.quote: there is a cloud cost, a pretty large amount of cloud cost and we'veseen one of our industry peers make a cloud in a capex model instead of an opex model and that'sanother way to look at the cost structure there

items.statement: DLG cost expensed upfront in other direct expenses; collection revenue recognized over 12-18 months, creating near-term drag but steady-state net take rate north of 5%.
items.quote: The DLG costis basis an ECL model. Given this is a new product, we have taken, basis of the ECL model, the entire costof DLG has been taken up front. It is in the other direct expenses, so above contribution margin. Thecollection revenues will come in under financial services revenue over time

items.statement: Current cost base guided as new floor; continuing optimization on people, software, and indirect expenses (85% of other indirect expenses) including AI-driven efficiencies.
items.quote: At the moment we are guiding to this being the newbase, although we continue to look at our cost base, particularly on people, software costs and otherindirect expenses, which is the largest chunk, about 85% of our other indirect expenses to continue tofind optimization opportunities

items.statement: Enormous demand for merchant loans at very good asset quality; personal loan demand sufficient with 6 lakh key financial services customers last quarter, focus on adding lending partners to unlock supply.
items.quote: we're seeing enormous amounts of demand at very good asset qualities and this is a veryprofitable business for us. So we do want to try to get into win-win partnerships with other lenders

items.statement: Open to DLG with more partners but not managing to a specific DLG mix; no cap set, will let mix evolve over next few quarters.
items.quote: perfectly okay for business to be done on DLG model going forward and I don't think there is a metricthat we're trying to manage to do x percent should be DLG and x percent should be non DLG and we're going to find out more in the next few quarters whether it stabilizes to a certain number

items.statement: DLG arrangement structured as lien-marked FD, fully expensed upfront; collection revenue permitted under regulation and not considered synthetic DLG.
items.quote: Our arrangement is that, in this case we would most likely give this asa FD, which would be lien marked, and all of that cost, 100% of the DLG that we give, the arrangement isthat we most likely give that in the form of a FD, and that FD would be lien marked, and that entireamount of DLG that we are giving in the form of lien marked FD, has been expensed in the last quarter

items.statement: Wallet business on hold awaiting clear regulatory direction on Paytm Payments Bank.
items.quote: The Paytm wallet was operated by Paytm Payments Bank, which is under regulatory supervision right now, we would wait for a clear direction on that side first.

items.statement: UPI consumer onboarding awaits NPCI approval; see penetration scope nearly double current levels in metro cities alone, targeting tens of millions more soundboxes.
items.quote: while we all see significant amount ofPaytm and Paytm soundboxes all around us in metro cities, I am going to surprise you by saying that thepenetration scope is nearly double of what it is penetrated as of now in metro cities, I'm talking metrocities only

items.statement: Active sales force stabilizing at 30,000-31,000; productivity per employee improving via AI, headcount to grow slowly.
items.quote: We are also enhancing the productivity per employee,behind the scene. Let me also say the AI that we keep singing a song of is also going to help us on peremployee productivity in the sales field. So while the number would increase slowly, there will be furtherproductivity enhancement rather

items.statement: Cash balance Rs 10,000 crores; board to decide on capital return framework after achieving sustained free cash flow positivity, expected in a couple of quarters.
items.quote: I do acknowledge that we have Rs 10,000 crores of cash, and I don't see any scenario under which we will be able to use up any meaningful percentage of that cash. But I think we havedecided that let's get to the the most important thing is that business should throw off cash

items.statement: Advertising on soundbox not a meaningful near-term contributor; viewed as 20% experiment with potential knock-on benefits to overall ad business.
items.quote: I don't think it will be a meaningful contributor. Theintention was to say that we really continue to innovate on the technology and the various aspects ofmerchant businesses.
