So I'm going to say that these areone of those 20% experiments that our team cont

items.statement: Food and FMCG turnover target of Rs. 6,000 crores plus for FY25 and Rs. 10,000 crores by FY27
items.quote: we are quite sure that we will have that target of Rs. 6,000 crores plus of turnover for the Food for the financial year '25, and we are committed to see that we reach to the Food and FMCG turnover of Rs. 10,000 crores by FY '27.

items.statement: Expect double-digit volume growth in Edible Oil going forward
items.quote: So, looking forward, if not 17% or like this, because these are not always a regular thing, but yes, double-digit growth is what we expect.

items.statement: Target of reaching 50,000 towns by March 2025
items.quote: Of course, our target of reaching 50,000 towns by March '25 continues, and we are focusing on that, and we are very sure that we will achieve this target by March '25.

items.statement: Edible Oil sustainable EBITDA run rate of Rs. 550-600 crores per quarter
items.quote: The gross margin is closely in the range of Rs . 1,700 crores quarter- after-quarter and EBITDA in the range of Rs. (+550) crores. The last 2 quarters were excellent adani wilmar For a healthy growing nation in terms of the EBITDA. In both the quarters, we have been able to post the EBITDA of Rs. 600 crores plus

items.statement: Food and FMCG segment EBITDA neutral by design, focus on volume and market share growth
items.quote: Food and FMCG, as we always keep saying that it still continued to be close to EBITDA neutral kind of business, given the fact that our entire focus is on growing the market share and growing the volume.

items.statement: Expect better demand in Q3 due to marriage season
items.quote: We are more optimistic on the next quarter's marriage season demand and how that spans out. So, hopefully, next quarter should be better.

items.statement: Duty hike passed on to consumers with 10-15 day lag; small inventory gains possible but not significant
items.quote: In Edible Oil, historically, whenever there is an increase in price, whether because of duty or any other reason, that is normally passed on. And there is always a lag of 10, 15 days because inventory pipeline, inventory at distributor level, retail level, even at Company warehouses, are there to take care of 15, 20 days.

items.statement: Food volume growth of 33% includes G2G rice sales; normalized underlying growth is 21%
items.quote: This 33% is inclusive of a government-to-government sale, which is rice sold to government agencies for the export, which is not a very sustainable business in a sense, we are not sure whether this will be there next year, yes or no. So, therefore, if we normalize this business also, the underlying volume growth in food is 21%.

items.statement: Bangladesh operations under stress; expect improvement in next 6 months but not optimistic for FY25; focus only on branded sales
items.quote: Bangladesh operation, as I said earlier, continues to be in stress. We lost Rs. 51 crores in H1; however, things have now started improving after the new government taking over in Bangladesh.

items.statement: Capacity utilization in Food segment at 57%, sufficient capacity for future growth
items.quote: Capacity utilization is decently placed at 57%, giving an indication that we have enough capacities in place to accommodate the future growth that this segment will see.

items.statement: ESOP scheme approved for 1% of issued shares, vesting over 2-4 years to retain talent
items.quote: the organization for growth of the Company. This scheme will have 1% of the pool, 1% of issued shares. Issued and subscribed shares would be the pool for this scheme. And this will be vested in a period from 2 to 4 years from the date of the grant for encouraging long-term commitment and the performance from the employees

items.statement: Wheat Flour market share increased to 5.25% from 4.42% per IMRB MAT Sep'24
items.quote: As per the IMRB MAT '24, market share of Wheat Flour on MAT 12 months basis in September '24 went up to 5.25% versus 4.42%, so close to 1% gain in the market share.

items.statement: Edible Oil market share increased to 16.2% from 16.12% per IMRB MAT Sep'24
items.quote: As per the IMRB, the Edible Oil market share has also gone up from 16.12% to 16.2%.

items.statement: Alternate channel revenue crossed Rs. 3,000 crores LTM; e-commerce grew 27%, quick commerce 46%
items.quote: Alternate channel now contributes close to Rs. 3,000 crores of revenue for the Company basis last 12 months. And overall growth for the alternate channel is 14%, in which e-commerce grew by 27% and quick commerce, which is most talked about channel today in India, and most of the FMCG companies are certainly trying to leverage more and more on this, grew by 46%.

items.statement: HoReCa channel revenue close to Rs. 500 crores LTM with 40%+ YoY growth
items.quote: HoReCa channel, which is another alternate channel for us, which we started 2 years back is growing very fast. 40% plus kind of year-on-year growth and now contributing close to Rs. 500 crores of revenue basis last 12 months.

items.statement: Food inflation pressure on margins; expect normalization with better wheat, pulses, rice crops
items.quote: Wheat production next year is going to be reasonably better because of the good monsoon this year. And dal, pulses, also, will be good. Rice, already it is 10% down. So, I think overall, food inflation will normalize, and we will see good growth in Food business as well as a little bit increased margin.

items.statement: Target to maintain ~13.5% EBITDA margin for FY25
items.quote: That's what we try to maintain 13.5% EBITDA, that's what we'll try to maintain this year.

items.statement: Employee cost expected to grow 12-13% YoY for next few years
items.quote: We see 12%-13% growth year-on-year for next few years.

items.statement: No major capex needed for next 2-3 years; minor investment in sweets capacity
items.quote: We don't need major capex for growing the capacity for investment. In sweet category, of course, we'll do some investment in next one year to grow the capacity to meet the

items.statement: No major fund raise needed; strong cash generation expected over next 2-3 years
items.quote: we'll generate a lot of cash in next two- three years. So, we'll look at right asset, which can give either category addition or anything. But yes, it doesn't require any major fund in any way.

items.statement: Direct retail reach 278k outlets (Sep'24), targeting 300k by FY25 end and 350k by FY26
items.quote: We increased it 2, 78,000. So, that's 7 0,000 increase in direct coverage. And that's what our endeavour is to reach at least 3.5 lakh outlet till FY '26.

items.statement: Revised FY25 volume growth guidance to 10-12% overall with 15% in H2; EBIT margin target 8-8.5% for wire & cable in H2
items.quote: For the second half of FY'25, we now expect a volume growth of approx. 15% which should help us to achieve an overall volume growth of 10% to 12% in FY'25. We anticipate a stronger performance in H2 FY'25 and expect our EBIT margins in the wire and cable segment to improve back to the range of 8% to 8.5% for the second half of FY'25.

items.statement: FMEG revenue growth guidance of 20-25% for H2 FY25
items.quote: But still when we talk about like 20-25% kind of revenue growth we are expecting in FMEG business.

items.statement: Rs 500 crore capex cycle over FY24-25 to be completed by March 2025; doubling power cable capacity and increasing wire capacity 20-25%
items.quote: So, overall, our CAPEX plan was of Rs.500 crores, which was spread over two years, which is like FY'24 and FY'25. Since we are executing CAPEX only, this will be completed by March '25.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 wire & cable EBIT margin 5.1% due to copper volatility and delayed price pass-through; gross margin contraction ~4% YoY
items.quote: The EBIT margin for the segment stood at 5.1% impacted by copper price volatility and delay in passing the cost instantaneous.

items.statement: Copper price volatility caused ~4% gross margin contraction in Q2; unable to fully pass on higher prices to consumers in timely manner
items.quote: So, when we see figures of this quarter or even for this first half of this year, the major contraction has come at the gross margin level only. So, it was reflected by two things: one, copper price volatility, and secondly, like passing on this impact to consumers in timely phase.

items.statement: Domestic wire volume grew 2% YoY in Q2; domestic cable volume grew 36% YoY; export volume declined 9% YoY due to shipment delays
items.quote: It's still like in domestic also we have grown at much higher pace in cable compared to cable wire. So, in domestic, our wire business has grown by 2% only while cable business has grown by 36% and I am talking this about on YoY basis for Q2.

items.statement: Export shipment delays increased from 25 to 35-40 days causing some order loss to nearby suppliers like Turkey; cable product approvals in US/Europe expected by quarter end
items.quote: So, what happened like earlier what we were making export to Europe, like they were taking regularly from us, but when there were delays in shipment, so they might have some purchased some quantity from Turkey or similar places which are very nearby to them.

items.statement: FMEG growth driven by shift to premium/mid-premium products in fans, appliances, switches; lighting faced price pressure
items.quote: So, majority of the contribution have come in spite of the challenge in like price pressure or price correction in lighting, in spite of that, we were able to achieve this growth of 24%. So, it is mix of like shifting some sales from economic category to premium and mid-premium category which are high margin products.

items.statement: Export demand temporarily impacted by Red Sea shipping delays increasing transit time and freight costs; some customers shifted to nearer suppliers
items.quote: Europe is my largest export market and due to some delay in shipments, what happens like if it was taking 25 days, now it is taking 35 to 40 days. So, this has delayed some shipments also and even some few parties changed their orders from us to maybe some other suppliers also.

items.statement: FMEG breakeven expected at Rs 1,100 crore revenue (EBIT level) by early FY26, earlier than previously indicated Rs 1,500 crore
items.quote: So, we are expecting to achieve that one much before that like Rs 1,100 crores of level of top line EBIT level break even.

items.statement: Management expects to continue growing at 25% year-on-year and close FY25 in line with IPO communicated targets.
items.quote: We have in the past also grown at a CAGR of 23% and for the last 3 years. And if you say 6-7 years in the past, we have grown at a CAGR of 29%. So, during my last call also I have mentioned that we will continue to grow at an annual speed of 25% year-on-year and we will maintain that.

items.statement: PAT margin historically 4.5%-5.5%, EBITDA margin 6.5%-7.5%; aspiration to beat past margins but maintaining guidance range.
items.quote: Our PAT margin always has been in the range of say, 4.5% to 5.5%. Our EBITDA margin always has been in the range of. 6.5% to 7.5%, which is anyway better. But we are not stopping at that and we are not complacent, and therefore, we have plans to even better it, but it is not right for me to say that.

items.statement: Order book closed H1 FY25 at Rs. 566 crores, close to last year's level; new contracts added in government and corporate.
items.quote: We have closed the half year at Rs. 566 crores. So, we are very close to our order book position for the last year. And now for the new year with these two tenders also, the ones that we have disclosed, which we have added, we are good to go with our targeted numbers for this financial year ending 2025.

items.statement: Investing in technology, robotics, and AI to strengthen MEP O&M and launch Technical Facilities Management as fifth portfolio.
items.quote: In line with this vision, we have established a new vertical and rather there was this service which was already present, which is MEP O&M. items.quote: Our tender team is doing this exercise on a pan-India basis. So, every day, while I am speaking to you, there must be about half a dozen tenders which are under evaluation, which are under, what do you say, survey, which are under approvals of different authorities.

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 73 days from 77 days; government stipulated wages set baseline for employee costs.
items.quote: The working capital days are about 73 days for the current capital. Earlier it was 77, 69 and now we've come down to 73, which is a very good working capital zone to play and given our portfolio composition of government and corporate.

items.statement: Brand logo owned by promoter, licensed non-exclusively until September 2031; related party loans increased to Rs. 94 crores but are short-term with plan to reduce.
items.quote: These are all short-term and we plan on reducing this.

items.statement: Acquired waste management contract from Thane Municipal Corporation worth Rs. 71 crores till June 2026; MOU with VPRC for patented bio-enzyme technology to treat waste.
items.quote: We acquired the waste management contract from Thane Municipal Corporation. This is a collection and disposal of waste contract worth Rs. 71 crores. Again, the value is not so important, but the contract is applicable till June 2026, and what is important that the contract helps us build our prequalification for future such contracts.

items.statement: Catering revenue share doubled from 2.82% to 5.01%; centralized kitchen in Kalina serving 218+ locations across government and corporate.
items.quote: If you say last year, it constituted about 2.82% of our revenue. This year it is constituting about 5.01%. So, there is a distinct focus and now the corporates, they used to earlier also outsource catering.

items.statement: 100% corporate contract renewal rate in FY24; corporate contracts shifting to 2-3 year terms from 1 year.
items.quote: We have 100% renewal. So, our serviceability with our corporate clients and our relationships and the kind of value-add that we have been doing, we were able to renew 100% of our contracts. We have not lost even a single contract.

items.statement: Employee count: IFMS ~23,000, Staffing & Payroll ~12,139, Security ~5,800, Catering 132; training model replicated across 28 cities via partnerships with schools/colleges.
items.quote: In IFMS, we have around 23,000 employees. In staffing and payroll management, about 12,000 employees, 12,139. In security and manned guarding, 5, 800 odd. And in catering services, because these are only our staff, so it is 132.

items.statement: Loss ratio increased 5.5% in Q2 FY25, driven by 2% from floods and an outlier TP reserve release in Q2 FY24.
items.quote: One is the loss ratio has gone up by 5.5%, which has then increased the combined ratio by about 3.4%.

items.statement: Motor TP loss ratio rose to 66% in Q2 FY25 from 56% in Q2 FY24 due to high reserve release last year.
items.quote: Last year our motor TP loss ratio was about 56%. This year our motor TP loss ratio is 66%.

items.statement: Expense ratio reduced by 2.2% in Q2 FY25 despite de-growth in low-expense employer-employee business.
items.quote: Expense ratio has reduced by 2.2%. This is despite the fact that our employer-employee business has actually degrown, which comes with a lower expense.

items.statement: No formal guidance given, but TP reserve releases expected to continue in H2 FY25 if claims trend holds.
items.quote: we have no reason to believe that this trend will not contin ue for the next two quarters and TP release, but since by principle we don't give

items.quote: By end of, say, 31st March '26, so next financial year, I think the leverage should increase to something like 5x.

items.statement: Motor OD grew 14% vs industry 6% in Q2 FY25; TP grew 2% vs industry 6% with market share rising to 6.9%.
items.quote: In motor OD, industry has grown by 6%, we have grown by 14%. In TP, industry has grown by 6%, we have grown by 2%.

items.statement: Non-employer-employee attachment health business grew >100% in H1 FY25; employer-employee de-grew 3.3%.
items.quote: Our employer-employee business de-grew by 3.3% in this quarter, while the growth in attachment business was 110%.

items.statement: TP mix stable at ~21% in H1 FY25; OD stable at ~23%; attachment health growing rapidly.
items.quote: There is a continuous increase in the mix towards TP business, which is now I would say stable at about 21%.

items.statement: IRDAI issued show cause notice on EOM; no correspondence since Dec 2023; industry EOMs rising.
items.quote: IRDAI has issued this show cause notice to a lot of companies. Since we are listed, we obviously had to publish it.

items.statement: Investment portfolio: 40% sovereign, 40% AAA, 10.8% AT1 bonds (67% SBI, 27% Canara, 6% HDFC); H1 capital loss.
items.quote: Equity is 2.4, sovereign is 40%, AAA and equivalent is 40%, AT1 bonds is constituting about 10.8%.

items.statement: Added 270 new APIs in H1 FY25; two-thirds of policies issued via APIs.
items.quote: We have added 270 APIs, new APIs in 6 months, which I think is a decent number.

items.statement: H1 FY25 ROE 6% (IGAAP); profit up 3x YoY in Q2 despite combined ratio increase.
items.quote: Our H1 ROE is about 6%, not normalized. And despite the increase in combined ratio in Quarter 2, our actual profit has gone up 3x.

items.statement: Management guides annual train take rate around 6% and branding plus performance plus discount expense near 3.5% of GTV
items.quote: I think from a guidance perspective, right, 6% kind of a take rate, on an annual basis is, that's something we will continue to maintain. Plus, there has been a change in mix also.

items.statement: Branding plus performance plus discount expense guided near 3.5% of GTV for the year
items.quote: And what the broad thumb rule guidance we've always talked about will remain in as a percentage will be near and near about what I think is about 3.5% of the GTV as my branding plus performance plus discount, which is where we internally think of that business as an expense.

items.statement: Board approved acquiring 51% stake in Zoop for INR 12.54 crores including non-compete fee with option to buy remaining stake later
items.quote: Our board, at its meeting held today on October 24, has approved entering into a definitive agreement to acquire 51% stake in Zoop Web Services Private Limited, known as Zoop, for a total consideration of INR 12.54 crores, including non -compete fee, subject to the completion of certain conditions precedent through a combination of secondary and primary share purchases.

items.statement: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin at 10% of revenue from operations, adjusted EBITDA INR 21 crores first time ever
items.quote: Despite the unusually strong monsoon rains disrupting travel in some parts of the country, we achieved the growth acceleration in GTV while maintaining a double -digit adjusted EBITDA margin in the quarter, achieving a margin of 10% of our revenue from operations, with the Q2 adjusted EBITDA coming in at INR 21 crores for the first time ever.

items.statement: Contribution margin grew 23.6% YoY to INR 91.1 crores, contribution margin percentage slightly down to 44.11% from 44.94%
items.quote: This was achieved on the back of the operating leverage derived from the expanded contribution margins in our business with INR 91.1 crores of contribution margin in the quarter, up 23.6% versus last year.

items.statement: One notch rating upgrade expected in November 2024

items.statement: Q3 expected to be one of the best quarters due to festive season demand

items.quote: Now, can I get to a 15% margin two quarters out ? The answer is no , but over period of time , is that my aspiration? It absolutely is, and we will drive towards that.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 to Q3 FY26 will see margin uptick as deals mature; timing to reach prior 15.8-16.3% levels uncertain due to volatility
items.quote: Q4 onwards we will start improving margins and Q4 , Q1, Q2, Q3 the next four quarters you will see our margin uptick coming in because by the time all the deals that I and Kamini spoke about will also mature and the margin uptick will happen.

items.statement: Deal pipeline is strong and improving QoQ; currently 50% transformation deals and 50% vendor consolidation deals; some conversions expected in Q3 FY25
items.quote: So, currently, the deals that we have on table is really 50/50 . We have got 50% transformation deals. We have got 50% vendor consolidation deals . But these deals have to convert .

items.statement: FY24 order signings grew only 1% YoY; first half FY25 signings at $300M; need >$550M in H2 to show growth; targeting $250M per quarter in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our dream is to deliver growth on order book even this year, though it is going to be a very tall order because in the first half year, we have delivered only 300 millions of signings and I really need to deliver more than 550 million in the next two quarters even to show growth.

items.statement: Project Optimus internal tech transformation will contribute cost takeout over next 3-4 quarters
items.quote: Project Optimus that Kamini spoke about will contribute over the next three-four quarters to cost takeout.

items.statement: Vendor consolidation deals ($10-30M, 1-3 year tenure) create medium-term margin pressure due to onsite subcontracting; margins improve as work moves offshore
items.quote: These deal sizes range from anywhere between $10 million to $30 million. But there is a small change, Anmol. You know, in today's world, the long-tenure deals are pretty much over.

items.statement: Deal closures delayed due to US election uncertainty; transformation projects expected back on table ~6 months post-election; Europe/Asia pipeline building
items.quote: Typically, after an election cycle happens in the U.S., since almost 86%-87% of our business is in the U.S., it'll take a lag of about six months, but I am sure that all the transformation projects will be back on the table.

items.statement: Digital and Data business grown to $250-280M; will balance consolidation deals with Digital/Data wins to maintain margin profile
items.quote: I don't know if you realize this , but I am sure you do , our Digital and Data business has also grown to become almost $250-$280 million, right?

items.statement: Unpredictability may persist for a couple of quarters due to market volatility; focused on predictability over next 6-9 quarters
items.quote: Even in the future, will there be a couple of quarters where there will be a little bit of unpredictability? It will happen, because the markets are very volatile.

items.statement: Cutting long tail of customers further to redeploy human capital for growth; support staff optimization via automation; sales headcount investment continues
items.quote: We are on an endeavor to cut our tail. We have done a lot, but given the circumstances like you have rightly pointed out, Manik, we will do even more.

items.statement: Business growth guidance for FY25 is 10%; achieved 9.42% up to September 30.
items.quote: The whole financial year we have given a guidance of business growth at 10%. As against that, 9.42% we have grown up to September 30th.

items.statement: Gross NPA guidance for March FY25 is 3.5%; currently at 3.73%.
items.quote: Our Gross NPA has come down from 4.14% to 3.73% as against our next March level guidance of 3.5%.

items.statement: Net NPA guidance for March FY25 is 1.10%; currently at 0.99%.
items.quote: Our Net NPA, next March level guidance w e had given 1.10, but already we are at below 1% i.e. 0.99

items.statement: PCR guidance for March FY25 is 90%; currently at 90.89%.
items.quote: Our PCR we had given a guidance of 90% at the next March level, but we are already touching the 91% at 90.89%.

items.statement: Slippage ratio guidance for March FY25 is 1.3%; currently at 1%.
items.quote: Slippage ratio also we had given a guidance of 1.3% for March , but we alr eady could successfully control slippages and we have touched that 1% slippage

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY25 is 1.10%; currently at 0.97%, expected to be below 1%.
items.quote: Our credit cost slightly increased quarter-on-quarter from 0.9 to 0.97, but still it is much below the guidance that we have given at 1.10.

items.statement: Return on Equity guidance for FY25 is 18%; currently at 20.44%.
items.quote: Our Return on Equity also is maintained well above that guidance of 18%, at 20.44%.

items.statement: Earnings Per Share guidance for FY25 is Rs 16.40; achieved Rs 17.41.
items.quote: And our Earnings Per Share, what we had given the guidance is 16.40, and as against that 17.41 we could achieve.

items.statement: Return on Assets guidance for FY25 is 1%; currently at 1.05%.
items.quote: Return on Assets, the guidance was the 1%, but we are able to maintain at the 1.05.

items.statement: Credit growth outlook for FY25 is around 11% despite shedding low-yielding advances.
items.quote: overall, definitely, what we com mitted that we may reach 11%, definitely, it may happen , even after shredding that 35,000 crores, low yielding advances

items.statement: Corporate credit growth expected at 9-10% for FY25; RAM sector at 12%.
items.quote: Corporate may grow around 9 to 10%. But the RAM sector may continue to grow around 12%.

items.statement: Retail credit growth expected at 13-14% for FY25.
items.quote: Retail growth will be definitely a dominating contributor in RAM credit. That will continue to grow around 14%, 13 to 14%.

items.statement: MSME credit growth expected at 9-10% for FY25.
items.quote: In MSME also we are expecting that the growth may be touching near to 9 to 10% this year.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio growth expected at 16-17% for FY25.
items.quote: With all these steps already existing, we are growing at 15 to 16%. And we look at that, the growth will be around 16 to 17% this year.

items.statement: NIM declined 2 bps to 2.88% in Q2 FY25; cost of deposits stable at 5.7%; yield on advances improved to 8.77%.
items.quote: Our NIM slightly has come down compared to the peer banks. It come down from 2.9 to 2.88. Though there is a lot of pressure on the cost of deposits, but we could manage this because of efficient management of

items.statement: EBITDA margin to improve by 100-125 bps annually for next 3 years, reaching late teens in 3 years
items.quote: As we have been guiding in earlier calls also that we will improve our margin every year by 150 basis points or so. So, over the last year, we will be doing much better than that. And thereafter, also for the next 3 years, we will continue to improve our margin by 100 to 125 basis and that's how we will reach to the late teens margin in 3 years' time.

items.statement: P&A volume growth of 15%+ expected in next 2 quarters and 1-2 years further
items.quote: the premiumization is happening, and we will continue to grow our P&A category volume by 15%-plus in next 2 quarters also and in 1 to 2 years further

items.statement: Gross margin improved 258 bps QoQ to 43.6% due to premiumization and stable raw material costs
items.quote: Gross margin improved 258 basis points on a quarter-on-quarter basis due to the ongoing premiumization, stable raw material and packaging material scenario.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 150 bps YoY due to economies of scale
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded on Y-o-Y basis by 150 basis points due to economies of scale.

items.statement: Regular category to see mid-single-digit growth from Q3 onwards after state-specific disruptions
items.quote: But now onwards, you will see in Regular category also, we will see that continued demand, and we will have a mid-single-digit kind of growth from here onwards.

items.statement: ENA and grain prices expected to soften from November with new season and buffer stocks; glass prices stable after 4-5% correction
items.quote: November onwards, we should see some softening of the prices of grain, maize, rice, et cetera. At the same time, the government has built up a lot of buffer stocks. Even the buffer stock, they don’t have space to keep, store and all that. And the new rice miller processing is starting. So, we can’t say, but if there is any support to the ethanol producer from some alloca tion on the SCI side , tha

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh policy change expected to improve cash flows and premium brand traction; shifting from Royalty to own brands from Q4
items.quote: right now, in Andhra Pradesh, we have been operating on Royalty. And we are assessing the situation. So, starting from Q4 we might get away from Royalty and get into our own brands

items.statement: Magic Moments Vodka growing strong double-digit with 60% market share; White Spirit category growing fast at 4% of market vs 28% globally
items.quote: And Magic we see as Abhishek has said in his opening remarks that still nascent, it's still below 4% as the volume of the total industry. And the consuming class is the youngsters and the women. And we are the leader with 60% market share across all price categories. So, I think we see a great growth, and we continue to see strong double-digit growth in years to come.

items.statement: New super premium brand launch expected this fiscal year or early next fiscal year
items.quote: See, there is one brand which is in store, we are working on it, which is in the super premium segment. So, hopefully, maybe this fiscal year, you should see it or maybe beginning of next fiscal year, for sure.

items.statement: Expects Dahej utilization of 95-100% in H2 FY25 and moderate spot LNG prices to support consumption growth
items.quote: We are expecting that it should be in the range of 95% to 100% capacity utilization at Dahej . So, this should continue. We don't foresee any challenge.

items.statement: Dahej 5 MMTPA regas expansion (Rs 570 cr) on track for March 2025 completion; Dahej third jetty awarded, completion by 2027; Kochi pipeline connectivity expected by March-April 2025
items.quote: Another project which is going on in Dahej is our Regasification project, this expansion of our capacity by 5 MMTPA and this is likely to be completed by March 2025 as per the scheduled completion time.

items.statement: Petchem project: PMC and licensor contracts awarded; tendering underway; major capex expected FY26; debt-equity 70:30, lenders to be lined up in 2-3 months
items.quote: This year only this processing will continue because awarding the contract also sometimes takes more time. So, that is there and progress I have told you. And as you know we are also lining up our lenders for this project.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 inventory gain Rs 70 cr vs Rs 261 cr previous quarter; trading margin Rs 39 cr this quarter
items.quote: And as far as the trading is concerned, trading margin has (Inaudible)…and there has been inventory gain of around Rs. 70 crores this quarter as again Rs. 261 crores in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Dahej regas tariff escalates 5% annually per contract till 2036; review every 3 years for inflation only upward; formula confidential but lowest among terminals
items.quote: This is as per contract. See, it's not there that they have a choice because it has been agreed to and it's not in Dahej only. If you go any other terminal also, you go to Dhamra, you go other terminals, they are also charging 5% every year.

items.statement: Optimistic on India LNG demand growth driven by price-sensitive market, moderate prices, CGD expansion, transport sector potential 10-12 MMTPA, domestic gas constraints
items.quote: So, I think in India there is huge potential for LNG consumption. And even existing sectors and more new sectors will come up, CGD entities will come up. So, I hope that our LNG consumption will further increase because domestic gas availability is a hindrance.

items.statement: 2021 take-or-pay receivables ~Rs 378 cr (down from Rs 420 cr); ~75% provided; settlement by Dec 2024 backed by bank guarantees; 2022 defaulters have till Dec 2025
items.quote: It was around Rs. 420 crores, whatever it may be, but now it has come down slightly because some of the capacities have been brought. So, it has come down to almost Rs. 378 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 Dahej throughput 225 TBTU, Kochi 22% utilization; combined 239 TBTU; H1 FY25 PBT Rs 2,660 cr (+23% YoY), PAT Rs 1,989 cr (+24% YoY); interim dividend Rs 7/share
items.quote: Dahej throughput has been 225 TBTU as against 210 TBTU in the corresponding quarter and 248 TBTU in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Next year (FY26) Dahej capacity 22.5 MMTPA, Kochi 5 MMTPA; expects to utilize maximum expanded capacity at Dahej via spot/short-term volumes
items.quote: Next year estimate is 22.5 MMTPA from Dahej and 5 MMTPA from Kochi. We have the capacity, we can utilize it, but at least Dahej , we are hopeful that we will be able to utilize maximum capacity.

items.statement: Reaffirmed full-year volume growth guidance of 15% to 20% year-on-year despite 4% raw material price decline impacting revenue
items.quote: No. I think we will stick to our guidance of 15% to 20% growth. And if you see, realization from raw material basically has gone down by 4% in this quarter. That also has resulted in lower revenue. But overall, we expect 15% volume growth for the full year.

items.statement: Confident of achieving 15% to 20% year-on-year growth for the near foreseeable future
items.quote: Yes, we are confident of 15% to 20% year-on-year growth also.

items.statement: Board approved Rs. 57.5 Crores investment for 3,000 MT aluminum forging capacity at Jamshedpur for EV segment
items.quote: The Board of Directors has also approved an investment of Rs. 57.5 Crores to establish an aluminum forging capability around 3,000 metric tonnes per annum at Jamshedpur, primarily to serve the EV segment.

items.statement: Full-year CAPEX guidance increased to Rs. 550 Crores from initial Rs. 500 Crores; subsidiary investment guidance Rs. 100 Crores for JV with Titagarh
items.quote: And what we have given the guidance of about Rs. 500 Crores of CAPEX initially, it may increase by another Rs. 50 Crores during the year. And on the subsidiary side, it remains the same. On the investment side also we only need to invest on the JV with Ramkrishna Titagarh, and for that also we have given a guidance of Rs. 100 Crores for the full year.

items.statement: Secured orders worth Rs. 1,522 Crores in Q2 FY25 to be executed over 4 years; Rs. 1,475 Crores from North America (Rs. 1,312 Crores auto, Rs. 163 Crores non-auto) and Rs. 47 Crores from India
items.quote: I would like to convey that we have secured orders during the quarter worth Rs. 1,522 Crores to be executed over a period of 4 ( four) years. Against the Rs. 1,522 Crores orders, we have Ramkrishna Forgings Limited 24 October, 2024 received from North America orders worth Rs. 1,475 Crores, in which we have secured Rs. 1,312 Crores from the auto segment and from the non -auto segment we have fetche

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin moderated 20 bps YoY to 22.09% in Q2 FY25; management expects improvement in near future
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA margin for Q2 FY '25 stood at 22.09% and the same has moderated by 20 basis points year -on-year. We believe that we will be able to improve upon the above margin in the near future.

items.statement: Trailer axle assembly launched in Q2 with Rs. 20+ Crores sales; targeting 25% market share in Rs. 2,000+ Crores market growing 17-20% annually
items.quote: I mean, trailer axle assembly, we have just launched in this quarter, and we have achieved a sales of almost Rs. 20 plus Crores. This is a Rs. 2,000 plus Crores market and growing at a very rapid pace of 17% to 20% every year. And it's that we are expecting to at least by this year-end or first quarter of next year to get to almost 25% market share in this segment.

items.statement: North America market flattish but RKFL growing exceptionally well due to new customer penetration; Mexico facility to further consolidate growth from next quarter
items.quote: Raghu, right now the market is flattish. We are growing and we are doing exceptionally well because of our marketing has been able to penetrate new segments and new customers in North America. And that's the reason we are growing. And with setting up of a facility in Mexico, we expect this to further consolidate and grow.

items.statement: Internal vision for 15-20% of revenue to come from EV/hybrid vehicles by FY27
items.quote: But I think Raghu, just to update on what Lalit said, our internal vision in next 2 (two) years by FY 27, is that our 15% to 20% revenue should be coming from EV or hybrid vehicles. That is the vision we are working with and I think we are on track to achieve our vision.

items.statement: Aluminum forging capacity of 3,000 MT fully backed by firm 5-year order; CAPEX ~Rs. 60 Crores; potential 20x capacity opportunity with same customer
items.quote: It is already backed by an order. The entire capacity of 3,000 tonnes is completely backed by a firm order for 5 (five) years.

items.statement: Ramkrishna Titagarh JV on track; wheel production and delivery to railways to start in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Last quarter of FY '26 we will start producing wheels and delivering to railways.

items.statement: Red Sea issues increased transit time and inventory in transit/warehouses; exports continuing full-fledged
items.quote: Further, inventory has also gone up due to the build-up of stock in transit and at warehouses due to the Red Sea issues.

items.statement: Aluminum forging line at optimum utilization can generate ~Rs. 250 Crores top line with 4x+ asset turn; payback under 2 years at full capacity
items.quote: And as optimum capacity utilization, it can give me around Rs. 250 Crores of top line. You can understand that it will be around 4 plus kind of asset turn. And in terms of percentage margin, certainly EBITDA will be lower, but in terms of realization it is much higher in terms of EBITDA per tonne. And that's why, if you look at, it will be a payback of less than 2 (two) years, if you go on the ful

items.statement: Consolidated revenue guidance for FY25 adjusted to Rs. 4,500-4,600 Crores from earlier Rs. 5,000 Crores due to raw material price impact and Globe divestment
items.quote: But certainly, now it will be not a Rs. 5 Billion, it can be somewhere between Rs. 4,500 Crores to Rs. 4,600 Crores kind of thing, right now, on the consol basis for FY '25, considering that adjustment.

items.statement: North America Class 8 truck demand expected strong in CY26 due to pre-buy ahead of 2027 emission norms; infrastructure demand to sustain pace
items.quote: But obviously, when the norm change comes in '27, '26 is going to be a very strong year and North America has already been spelling so. But because of many of the infrastructure demands and the way America is trying to rebuild itself, the demand is going to be very strong for the next 2 (two) years.

items.statement: Divested 100% stake in Globe All India Services to Yatra Online for Rs. 128 Crores; funds deployed as growth capital
items.quote: In Q2, we divested 100% stake in our travel company, Globe All India Services Limite d to Yatra Online for a cash consideration of Rs. 128 Crores. These funds, unlocked from non -core assets, are being invested as growth capital.

items.statement: Grey cement volume growth revised to 6-7% for FY25 from earlier 10% target
items.quote: Even though we are expecting a good demand, we would see that we should be closing anything around with the growth of about 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Capex target maintained at Rs 1,800-1,900 crore for FY25; Rs 750 crore spent in H1
items.quote: We have spent 750 crores till now out of the target of 1,800-1,900 crores.

items.statement: 6 mtpa expansion commissioning expected by end of Q3 or beginning of Q4 FY26
items.quote: By December '25/last quarter, end of third quarter, beginning of fourth quarter should be the commissioning.

items.statement: Unit production cost expected to reduce by Rs 50 per ton in each of Q3 and Q4 FY25
items.quote: With the fuel prices softening and all, we should see an impact of about Rs. 50 coming up in each of the remaining two quarters.

items.statement: Cost savings exit rate of Rs 60-75 per ton targeted by March 2025; cumulative Rs 150-200 per ton over FY25-26
items.quote: I think if we look at an exit by FY25, we should definitely have an exit of between Rs. 60 to 75. So, Rs. 60 which is a saving which would have accrued we should be seeing that saving in FY26 and other savings will come in FY26 which will pile up to about Rs. 150 to 200.

items.statement: Demand dip seen in north and south regions during Q2; central India relatively better
items.quote: See the demand slip was not so much felt in the central India. There was a dip in demand definitely in the north and the southern part.

items.statement: October volumes expected to show year-on-year growth; government spending pickup expected from November
items.quote: No actually I think we should be showing a growth year-on-year also in October.

items.statement: White cement putty volumes expected to grow 5-6% in FY25 vs industry growth of 8-9%
items.quote: And we are trying to see that we grow at least 5%, though our internal target is definitely much higher. But as of what it looks anything between 5% to 6% should be our growth numbers.

items.statement: Grey cement realizations flat QoQ despite price pressure due to mix improvement and cutting low-retention volumes
items.quote: All these factors have resulted that though the prices were under pressure but on an average with a mix, we are not seeing any fall in the realization per ton.

items.statement: October grey cement prices marginally up vs Q2 average; further increases possible post-Diwali
items.quote: Q2 average marginally up. But we have to really see this is, whatever some prices had increased but not across but in the north and all, so marginally up as compared to average of Q2.

items.statement: One-time impact of Rs 45-50 crore in Q2 from extended shutdowns and clinker purchases
items.quote: These two could be the one-time expenditure which if we look at in terms of the value, could be anything around 45 to 50 crores, could be a onetime impact which is there in this quarter.

items.statement: Paints business revenue Rs 53 crore in Q2, Rs 117 crore in H1; EBITDA loss Rs 15 crore in Q2, Rs 25 crore in H1
items.quote: Our turnover in this quarter was 53 crores and 6 months is 117 crores and the EBITDA loss for the 6 months is 25 crores.

items.statement: Paints business targeting Rs 250-300 crore revenue in FY25, Rs 400-450 crore in FY26, Rs 600 crore by FY27 with breakeven
items.quote: As we had a guideline that we should be closing the year somewhere between 250 to 300 crores as a top line. We are confident that we would be in that region on the top line.

items.statement: Won two coal blocks (Shahdol and Mahan) in Madhya Pradesh; targeting commissioning 12-15 months ahead of FY29 deadline and within 30 months for larger block
items.quote: We feel that we are planning that maybe if exact timelines will know once we go to the site. But we plan maybe in 30 months, we are able to commission this block.

items.statement: Coal blocks expected to reduce fuel cost to Rs 1-1.10 per 100 NCV vs current linkage cost of Rs 1.50-1.60
items.value: Rs. 1 max, outer limit Rs. 1.10 paisa
items.quote: Today we are getting linkage fuel at about Rs. 1.50 paisa to Rs. 1.60 paisa per 100 NCV. This would come at a much lower around Rs. 1 max, outer limit Rs. 1.10 paisa.

items.statement: Thermal substitution rate dropped to 13% in Q2 due to maintenance period and inclusion of 4 new plants in SBTi reporting scope
items.quote: So, see you would see that Q2 being a maintenance period for all the kilns, so that has resulted in a sharp decline.

items.statement: NIM guidance maintained at 3.4% to 3.6% for the year; current half-year NIM at 3.38%.
items.quote: The NIM, we have clocked at 3.38% for the half year. There has been a dip in Q2. But overall, we still have done better and we are still within the guidance for 3.4% to 3.6%, and we are about 3.38%.

items.statement: Gross advances growth guidance revised to 15-18% for FY25 from earlier 18-19%.
items.quote: So I think we will grow probably about, in the next 2 quarters, at about 15%, and then grow to the 18% because this is the transitionary phase where we were growing with some bulk advances in the past, but the bulk has come down drastically.

items.statement: ROA guidance maintained at 1.2% to 1.25% for upcoming quarters; current Q2 ROA at 1.13%.
items.quote: Our guidance has been 1.2%. I think that we will get back to the 1.2% to 1.25% in the following quarters, and we have reasons to support this.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected to moderate to around 55% in H2 FY25 from 58% in Q2.
items.quote: For H2, we would come back to about 55 odd.

items.statement: Gross slippages guidance for full year FY25 at 50 bps (0.5% annualized).
items.quote: 0.5% is the annualized for the entire year.

items.statement: NII for H1 FY25 was INR 1,736.92 crores, up 6.1% YoY; NIM at 3.38% for half year.
items.quote: The NII for H1 FY '25 was INR1,736.92 crores. It was up 6.1% on a year-on-year in comparison. The NIM, we have clocked at 3.38% for the half year.

items.statement: Cost of funds stable at 5.58% for Q2 and H1 FY25 vs 5.29% in H1 FY24.
items.quote: As far as the cost of funds is concerned, despite the market volatility, we have remained stable at 5.58%, and it was the same number almost for the Q1. And cost of funds for the entire half year was about 5.58%.

items.statement: Credit cost for Q2 FY25 at 0.09%, lowest so far; H1 FY25 credit cost at 0.2%.
items.quote: Our credit cost for the Q2 was at 0.09%, which is actually the lowest that we have had so far compared to 0.11% in the previous quarter and as against 0.17% in the quarter 2 of last year.

items.statement: Retail net accretion at INR 1,300+ crores in Q2; expect run rate to increase significantly in next two quarters with new DSA and corporate structures in place.
items.quote: And this quarter also, we have clocked more than INR1,300 crores. Now with our DSA structure in place, corporate DSA structure in place, we would be in a better way where we will be able to increase this run rate. And in the following two quarters, we believe that we will be much higher than the current run rate.

items.statement: Loan book 90% secured (collateralized); unsecured retail exposure minimal (INR 200-250 crores via co-lending).
items.quote: The unsecured and secured mix has always been 90% fully collateralized book for us, and that continues. There is no change to that. The balance 10% also has been more to large corporate PSU, etc. So technically, we do not have any unsecured retail exposure per se, other than some co-lending and a couple of other arrangements that we have. But there, the total book has not even crossed about INR200

items.statement: Approximately 50% of loan book is EBLR-linked; retail liabilities form 92% of deposit base enabling quick ALM repricing.
items.quote: About 50% of our book is EBLR linked. There could be some on the retail side also. But overall, I'm saying I'm calling out to say that about 50% would be EBLR plus.

items.statement: Gross NPA improved to 3.21% from 3.54% QoQ; Net NPA improved to 1.46% from 1.66% QoQ.
items.quote: On the standard assets, this is one area where we'll be very proud this quarter because the gross NPA significantly improved from 3.54% to 3.21%.

items.statement: Gross slippages dropped sharply to 0.33% in Q2 from 0.59% in Q1 and 0.52% in Q2 FY24.
items.quote: This has been achieved because the gross slippages has come down drastically, and we are at 0.33% in Q2 as against 0.59% in Q1 and as against 0.52% in Q2 of last year.

items.statement: Restructured book (excl. related accounts) down to INR 1,051.86 crores from INR 1,160.94 crores in Q1 and INR 1,338.78 crores in March '24.
items.quote: Without related accounts, the restructured book has come down to INR1,051.86 crores compared to INR1,160.94 crores as of 30th June and as against INR1,338.78 crores as of 31st March, '24.

items.statement: Combined Gross NPA + Restructured book as % of gross advances improved to 4.89% from 5.39% in Q1 and 6.78% a year ago.
items.quote: And I'm actually happy to report that as of September '24, our percentage has come down to 4.89% as against 5.39% in the previous quarter and as against 6.78% in the previous year the same quarter.

items.statement: Technology infrastructure enhancements (storage, processing, functional features) completed; national back-office centralization (clearing done, treasury ops in couple of weeks).
items.quote: All the enhancements are in place, and we have done some major enhancements both in terms of our storage, processing, and also a lot of other functional features in our overall tech stack.

items.statement: LCR at 143.93% under revised RBI draft guidelines (effective April 2025) as of Sept 30, well above 100% statutory requirement.
items.quote: So even after the revised guidelines as of September 30th, we stand at 143.93% on the LCR, which is very comfortable and as against the statutory target of 100%.

items.statement: Strong demand traction seen from August end, positivity expected to continue for next two quarters
items.quote: We have seen a strong traction coming from August end itself. And we feel that, okay, this positivity is going to continue for the next 2 quarters at least.

items.statement: Standalone double-digit growth expected in Q3 and Q4 FY25 after production issues resolved
items.quote: It should be in the case of quarter 3 and quarter 4.

items.statement: Kraus EBITDA margin at par with KKCL in Q2 FY25
items.quote: The top line has been INR 55 odd crores, and the brand has been able to achieve EBITDA margins, which is equivalent at KKCL.

items.statement: Target consolidated EBITDA margin of 18-20% maintained across brands including Junior Killer
items.quote: And if we see on margin -- see, we will maintain as Kewal Kiran, we will maintain 18% to 20% EBITDA margin. And averaging is around 18% to 20%, we will maintain that.

items.statement: Land purchase of INR 57 crores for head office and registered office, 100 meters from current office
items.quote: The property, which we are looking at buying out, it is required for the head office and the registered office. Currently, the head office is falling short of the manpower requirement.

items.statement: Pre-booked orders in hand but unable to produce equivalently due to manufacturing constraints

items.statement: Integriti strategy revised to compete with value brands and private labels, results expected from Q1 FY26
items.quote: Integriti, we have looked at, okay, competing against the value price brands and as well as private label, okay. The extraction or maybe the numbers for the same should fall from quarter 1 of the next year.

items.quote: Particularly for Lawman, we are looking at retail expansions, which you'll see from quarter 3 and quarter 4.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth guided at 10%-11% and EBITDA margin in the range of 12%
items.quote: So, as per earlier guidance given , we will be having a growth of about 10% and the EBITDA margin will be in the range of 12%.

items.statement: Q2 gross margin expanded 320 bps to 34.1% due to premium mix and organic growth; EBITDA margin flat at 12% due to freight

items.statement: Paddy prices for new crop down 10%-17% vs last year; expected to improve margins in FY26
items.quote: Roughly it depends on variety to variety but in the range of 10% to 17% or same that is the range.

items.statement: No demand challenges; Basmati category growing in USA, Middle East (34% growth), India; expect continued category growth
items.quote: No, we are not facing challenge, actually whichever part of the world we are present the category is growing be it USA, Middle East. Middle East we have grown 34%. In USA we are growing, in India we are growing.

items.statement: Organic business expected to exceed INR 1,000 cr revenue this year with 10%-12% growth; sourcing diversified to Africa, Brazil
items.quote: This year we are expecting to do more than 1 ,000 crores in organic. So, that's building up. We are expecting both in terms of growth and margin expansion.

items.statement: Insurance claim won in all courts; execution pending, next hearing 5th November; hopeful of resolution soon
items.quote: We have won in Lower Court, we have won in High Court, we have won in Supreme Court. But executing court takes time, they will take date and all this. So , we all know that the system. But I think everything is clear. It's a matter of some days only.

items.statement: Ready-to-eat/cook breakeven at INR 350-400 cr revenue in 2-3 years; Q2 degrowth due to Daawat Sehat discontinuation (INR 18.5 cr)
items.quote: We will be breaking even at a revenue of around 350 to 400 crores. So, that will be the breakeven point and this we wish to achieve. We have plans to achieve at 2 to 3 years' time frame.

items.statement: Inventory days increased to 194 from 166 to meet higher demand; expected to normalize to prior March levels by March
items.quote: Yes, our inventory days have increased from 166 to 194 days. So, that is an increase of 28 days. This inventory day is actually in order to c ater the increase in the demand that we are seeing in the different parts.

items.statement: Middle East premium share in Dubai up to 9.8% from 6.2% per Nielsen; Saudi distributor appointed, good news expected in a month
items.quote: In Dubai, our share in premium segment as per Nielsen has gone to 9.8% from 6.2 %. we are improving our market share in Kuwait , in Qatar, in Muscat and Iraq also. Now the strategy is in place. The distributor has been appointed and we are hopeful that we will do good in Saudi Arabia.

items.statement: Non-Basmati export relaxation evaluated for branded sustainable opportunities only
items.quote: Definitely, Resham, we will evaluate the opportunity and normally we are not into non-Basmati business and business which is not sustainable in nature but in a branded segment where sustainability comes, we will definitely evaluate.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance raised to 19.5%-20.5% in constant currency including ~5% from Ascensos; organic guidance 14.5%-15.5%
items.quote: For FY25, we now expect our revenue to grow in the range of 19.5% to 20.5% in constant currency terms. This includes about 5% contribution from Ascensos over the 7 months in FY25.

items.statement: FY25 normalized EBIT margin guidance 11%-11.5% excluding one-time acquisition charges
items.quote: For operating margins, we expect our normalized FY25 EBIT margin, excluding one-time charges related to the acquisitions, to be in the 11% to 11.5% band.

items.statement: Q2 normalized EBIT margin 11.1% excluding Ascensos one-time charges, stable QoQ and YoY
items.quote: EBIT margin for the quarter was 11.1%, excluding one-time charges related to the Ascensos' acquisition. This is broadly stable, both on a QoQ and a YoY basis.

items.statement: Healthcare payer segment seeing decision delays due to open enrollment and US elections, but pipeline healthy; expect bounce back next quarter

items.statement: UK/Europe organic revenue down ~4% QoQ due to cost pressures driving offshoring; expect improvement over next two quarters
items.quote: Europe grew 3.6% QoQ, our organic revenues excluding Ascensos' were down about 4% QoQ. However, companies in the UK are facing significant cost pressure that has led to them increasingly exploring offshore or nearshore delivery options even in some of the previously awarded deals.

items.statement: Added new seat capacities in Chennai, Hyderabad, Philippines and Mexico in Q2
items.quote: We continue to invest in expanding our execution infrastructure in Q2. We have added new seat capacities in Chennai, Hyderabad, Philippines and Mexico.

items.statement: Guidance does not build in any changes in macro environment; potential upside if macro improves
items.quote: Our guidance does not build any changes in the macro environment. And if there is something out there, that's potentially an upside.

items.statement: Investing in domain-centric LLM for mortgage and AI-infused digital collections platform; saw >10% uplift in collection efficiency
items.quote: We have already seen more than a 10% uplift in our collection efficiency with the revamped platform.

items.statement: Paid Rs. 3 billion for Ascensos acquisition; acquired 100% stake at GBP 42M including GBP 9.5M earn-out over two years
items.quote: We have paid Rs. 3 billion to our Ascensos' acquisition during this quarter. As we have reported earlier, we have acquired 100% stake in a company at a purchase consideration of GBP 42 million, which includes 9.5 million GBP as an earn-out linked to achieving predefined milestone in the next two years.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month attrition reduced to 31% from 32% in Q1 and 39.8% a year ago; expect gradual further decline
items.quote: Our trailing 12-month attrition rate for the quarter was 31%, a reduction from 32% in Q1FY25 and 39.8% in Q2 of last year. We anticipate this downward trend to continue in the coming quarters, though at a more gradual pace.

items.statement: Medium-term aspiration to hit $1B run rate by Q4 FY26 unchanged; will revisit as visibility improves
items.quote: This was a medium-term aspiration that we had put out there, which is that we would look to hit a billion-dollar run rate business by Q4 of FY26.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR8,200 crores with freight car business accounting for 72%
items.quote: Looking forward, our order book is at INR8,200 crores with freight car business accounting for 72% of the same.

items.quote: The H2, we expect that we will be doing better than H1.

items.quote: And this year and middle of next year, we expect around 30,000 more wagons to come in, whatever we know about -- I mean, the tenders have come up and something is in the pipeline.

items.quote: So these are -- I mean, to answer you, I don't -- we don't need any CapEx to do that. So these capacities, you can see that it's not a problem and not a challenge for your company.

items.quote: So private is always better than what we have in terms of railways. And after private, we have export. Export is even better than what we supply to private.

items.quote: Sir, of course, our intention is common with you, but you know that the government machineries and statutory obligations are there where it is very difficult for you and me to commit.

items.quote: So yes, Mohit, the H1, they made a total revenue from operation was INR426 crores and their PBT was INR63 crores, INR62.73 crores to be exact.

items.quote: So we believe that the automobile companies are where looking for an efficient logistics solution where they can reduce the carbon footprint in their company by doing so many trucks enter at the same time, they wanted an efficient logistic where they can reduce their logistic cost.

items.quote: We also are looking at revamping our foundry capacity by putting in a new foundry, which perhaps will be mostly export -oriented and will be going to the countries outside India and developed countries like U.S. and Australia, et cetera.

items.quote: And along with -- as I mentioned about top line, but I must add that bottom line will be very strong of that business too.

items.quote: Nothing official about it. There was an advertisement of Pepsi, I believe.

items.quote: For us, I think housing finance is growing at 20% and that should be quite stable.

items.quote: Now, 10 % has to move to 12 %, 12% has to move to 14 %, 14% has to move to 16%.

items.quote: we can expect about 24%-25%, we can expect operating profit to increase this year also.

items.quote: do expect that maybe FY27 onwards for the next 7 or 8 years , that is FY27 onward, we do expect that by the time whatever had to come and go would have come and gone and then it becomes a reasonably stable machine

items.statement: FY27-FY30 expected to show strong uptrend in operating profit with credit costs stabilizing at 1.85%
items.quote: we do expect that our FY27, FY28, FY29, FY30 should be reasonably strong uptrend.

items.quote: the provision which is about 225 basis point guided for this year that would come off to a normalized level into the next year, right.

items.quote: in Q2 that has inched up to about 7% and of average microfinance book is about Rs. 12,000 odd crores, right , so if you apply these percentages, you will realize that the credit cost, which has come through is about Rs. 400 crores. items.statement: Restructured book at 0.23% (~Rs.500 cr) with 19% provision coverage
items.quote: the restructured book, as I said, that book is now only 0.23% in value terms that it is about Rs. 500 crores of restructured book which we have and the predominant part of it is the mortgage book which is sitting here. On this, we are carrying a provision of about 19%.

items.statement: Launched 20+ products and expanded branch network in last 5 years; costs to amortize over time

items.quote: networth accretion would be about Rs. 618 crores at September end and this benefit would flow into Q3. And in terms of capital adequacy benefit, this would give us about 24 bps of relief, right, which will come in Q3.

items.statement: Full-year capacity growth guidance of early double digits maintained

items.quote: The CASK ex fuel ex forex came in at 2.90 rupees, which is 23 percent higher on year-over-year basis.

items.statement: Fundraising process started: first tranche via rights issue (Board approved), second tranche with EY underway; no headwinds

items.quote: The operational revenue from Dehradun has increased to about INR 6.2 crores for Q2 F Y '25, a 23% growth over last quarter. Dehradun community is on track for operations break even much ahead of plan.

items.quote: PAR 1 to 30 book, 2.8%, less than 3%.

items.quote: the total price growth for the first half of the year is at about 3% YTD, which is in line with our guidance for 6% to 7% price growth for the full year

items.quote: The Specialty Chemical industry continues to face challenges across major end user sectors. items.quote: So, the product, if I give you the idea, then a lot of new products like Flonicamid, Ethiprole, Cyfluthrin, Beta Cyfluthrin, Dinotefuran, Spiromesifen. So, a lot of new products we have introduced.

items.quote: First of all, we are very confident that the antidumping duty will come. If it doesn't come, then also we have different plans so that we can come out of this problem as fast as possible.

items.quote: As a Meghmani, we are not expanding, we are not doing expansion in pigment green and blue as a strategy. So, we will try to do some sell in other markets where we will have a better realization.

items.quote: So, there was an MTM during this quarter around INR15 crores and on YTD basis also it was INR14 crores, that reflects in the finance cost, but if you see the overall foreign currency gain or loss, so there is a roughly INR14 crores gain in that other income.

items.statement: Company aspires to achieve 15% to 20% revenue growth going forward

items.quote: So, I think on a steady state basis, Ankit, you can expect a GM of about 61% to 62%, it will range in that bracket.

items.statement: M&A pipeline robust; competitive intensity moderating; targeting synergistic deals to expand offerings; no commitment on H2 timing
